Inside the per-ancestor loop (line 70), each of the entry's up to about 2048 ancestors is copied with to_owned() and inserted into BTreeMap<PathBuf, Kind>. The key always exists already. Each insert allocates O(j) bytes and makes about c full-prefix comparisons of O(j) bytes, for about c x D^2 byte steps per entry.

evidence.description: entries: BTreeMap<PathBuf, Kind> is keyed by the full relative path. PathBuf ordering is component-wise with a byte-wise shared-prefix fast path, so each search comparison scans up to the shared prefix (up to about 4 KB at this depth).

for a in entry.path.ancestors().skip(1) runs for every reported entry with no early exit. BTreeMap::insert on an existing key keeps the old key, drops the new PathBuf and only replaces Kind::Dir with Kind::Dir, so the allocation and the search are pure overhead.

self.ready.push_back(held) reports each unreported parent before the child (and line 276 reports every non-excluded entry, directories included, as it is visited), which makes the ancestor loop in load redundant.
Every visited directory is read with read_dir(&entry.path), that is, opened by its full relative path. This is the strongest source-visible bound on depth: PATH_MAX, not an explicit limit.

openat2_retry(self.fd(), rel.as_os_str(), ...) passes the whole relative path, so the kernel rejects a directory path of 4096 bytes or more with ENAMETOOLONG and the build fails cleanly. This caps depth but not the entry count.

Every pending entry carries its full PathBuf (rel.join(&name)), and load keeps another copy per kept entry (sources.rs:85). That is about 8 KB per entry at depth about 2000: linear memory that bounds a practical N and is decisive for how far the CPU effect can go.

Variant on the resolution path: follow() runs at.join(&name) and entries.get(&next) for each component (line 195), restarting from the root for each of up to MAX_HOPS = 40 symlinks. It needs a Dockerfile source, such as a wildcard, that resolves through many deep context symlinks.

dockerfile_source accepts an absolute or existing host path as the Dockerfile, outside the context. This is the deployment in which the context owner is a principal distinct from the Dockerfile author and gains a CPU spend that RUN would not give them anyway.

A named store holds only the per-build flock on builds/<id>.lock during prepare, so a slow load blocks no other build. The effect stays within the building process's own CPU time and the operator's job time.
Dockerfile and build context: the operator decides whether to build them, but ranikust's own code that reads them (parser, COPY, .dockerignore) treats them as hostile.

T15 names huge or very many files and deep trees as a threat to A7 and leaves only fork bombs to the outer cgroup. Its stated mitigation (stream, fail cleanly on exhaustion) does not cover CPU amplification in ranikust's own code.
Denial of service from untrusted input with default settings (T15, T16) is rated Medium. Section 6 accepts no risk for context size or depth.

blockers: This run allows no target-controlled execution: there is no OS-enforced sandbox, and the host rules forbid namespaces. The per-leaf cost of load at depth about 2000 is therefore unmeasured: an estimated 1 to 50 ms, depending on whether std's byte-wise prefix loop vectorizes and on musl malloc and memcpy speed. It is decisive. Near the low end, the linear memory of about 8 KB per entry exhausts first and the quadratic term is a constant-factor slowdown (hardening). Near the high end, about 10^5 leaves (under 1 GB) cost an hour of CPU (a T15 denial of service).

The repository does not show whether a supported deployment builds an untrusted context with an operator-supplied Dockerfile from a host path whose steps do not execute context-controlled code. Only then does the context owner gain a capability beyond RUN. The repository also does not show which job timeout and CPU or memory cgroup limits cap the spend.

validation_plan.local: Run in the disposable VM lane (T2, just test-vm) with dummy data. The test needs no privilege, so any T0 lane also fits; do not run it on the shared host. Build first with cargo test -p rnk-builder --release --test context_depth --no-run, then run the test under ulimit -v 4194304, ulimit -n 4096 (needs a hard limit of at least 4096) and timeout 1800. Add an #[ignore] test crates/rnk-builder/tests/context_depth.rs. In a tempfile::TempDir it builds a chain of D directories named 'a', with D in {128, 256, 512, 1024, 2000}, creating each level with rustix mkdirat and openat relative to the previous directory fd (closing the previous fd) so that no full path nears PATH_MAX. In the deepest directory it creates N empty files f00000..f{N-1}, with N in {0, 200, 2000}. For each (D, N) it opens the context with rnk_context::open(&ContextSpec::Dir(dir)) and times (i) ctx.walk(None).count() and (ii) rnk_builder::ContextFiles::load(&ctx, None) separately, three runs each, reporting the median. Run: cargo test -p rnk-builder --release --test context_depth -- --ignored --nocapture. Record the per-leaf cost of load, ((ii at N) minus (ii at N=0)) / N, the walk's per-leaf cost, ((i at N) minus (i at N=0)) / N, and the chain-only cost (ii at N=0). The claim holds if the per-leaf cost of load roughly quadruples per doubling of D (the walk's own per-leaf cost grows at most linearly in D, so (ii)/(i) grows by between about 2x and 4x per doubling, not necessarily 4x) and the per-leaf cost at D=2000 is at least about 5 ms. Then keep it as a T15 denial of service. If the per-leaf cost stays at or below about 1 ms, downgrade it to hardening, because memory bounds N first; in between, report the measured per-leaf cost and memory per entry to the owner together with the deployment answer. Either way, make the fix: drop the ancestor loop, which the walk's parent-first order makes redundant, or break it at the first ancestor already present. Confirm that the per-leaf cost of load then grows at most linearly in D (about 2x per doubling: the entry's own insert still makes about c comparisons of up to L bytes, so do not expect (ii) to stay within a fixed small factor of (i) at D=2000). Keep two regression tests: load's per-leaf cost at D=2000, N=200 is at most about 3x its per-leaf cost at D=1000, N=200; and, as a unit test in the tests module of crates/rnk-builder/src/sources.rs because keeps() is pub(crate), every kept entry's parent remains in the set (keeps() on each parent). Teardown: TempDir's drop calls std::fs::remove_dir_all, which keeps one directory fd open per level, so at D=2000 it fails silently under a soft RLIMIT_NOFILE of 1024 and leaves the tree; the ulimit -n 4096 above avoids that (or remove the chain bottom-up explicitly), and each case asserts that its TempDir path is gone. Optionally measure ContextFiles::resolve('*.json') over 100 top-level symlinks, each heading a 40-hop chain of targets near PATH_MAX, before and after replacing the per-component full-path join and lookup in follow().
validation_plan.deployment: The owner confirms two things: whether any supported or documented deployment builds an untrusted build context with an operator-supplied Dockerfile, given by --dockerfile as a host path outside the context, whose steps do not run code from the context, and which job timeout and CPU and memory cgroup limits its CI runners apply. Those limits cap the operator-owned spend. If every supported deployment takes the Dockerfile from the same principal as the context, the effect adds nothing beyond RUN's own unbounded CPU use, which T15 leaves to the outer cgroup, and the finding is hardening.

title: Root-run canonicalize of --context follows a symlink that a lower-trust principal controls in the operator's path, so COPY can copy root-only host directories into the stage root
description: ranikust runs as root and resolves the operator-typed --context with std::fs::canonicalize (crates/rnk-context/src/source.rs:46). canonicalize follows symlinks in every component and checks neither who owns a symlink nor who controls the directory that holds it. config.rs:576-602 and 639-643 only make the path absolute, and RootPath::open (root.rs:185-203) applies RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS to the path that is already resolved, so the resolved directory becomes the context root. Two lower-trust principals can choose that directory. (a) The author of an untrusted checkout can commit a symlink such as `services/api -> /root/.docker`. git recreates it on checkout, so the symlink is owned by whoever runs the checkout, root included, but its target is the author's choice. A CI step `ranikust --context=services/api` then reads it. The default -f 'Dockerfile' exists in the cwd, so the host route (build.rs:561-568) reads the same author's Dockerfile. (b) A local user who owns a component, such as /home/alice/ctx, can replace it with a symlink to a root-only directory. ranikust then walks that directory (build.rs:435-436, sources.rs:64-87) and lets COPY copy it into the stage root (stage.rs:905, 981). The exposure applies in overlay mode and in kaniko mode with per-stage directories. In those modes RUN otherwise cannot reach host files (full sandbox, pivot_root), and RUN --mount=type=bind is refused, so the redirected context is the only way host files reach the build. A later RUN can send the copied files out over the default host network, and they are also written to the image. Exposed: registry credentials (A3), other root-only host files (A1), and the state directory (A5). In kaniko per-stage mode, main.rs:568/673-722 refuses only a context inside the stages directory. Kaniko mode on a container's '/' adds nothing, since its RUN already reads '/' (threat-model.md section 6), and main.rs:537 refuses a context inside the root that the ignore list does not keep. No peer control applies. Neither an accepted ADR nor threat-model section 6 accepts this: ADR-0003 grants RUN docker-build-like isolation, and ADR-0053 only drops dir://. The only justification is the code comment at source.rs:44-45. Sibling operator paths are protected: the state directory is opened with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS and needs a root-owned, non-writable ancestor chain (statedir.rs:30-46, 246-254), and the beside-Dockerfile ignore file refuses a final symlink (source.rs:202-232). Calibration only, read from the local upstream checkouts: kaniko (kaniko@44aa7ddc0 cmd/executor/cmd/root.go:599-601, 656) uses a plain-path --context as given after filepath.Abs, so a symlinked context directory is followed as kaniko's root; buildctl --local (buildkit@cd8ee24 cmd/buildctl/build/local.go:18, vendor/github.com/tonistiigi/fsutil/fs.go:25-26) runs filepath.EvalSymlinks on it in the client, as the invoking user. The docker CLI is believed to do the same (no local checkout, unverified). Upstream parity does not settle the question: ADR-0049 lets parity break ties only between options equal on security and performance. Fix direction, for a maintainer ruling. Resolve a relative --context beneath a descriptor of the current directory (openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH or RESOLVE_IN_ROOT), so a symlink in the checkout cannot leave it. Refuse a symlink in an absolute --context (RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, as statedir.rs:246-254 does) with a message naming the resolved path. The ownership-only rule (systemd CHASE_SAFE) the hunter proposed would stop variant (b) and a checkout made by an unprivileged runner user, but not variant (a) when root runs the checkout: there every component and the symlink are root-owned. Regression tests (T2): a --context that is a symlink to a 0700 root-only directory, and a relative --context through a root-owned symlink committed in a checkout, must both be refused.
claimed_root_cause: DirSource::open treats every component of the operator-typed --context path as the operator's own (source.rs:44-45: 'The user's own argument: resolving its symlinks on the host is fine'). It resolves the path as root with std::fs::canonicalize (source.rs:46) and does not check whether a lower-trust principal controls a symlink it follows, either by owning a component or by committing the symlink to an untrusted checkout. A path the operator typed therefore resolves to whatever that principal chooses. The confinement RootPath gives inside the context (RESOLVE_IN_ROOT) only starts after that redirection, because RootPath::open (root.rs:185-193) sees only the already-canonical path.

trace.description: Operator-typed --context, default /workspace/ (line 77). In a monorepo CI step it often names a subdirectory of an untrusted checkout, and cli.rs:82-84 and config.rs:565-571 tell the operator to pass such a subdirectory as --context. The lower-trust input is not the flag string. It is what the filesystem at that path holds: a symlink that the checkout's author or a component owner controls.

context_with_sub_path/context_dir (config.rs:563-602) only check the scheme. absolute() (config.rs:639-643) applies std::path::absolute lexically. Nothing resolves the path or checks its ownership or symlinks.

rnk_context::open(&ContextSpec::Dir(config.context.clone())). Overlay mode reaches this with no context check (main.rs:353-362). Kaniko per-stage mode checks only that the context's physical path lies outside the stages directory (main.rs:568, 673-722).
ContextSpec::Dir dispatches to DirSource::new(path).open().
std::fs::canonicalize (realpath), run as root, follows the planted symlink to a root-only directory. It makes no check on owner, mode, sticky bit or a beneath-cwd rule.

RootPath::open(&canonical) pins the redirected directory as the context root. Its RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (root.rs:187-193) sees only the already-resolved path, and the canonical path becomes the context origin (line 53).
ContextFiles::load walks the redirected directory as the build context (sources.rs:64-87). The context-root .dockerignore is read in-root from that directory.
For a COPY from the context, src_root is cx.context.root(), which is now the root-only host directory.

rnk_rootfs::copy reads the root-only host file into the stage root (also stage.rs:963/965 for directory sources). The file lands in the layer, and a later RUN can read it: full isolation, but host network by default.

evidence.description: Design comment at lines 44-45: the --context argument is the user's own, so resolving its symlinks on the host is fine. It does not consider symlinks controlled by someone else. No ADR records this choice.
std::fs::canonicalize(&self.path), run as root, is the only resolution of the operator path.

RootPath::open calls openat2(CWD, host_dir, O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC, RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS) on the canonical path. It checks no owner, and NO_SYMLINKS has nothing left to refuse (doc at root.rs:175-177: callers pass a canonical path).
context_dir checks only the empty value and the URL schemes, and config.rs:639-643 makes the path absolute without touching the filesystem. No symlink or ownership check on --context.

Sibling control on another operator path: open_dir uses RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS (lines 246-254), and the ancestor chain must be root-owned and not group- or other-writable (statedir.rs:30-46).

Sibling control: the beside-Dockerfile ignore file is opened O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK and type-checked (source.rs:202-232, test crates/rnk-context/tests/context.rs:133-149). The context root gets no equivalent.

--context-sub-path is refused for a local directory, and the message (lines 566-570) tells the operator to pass dir.join(sub) as --context, which is the host-resolved route. Context::sub_context (source.rs:128-134) would resolve the subdirectory in-root.

dockerfile_source takes the host route for an absolute or cwd-existing -f (default 'Dockerfile', cli.rs:93). From a checkout root, the attacker's own Dockerfile is read while the context is the redirected directory.

paths_outside_the_root (kaniko modes only) resolves the context with physical_path (main.rs:725-745, canonicalize) and only refuses it inside the build root. Overlay mode (main.rs:353-362) has no context check.

Line 43: the Dockerfile and build context are hostile to ranikust's own code that reads them. Line 42: the operator's flags are trusted, and ranikust protects against typing mistakes, not intent. A symlink planted by a third party is neither the operator's intent nor a dangerous flag passed knowingly (section 8, lines 205-207). Section 6 (lines 100-160) does not accept this.
ADR-0003 makes trust in the Dockerfile the user's call and gives RUN isolation like docker build (pivot_root into the stage root). It does not accept the build input reaching root-only host files.

Every path from a build context is untrusted: reach it only through RootPath, never std::fs or Path::join onto a host path. The checkout containing the --context subdirectory is content of the same principal.
Limit: copy_data refuses a file that holds more than its stat size (copy.rs:777-786), so procfs targets such as /proc/self/environ are not copied. Ordinary root-only regular files are copied.

blockers: Run-specific constraint: no target-controlled execution and no OS-enforced sandbox in this run, so the end-to-end result is unobserved: a redirected context root, a layer holding the root-only file, and a RUN reading it under full isolation.

The precondition needs root outside a container: a symlink owned by another uid or committed to a root-run checkout, a 0700 root-only directory, and overlay or kaniko off-'/' mode. Project rules allow this only in the disposable VM (T2). The T2c lane reaches only kaniko mode on '/', which refuses this redirect (main.rs:537) and adds no exposure there.

Deployment fact: whether operators run ranikust as root with a --context (or absolute -f) that names a path a lower-trust principal controls. Examples are a subdirectory of an untrusted pull-request checkout in a pipeline whose definition that author cannot change, or another account's directory. If the author can edit the pipeline flags, there is no boundary.

Scope ruling from the maintainer: threat-model.md section 3 trusts operator flags, and source.rs:44-45 treats the --context path as the operator's own. statedir.rs:246-254 and read_beside_dockerfile treat lower-trust-controlled path components as a threat. The ruling should also pick the fix: beneath-cwd resolution and/or RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS. An ownership-only CHASE_SAFE rule does not cover a root-run checkout.

validation_plan.local:
In the disposable VM only (`just test-vm`, tier T2), as root on the guest, with dummy data. Overlay mode and kaniko off-'/' mode both need a non-container root. The T2c rootful-Docker lane reaches only kaniko mode on '/', where main.rs:537 refuses a context inside the root, so use it only as a negative control. (1) Root-only directory: `install -d -m 0700 /srv/h43/rootonly && echo DUMMY-H43-TOKEN > /srv/h43/rootonly/token && chmod 0600 /srv/h43/rootonly/token`. (2) Owner variant: `install -d -o 1000 -g 1000 -m 0755 /srv/h43/alice && setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --clear-groups ln -s /srv/h43/rootonly /srv/h43/alice/ctx`. As uid 1000, confirm that `cat /srv/h43/alice/ctx/token` is denied. (3) `printf 'FROM busybox
COPY token /token
RUN cat /token
' > /srv/h43/Dockerfile`. (4) `ranikust --context=/srv/h43/alice/ctx --dockerfile=/srv/h43/Dockerfile --no-push --oci-layout-path=/srv/h43/out --mode=overlay`, then the same with `--mode=kaniko` and `--oci-layout-path=/srv/h43/out-k` (off '/', per-stage directories). Expected at ed718fb: exit 0, the RUN output prints DUMMY-H43-TOKEN, and `for b in /srv/h43/out/blobs/sha256/*; do tar -xzOf "$b" token 2>/dev/null; done` prints it. (5) Repository variant, checkout made by root, which shows that an ownership-only fix is not enough: `git init /srv/h43/repo && cd /srv/h43/repo && mkdir services && ln -s /srv/h43/rootonly services/api && cp /srv/h43/Dockerfile Dockerfile && git add -A && git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm t && git clone -q /srv/h43/repo /srv/h43/checkout && cd /srv/h43/checkout && stat -c '%U %N' services/api && ranikust --context=services/api --no-push --oci-layout-path=/srv/h43/out2 --mode=overlay`. Expected at ed718fb: the same token disclosure, through a root-owned symlink. Repeat (5) with the clone made by uid 1000 (`setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --clear-groups git clone -q /srv/h43/repo /srv/h43/checkout-u`), still running ranikust as root. Expected after a fix: steps (4) and (5) are refused with a message naming the symlinked --context component, and a plain directory --context still builds. Clean up with `rm -rf /srv/h43` afterwards, and stop after observing the boundary result.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed check, no live probing. In the maintainer's own CI and pipeline definitions, list ranikust invocations that run as root in overlay mode or kaniko off-'/' mode and whose --context, or absolute --dockerfile, names a path below a checkout of code the pipeline author does not control: a pull-request or fork checkout built by a pipeline the PR cannot edit (for example pull_request_target or a centrally defined pipeline), or another account's directory. Each such invocation meets the precondition. Also note whether root-only files with credentials (for example /root/.docker/config.json or a mounted service-account token) exist where that ranikust process runs.

title: --registry-certificate read follows a symlink at an operator-chosen path and opens any host file as root (operator-trust issue, not a vulnerability)
description: TrustStore::with_pem_file reads the --registry-certificate path with std::fs::read (tls.rs:68). That is a blocking open that follows symlinks, with no file-type check and no size bound. The candidate says that when the operator names a path inside the build context, or a relative path while cwd is the checkout, a context owner can commit a symlink there to /dev/watchdog, /dev/port, /dev/zero or a FIFO. Root on the host then opens and reads that file at build start. The source trace is accurate. But the path and the cwd are both chosen by the trusted operator (threat-model.md:42). The context owner only gets an effect once the operator has made a context-owned file the CA for a registry, and that already hands the context owner the registry's trust anchor, a stronger capability than the DoS the symlink adds. Threat-model section 8 (threat-model.md:205-207) says anything that needs the operator to pass a dangerous flag knowingly is not a vulnerability. The cited peer control, open_secret, also follows symlinks and opens devices (O_NONBLOCK does not stop a device's open handler), so it would not prevent the watchdog effect either. A sibling candidate about --secret following cwd symlinks was rejected for the same reason. What remains is at most a hardening or documentation note.
claimed_root_cause: TrustStore::with_pem_file reads the operator-named path with std::fs::read (tls.rs:68): a blocking open that follows symlinks, with no fstat type check and no size bound. config.rs:426-429 keeps the path made absolute against cwd without touching the filesystem, and Client::new (client.rs:390-392) passes it on unchanged. The candidate contrasts this with open_secret (mounts.rs:75-96: O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, regular-file and size checks) and read_beside_dockerfile (source.rs:204-232: O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK, regular-file check).

trace.description: The operator, a trusted principal, passes --registry-certificate REGISTRY=PATH. It is split into (registry, PathBuf) with no check. The operator chooses both the path and the cwd it resolves against; the context owner chooses neither.
The path is made absolute against cwd with std::path::absolute, which does not touch the filesystem. Nothing checks whether it lies in the context or what type of file it is.
config.registry_certificates is copied into ClientOptions unchanged.
Client::new runs at build start, after ContextFiles::load (build.rs:436) and before any stage, as ranikust's own process.
with_pem_file(path) is called for each registry_certificates entry. The result only adds trust for that registry (client.rs:390-393).

fs::read(path) opens the path, following symlinks, and reads to EOF with no type check or bound. Then it parses the content as PEM. If the operator pointed this at context-owned content, the context owner already chooses the registry's CA.

evidence.description: let pem = fs::read(path): no O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK or O_NOCTTY, no fstat type check, no size limit. The source description is accurate.

Operator flags are trusted. ranikust protects the operator from typing mistakes, not from intent. --registry-certificate is an operator flag, and the operator also chooses the cwd it resolves against.

The context is treated as hostile where ranikust's own code reads it (parser, COPY, .dockerignore). with_pem_file is not such a reader: it reads only the operator-named file, and reaches context content only if the operator points it there.

Section 8: anything that needs the operator to pass a dangerous flag knowingly is not a vulnerability, though it may still be a documentation bug. Naming a context-owned file as a registry CA is such a choice: it already gives the context owner the trust anchor, which can impersonate a credentialed registry.

Per-registry trust is the base store plus the named file's certificates, so whoever controls the file's content controls that registry's CA. That is strictly more than the availability effect a symlink adds.

The cited peer control, open_secret, opens RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY|CLOEXEC without O_NOFOLLOW. It also follows a symlink and runs a device's open handler (O_NONBLOCK does not stop watchdog_open) before its fstat refusal at line 84. So the operator-path peer read has the same watchdog exposure when an operator names a context path. The sibling --secret cwd-symlink candidate was rejected because the operator chooses that path and cwd.

Calibration: an operator-named host Dockerfile, including the default 'Dockerfile' that exists relative to cwd (build.rs:562), is read with plain File::open following symlinks. The code consistently treats operator-chosen host paths as operator input. Only reads ranikust makes into the context on its own (open_regular, read_beside_dockerfile) are confined.

--registry-certificate=r.example=certs/r.pem resolves to cwd/certs/r.pem (assert at line 230). This is the operator's relative path against the operator's cwd. It does not show that ranikust itself places the path in the context.

reason: The lower-trust principal does not control the input. The --registry-certificate path and the cwd it resolves against are chosen by the trusted operator (threat-model.md:42). The context owner gets an effect only if the operator has made a context-owned file the CA for a registry. That already gives the context owner the trust anchor for that registry, a stronger capability than the host DoS the symlink adds. Threat-model section 8 (threat-model.md:205-207) says such a dangerous operator choice is not a vulnerability. The claimed inconsistency with peer controls also fails for the main effect. open_secret (mounts.rs:79) follows symlinks and still runs a device's open handler before its type check, and an operator-named host Dockerfile is read with a plain open (build.rs:592). The sibling --secret cwd-symlink candidate was rejected for the same reason. Remaining value is a hardening or documentation note: open the certificate with O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, refuse a non-regular file by fstat, bound the size, and document that the certificate file must not live in an untrusted context.

title: Kaniko mode on /: ranikust follows RUN-planted links at operator output and --secret paths with capabilities withheld from the RUN (CAP_SYS_PTRACE), reaching files in the mount namespace of peers the RUN cannot reach by itself
description: In kaniko mode on a container's / (Isolation::Direct), a container whose bounding set holds a capability outside Docker's 14 together with CAP_SETPCAP (a Docker default) gets DirectCaps::Drop: only the RUN child drops the extras (direct.rs:66-70); the ranikust process never changes its own sets (the only capset/bounding-drop calls are child.rs:1268 and 1297; main.rs:95-99 says nothing changes ranikust's credentials), so a root ranikust keeps e.g. CAP_SYS_PTRACE effective for the whole build. ADR-0051:92-94 and the VM suite (tests/vm/guest/secrets.sh:95, scenario ptrace --cap-add SYS_PTRACE) treat that container as supported. Every operator output and --secret src path lies inside / there, so paths_outside_the_root (main.rs:673-724) requires it to be on the ignore list (a volume or bind mount point, /ranikust, --ignore-path); the check is a one-time physical_path canonicalization before the root changes, with nothing pinned or re-checked after RUNs. A Direct RUN is uid 0 with DAC_OVERRIDE and no mount namespace, so it can write in any such writable location (the VM suite itself binds a writable /ranikust/out and writes --oci-layout-path there) and can learn the flags from /proc/<ranikust>/cmdline (accepted as readable, threat-model.md:109-110). After the RUNs, ranikust reopens these paths by name with symlink and magic-link following: (1) write_digest_files (build.rs:734-753, called at build.rs:940) does DirBuilder recursive 0700 and OpenOptions write|create|truncate on the path, so a RUN-planted /out/digest -> /proc/<pid>/root/<file> makes ranikust create, or truncate and overwrite, <file> in the target process's mount namespace with the digest or repository@digest text; (2) write_oci_layout (output.rs:137, 387-399, 429-475), write_docker_tar (output.rs:177, 241) and the metrics report (report.rs:354-382, at exit via collector.rs:170) follow every parent component, so a RUN-made parent link (e.g. <layout>/blobs/sha256 -> /proc/<pid>/root/tmp) makes ranikust create or replace fixed-name files (oci-layout, index.json, blobs/sha256/<hex>, the tar or report basename) there, content partly RUN-controlled; the leaf itself is replaced by rename, not followed; (3) a --secret src file is re-opened for every RUN that mounts it (mounts.rs:147, 396 -> 53 -> open_secret at 75-82 via rustix::fs::open without O_NOFOLLOW), checked only for regular file and <= 500 KiB, and in Direct mode its bytes become the RUN's variable (mounts.rs:292, 404-410; NUL bytes refused), so a later RUN with --mount=type=secret,id=<id>,env=X receives a NUL-free file from the other mount namespace; this needs the src to sit in a RUN-writable directory, not a read-only secret volume. The magic link /proc/<pid>/root (and /proc/<pid>/fd/*) is gated by ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS), which compares the caller's fsuid/fsgid with the target's ids and, in commoncap, the target's permitted set with the caller's effective set. A Direct RUN keeps CAP_SETUID and CAP_SETGID (Docker defaults, caps.rs:13-14), so it passes that check by itself for any dumpable peer with uniform ids whose permitted set lies inside its own, a non-root peer such as a uid-1000 process included: switch fsuid/fsgid (or euid/egid) to the peer's, take /proc/<pid>/root as cwd or an O_PATH descriptor, switch back to 0 and open with DAC_OVERRIDE. Reaching such peers falls under the accepted lack of isolation between RUN and the container (threat-model.md:106-107, 127-128) and gains nothing from ranikust. The RUN fails the check, while ranikust's retained CAP_SYS_PTRACE passes it, only for a peer in ranikust's own user namespace that is not dumpable, holds a permitted capability outside the RUN's effective set (a root peer started with --cap-add; a --privileged peer too, but it runs unconfined under AppArmor, see below), or has mixed real/effective/saved ids [inferred from the kernel's ptrace and commoncap checks as ptrace(2) 'Ptrace access mode checking' describes them, unobserved]. A peer in another user namespace is no such case: a user namespace below the RUN's is owned by uid 0 when root created it (Docker userns-remap, Kubernetes hostUsers: false) or by a uid the RUN can take as its euid with CAP_SETUID (rootless containers), and a process of the parent namespace whose euid is the owner has every capability, CAP_SYS_PTRACE included, in that namespace and its descendants (user_namespaces(7)), so the RUN reaches such a peer by itself; a peer in a sibling or ancestor user namespace is beyond ranikust's capability as well [inferred, unobserved]. Reaching such a process needs a PID namespace shared beyond the build container (docker --pid=container:X or --pid=host, Kubernetes shareProcessNamespace or hostPID) and an LSM that permits the access (AppArmor docker-default and cri-containerd.apparmor.d allow ptrace read between peers confined by the same profile; unconfined peers, host processes and --privileged containers alike, and SELinux MCS-separated containers are expected to deny; with no LSM nothing denies). For such a peer this would let the Dockerfile author's RUN make ranikust write files outside the build container, its state and its requested outputs (asset A1, threat-model.md:30; rules.md:31; the Critical row at threat-model.md:200) and read them (cross-container secrets), using a capability ADR-0051 withholds from the RUN; no ADR or threat-model section 6 entry accepts ranikust acting on the RUN's behalf this way. Not affected: user-database reads (RootPath, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, root.rs:18) and procfs/cgroup reads. Related, needing no extra capability: a --secret src link to /proc/self/fd/<n> would make ranikust re-open one of its own descriptors for the RUN (T21's state); which of its descriptors hold NUL-free regular files <= 500 KiB is unobserved.
claimed_root_cause: In Direct mode on /, only the RUN child gives up the capabilities outside Docker's defaults (caps.rs:139-146 DirectCaps::Drop, spawner.rs:875-877, direct.rs:66-70); the ranikust process keeps them (by design, ADR-0051:49-52). Its operator-path I/O after the RUNs (build.rs:741-753 digest files, output.rs:137/393/445-472 layout and tar, report.rs:365-382 metrics, mounts.rs:75-82 secret re-open) resolves those paths by name, following symlinks and magic links, with no descriptor pinned at the one-time check (main.rs:673-724) and in locations a Direct RUN can rewrite. The by-path opens act as a confused deputy, applying CAP_SYS_PTRACE that the RUN was denied to RUN-chosen /proc/<pid>/root targets that the RUN could not pass the ptrace check for by itself, even after switching its fsuid/fsgid (peers in ranikust's own user namespace that are not dumpable, hold permitted capabilities outside Docker's 14, or have mixed real/effective/saved ids; not peers in another user namespace, which the RUN reaches by itself as, or after switching its euid to, the namespace owner, or which ranikust's capability does not reach either).

trace.description: The Dockerfile author's RUN command is exec'd as uid 0 on the container's own / with no mount namespace, after the child alone dropped the extras (direct.rs:66-70); it can create symlinks in any writable ignored location (a volume, /ranikust/out) where the operator's outputs and --secret src files must live.

Extras (e.g. CAP_SYS_PTRACE) with CAP_SETPCAP give DirectCaps::Drop, applied only to the child through job.args.direct_drop (spawner.rs:875-877); no parent-side capset or bounding-set drop exists, so ranikust's effective set keeps CAP_SYS_PTRACE.

Output, metrics and --secret file paths are canonicalized once before the root changes and only required to be on the ignore list; no descriptor is pinned and nothing re-checks them after RUNs. refuse_unsafe_slash (main.rs:462-504) does not consider extra capabilities or a shared PID namespace.
After run_units has run and swept every RUN, the image is assembled and write_digest_files is called with the operator's paths, then write_oci_layout and write_docker_tar (build.rs:942-947).

OpenOptions write|create|truncate .open(path) without O_NOFOLLOW (build.rs:747-752) follows a RUN-planted digest-file symlink to /proc/<pid>/root/<file>; for a peer the RUN cannot pass the magic link's ptrace_may_access check for by itself (in ranikust's own user namespace and not dumpable, holding capabilities outside Docker's 14, or with mixed real/effective/saved ids), ranikust's retained CAP_SYS_PTRACE passes it, so a file in that peer's mount namespace would be created, or truncated and overwritten.

evidence.description: direct_caps: extras with setpcap -> DirectCaps::Drop; without setpcap -> Refuse.
args.direct_drop -> drop_capabilities in the child only; the comment says a RUN with CAP_SYS_PTRACE would read ranikust's descriptors and memory (ADR-0051).

direct_slash_drop reads the bounding set and SETPCAP and only returns whether the child drops; the only set_capabilities/remove_capability_from_bounding_set calls in crates/*/src are child.rs:1268 and 1297.

DOCKER_DEFAULT keeps SETGID (6) and SETUID (7) in the Direct RUN's permitted and effective sets, so the RUN can match a peer's fsuid/fsgid and pass ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) by itself for a dumpable peer whose permitted set lies inside its own, and can be (uid 0) or become (seteuid) the owner of any user namespace below its own, which holds CAP_SYS_PTRACE there; only non-dumpable, extra-capability or mixed-id peers in ranikust's own user namespace make ranikust's retained capability a gain.

The drop is in the RUN child only, 'no constraint on ranikust's own threads' (lines 49-52); lines 92-94 call the container with SYS_PTRACE added supported. The ADR does not consider ranikust using the retained capability on RUN-shaped paths.

Scenario 'ptrace --cap-add SYS_PTRACE' is a supported deployment; the suite binds a writable /ranikust/out and writes --oci-layout-path there (lines 68-78); no output-path or secret-path symlink case.
refuse_unsafe_slash refuses only can_mount, --network=none and a writable /proc/sys; exposure.rs only warns about other processes in the PID namespace.
--secret src files are among the operator paths checked once, with --tar-path, --oci-layout-path, the digest files and --metrics-file (main.rs:679-700).
FIXED ignore entries (/ranikust at line 171) and mount points satisfy paths_outside_the_root; the ignore list governs walk and emptying only and does not make these places read-only to a Direct RUN.
DirBuilder recursive 0700 create(parent) follows symlinks; the comment 'These are operator paths, not the image's' (line 736) does not consider RUN-writable locations.
write_atomically: tempfile_in(parent) (line 461) then persist(path) (line 472) by name; parents (create_dir_all at 137 and 393) are followed, so layout and tar files land in a RUN-chosen directory.
write_file: create_dir_all(dir) (365), O_EXCL temporary and rename by parent path (382), called at exit from collector.rs:170.

open_secret: rustix::fs::open(path, RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY|CLOEXEC) follows symlinks and magic links; called per RUN (secret.read at 396 -> 53); Direct keeps env= secrets (292) and passes the bytes as the RUN's variable (404-410).
The sibling control for image paths, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, is not used at the operator-path sites.

Asset A1: host files outside the state directory, store, requested outputs and, in kaniko mode in a container, /; line 200 rates untrusted input making ranikust write a host file outside its directories as Critical; section 6 (lines 100-130) accepts the RUN acting on the container's own / and reading --secret src files, not ranikust reaching other mount namespaces for it.

Accepted: with kernel.yama.ptrace_scope 0 a RUN may trace other dumpable processes of its user, and lines 106-107 accept no isolation between RUN and the container; peers a RUN reaches by itself are within that, so the finding is limited to peers beyond the RUN's own ptrace reach.
Invariant: write only to the build root ranikust picked, the state directory or store, and the outputs.

blockers: Run-specific constraint: no target-controlled execution and no OS-enforced sandbox on this host, so the build, the RUN-planted links and the resulting writes and reads were not observed.

Kernel and LSM runtime fact (inferred from the kernel's ptrace_may_access, cap_ptrace_access_check and cap_capable as ptrace(2) and user_namespaces(7) describe them, unobserved): that ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) on /proc/<pid>/root fails for a Direct RUN (uid 0, Docker's 14 including SETUID/SETGID, whatever fsuid/fsgid or euid/egid it switches to) but passes for ranikust (uid 0, CAP_SYS_PTRACE) on a peer in their own user namespace that is not dumpable, holds a capability outside Docker's 14, or has mixed real/effective/saved ids, while a dumpable non-root peer with an empty permitted set (e.g. uid 1000) and a peer in a user namespace below the RUN's (the RUN being, or switching its euid to, that namespace's owner) are reachable by the RUN alone; and that AppArmor docker-default (ptrace peer rule, attach_disconnected path naming) then permits ranikust's open for write and read in the peer container; SELinux container_t across MCS labels and unconfined peers under AppArmor (host processes, --privileged containers) are expected to deny.

Deployment fact: impact needs a builder container with a capability outside Docker's 14 (CAP_SYS_PTRACE) plus CAP_SETPCAP, a PID namespace shared (--pid=container:X, --pid=host, shareProcessNamespace, hostPID) with a peer in the builder's user namespace that the RUN cannot reach by itself (not dumpable, holding capabilities outside Docker's 14, or with mixed real/effective/saved ids) under an LSM that lets ranikust read it, and, for the secret variant, a --secret src in a RUN-writable directory; how common that combination is in supported deployments is not source-visible.

validation_plan.local: T2 VM (just test-vm, Ubuntu 24.04 rootful Docker, AppArmor docker-default) or T2c (just test-container, ADR-0063 marker), dummy data only, modelled on tests/vm/guest/secrets.sh with IMAGE=mirror.gcr.io/library/ubuntu:24.04 and RNK=$HOME/rnk/bin/ranikust. (1) W=/var/tmp/rnk-deputy; sudo rm -rf $W; sudo mkdir -m 755 $W $W/ctx $W/out; printf dummy | sudo tee $W/out/s.txt. (2) A peer the RUN cannot reach by itself (root, its permitted set holding NET_ADMIN, outside the RUN's 14): sudo docker run -d --name rnk-victim --cap-add NET_ADMIN $IMAGE sleep 3600; sudo docker exec rnk-victim sh -c 'printf canary-RNK-7 > /etc/victim-canary; chmod 600 /etc/victim-canary'. (3) $W/ctx/Dockerfile, $IMAGE expanded: 'FROM $IMAGE' / 'RUN (cat /proc/1/root/etc/victim-canary && echo RUN-CAN-READ) || echo RUN-DENIED; ln -sfn /proc/1/root/etc/victim-canary /ranikust/out/digest; ln -sfn /proc/1/root/etc/victim-canary /ranikust/out/s.txt; mkdir -p /ranikust/out/oci/blobs; ln -sfn /proc/1/root/tmp /ranikust/out/oci/blobs/sha256' / 'RUN --mount=type=secret,id=s,env=S sh -c "echo leaked=$S"'. (4) sudo docker run --rm --pid=container:rnk-victim --cap-add SYS_PTRACE -v $RNK:/ranikust/bin/ranikust:ro -v $W/ctx:/ranikust/ctx:ro -v $W/out:/ranikust/out -v /etc/ssl/certs:/etc/ssl/certs:ro $IMAGE /ranikust/bin/ranikust --mode=kaniko --context /ranikust/ctx --no-push --digest-file /ranikust/out/digest --oci-layout-path /ranikust/out/oci --secret id=s,src=/ranikust/out/s.txt 2>&1 | sudo tee $W/run.log >/dev/null ($W is root-owned, so the log is written through sudo tee, not a plain redirect). Vulnerable if run.log shows RUN-DENIED from the first RUN and leaked=canary-RNK-7 from the second, sudo docker exec rnk-victim cat /etc/victim-canary prints sha256:..., and sudo docker exec rnk-victim ls -la /tmp lists blob files. Controls: (a) the same without --cap-add SYS_PTRACE (expect ranikust's secret open to fail with EACCES and the build to stop); (b) a peer the RUN reaches by itself, which is not a gain: recreate rnk-victim with --user 1000:1000 and no --cap-add, write the canary as root 0600 through sudo docker exec -u 0, reduce the Dockerfile to FROM and RUN perl -e '$)="1000 1000"; $>=1000; chdir "/proc/1/root/etc" or die "chdir: $!"; $>=0; $)="0 0"; open(F, "<", "victim-canary") or die "open: $!"; print <F>', and build with step (4) minus --cap-add SYS_PTRACE and the --digest-file, --oci-layout-path and --secret flags (expect canary-RNK-7 printed by the RUN alone; if it is refused, record the errno, since uid-1000 peers would then count too); (c) step (4) with --pid=host and the host pid of a root sleep 600 in place of 1 in the Dockerfile (expect apparmor="DENIED" operation="ptrace" in dmesg); optionally s.txt -> /proc/self/fd/<n> for a descriptor number listed from /proc/<ranikust>/fd (records which of ranikust's own descriptors a RUN can get re-opened). Record uname -r, docker info security options and aa-status. Stop after these observations; sudo docker rm -f rnk-victim; sudo rm -rf $W.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: for each supported deployment of kaniko mode on / (Docker, Kubernetes, Tekton/Argo/GitLab pipelines), record whether the builder container gets any capability outside Docker's 14 (notably SYS_PTRACE) with SETPCAP, whether it shares a PID namespace (hostPID, shareProcessNamespace, --pid) with a process in the builder's user namespace that the RUN cannot reach by itself (not dumpable, holding capabilities outside Docker's 14, or with mixed real/effective/saved ids; a process in a user namespace below the builder's is reachable by the RUN anyway), which LSM profile is attached to it and its peers (unconfined peers are expected to be denied under AppArmor), and whether the output and --secret src directories are writable volumes; only the combination of a retained extra capability, such a peer in a shared PID namespace, and a permitting LSM is exposed.

title: Base-image tar entry names reach ranikust's fatal error line on stderr with terminal control bytes and newlines intact
description: A base-image publisher (lower-trust per docs/security/threat-model.md:44) controls the raw name bytes of every entry in its layers. rnk-rootfs keeps a refused entry's raw name in Error::Entry (extract.rs:319-324) and renders it with path.display() (error.rs:58), which replaces only invalid UTF-8 and passes ESC, BEL, CR, LF and UTF-8-encoded C1 controls through. In overlay mode every image-based stage extracts its base layers at prepare time whether or not it has a RUN (rnk-builder pull.rs:123 -> rnk-snapshot stage.rs:300 -> layer.rs:127), and the error text survives every wrapper: rnk_store Error::Fill 'filling {key}: {source}' (store.rs:681, error.rs:107), rnk_snapshot Store/Rootfs (transparent), rnk_builder Snapshot (transparent), rnk_sched Prepare 'stage {name}: preparing: {source}' (sched error.rs:21; in kaniko mode the base is extracted in the stage run and Stage at line 10 applies), build.rs:923 to_string, main.rs:363/452 Failure::error, main.rs:166 report(), and main.rs:180 writes 'ranikust: error: {message}' to stderr verbatim. No neutralization exists anywhere on this path, and --log-format does not affect report(). Other refusals (GNU sparse, unsupported entry type, bad hardlink target) carry the same raw name, so '..' is not required. A secondary, lower-value sink: rnk-oci MediaType deserializes any string (media_type.rs:239) and Display writes it as is; a Docker tar output (--tar-path, write_docker_tar output.rs:177) fails with UnknownLayerType showing it raw (builder error.rs:61, raised at output.rs:211). The default color log formatter (logfmt.rs:65-75, default per cli.rs:296) also writes event messages raw, while text and JSON escape them (logfmt.rs:165, 179); no publisher-reachable non-failing warning carrying such a name was established in this check (meta.rs:531 SkippedXattrs is a candidate, reachability unverified). Corrections to the hunter: the overlay-mode error is a scheduler Prepare error, not Stage, and passes through rnk-store's Fill wrapper; ranikust's real success output is an INFO log line 'built image sha256:...' (main.rs:370) plus the bare digest on stdout (main.rs:371), so injected stderr text can imitate a success line but cannot change stdout or the exit code 1 of the failed build. Scope: where a RUN executes the publisher's code, that code already writes raw bytes to the same streams through the relay (relay.rs:58), so the increment is confined to images used only by COPY-only stages (for example a distroless final stage) and COPY --from=<image> sources. Impact is limited to forged or misleading log lines and terminal escape sequences in the operator's terminal or CI log; whether that goes beyond cosmetic depends on the consumer. The project already neutralizes untrusted registry text (rnk-registry excerpt(), error.rs:229-233) and quotes untrusted names with {:?} in rnk-sandbox and rnk-rootfs user.rs, and neither threat-model section 6 nor an ADR accepts raw untrusted text in ranikust's own messages, so this is a candidate rather than an accepted risk. Fix: escape control characters at report() and in the color formatter's message (an excerpt-like escape that keeps one line), and render rnk-rootfs, rnk-store and rnk-snapshot paths and MediaType in errors with an escaping form such as {:?}. Regression test: Error::Entry for a name with ESC, BEL and LF displays none of those bytes, and report() output is one line.
claimed_root_cause: ranikust's sink for its own fatal error, main.rs report(), and the default Color formatter in rnk-metrics logfmt.rs write message text verbatim, and the lower-trust strings embedded in those messages (tar entry names from base-image layers via path.display() in rnk-rootfs error.rs, manifest media types via MediaType's Display) are not escaped at the error-type level either, unlike registry text, which rnk-registry's excerpt() neutralizes.

trace.description: Each layer blob of the image named by FROM (or COPY --from=<image>) is pulled; its bytes are the base-image publisher's, checked only against the digests in the publisher's own manifest.
Every pulled layer is extracted through snapshotter.base_layer at prepare time, for any image-based stage, with or without RUN.
The overlay snapshotter calls layer::extract_layer with the blob file.
extract_overlay runs inside store.fill; its rnk_rootfs::Error is returned with ? as rnk_snapshot::Error::Rootfs (transparent).
The entry's raw name bytes (ustar/GNU name, GNU long name or PAX path; any byte but NUL) become raw, with no validation of the bytes.
path::clean returns None for a name that climbs above the root, and Error::Entry { path: raw, reason: 'the name leaves the root' } is returned; other refusals in this function use the same raw name.
Displayed as 'tar entry {}' with path.display(), which replaces only invalid UTF-8 and keeps ESC, BEL, CR and LF.

The filler's error becomes Error::Fill, displayed as 'filling {key}: {source}' (rnk-store error.rs:107), keeping the inner text; rnk_snapshot::Error::Store and rnk_builder::Error::Snapshot are transparent.

The failure of the stage's prepare step (base pull and extraction) is formatted as 'stage {name}: preparing: {source}'; in kaniko mode the base is extracted in the stage run and Error::Stage (line 10) formats it the same way.
summary.map_err(|e| e.to_string()) turns the whole chain into the failure string, which main.rs:363 (overlay) or main.rs:452 (kaniko) wraps with Failure::error.
The failure message is passed to report().
writeln!(std::io::stderr(), 'ranikust: error: {message}') writes the bytes verbatim to the operator's terminal or CI log, whatever --log-format says.

evidence.description: Sibling control: excerpt() is documented as 'At most 200 characters of an untrusted message, on one line' and replaces every control character with a space (line 233); nothing equivalent exists in rnk-rootfs, rnk-store, rnk-snapshot or main.rs report().
The same crate quotes an untrusted user name with {name:?}, while error.rs:30, 44, 58 and 68 render in-root and tar-entry paths with path.display().

rnk-sandbox formats host paths with {path:?} and the program with {program:?} (line 226), which escapes control characters; its Rootfs variant (line 318) is transparent, so rnk-rootfs path text still passes unescaped.
The Color formatter (a custom FormatEvent) embeds f.message raw in the line; the text format quotes it (line 165) and JSON escapes it through serde_json (line 179).
--log-format defaults to Color, so a warning that carries lower-trust text is written raw by default.

MediaType deserializes any string without syntax validation and Display writes it as is (line 209); with --tar-path, write_docker_tar (rnk-builder output.rs:177) raises UnknownLayerType at output.rs:211, whose message shows it (rnk-builder error.rs:61).
RUN stdout and stderr are copied raw to ranikust's fds 1 and 2, so base-image code that a RUN executes can already write control bytes there; the increment is limited to images used without RUN.

The genuine success output is an INFO log line 'built image <digest>' and the bare digest on stdout (line 371); injected stderr text can imitate the log line but cannot change stdout or the failed build's exit code.

Possible non-failing variant: SkippedXattrs::note keeps path.display() and the xattr name, warned through the color formatter at line 538 while the copy goes on; whether a base-image publisher can reach it depends on which xattrs the destination refuses (unverified).

Section 6 (accepted risks) and the ADRs accept no raw untrusted text in ranikust's own messages; the operator's terminal or CI log is not among assets A1-A7 either, which is why impact hinges on the consumer.

blockers: This run forbids executing target code, so the bytes reaching stderr are established from source only (std's Path::display keeps valid-UTF-8 control bytes), not observed.

Whether the effect goes beyond a misleading line in a failed build's log depends on the consumer of ranikust's stderr (terminal handling of OSC/CSI sequences such as OSC 52, OSC 8 or title reports, and whether a CI log processor interprets injected lines as commands), which is outside the repository.

validation_plan.local: T0, no root, dummy data: in crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract/tests.rs, next to names_that_leave_the_root_are_refused, build a stream with the existing raw-name Tar helper: let f = Fixture::new(); let mut t = Tar::new(&f); t.file("../\x1b]0;RNK\x07\n\x1b[36mINFO\x1b[0m[0001] built image sha256:0000", 0o644, b"x"); let e = extract(&f.root, t.bytes().as_slice(), Whiteouts::Apply).unwrap_err(); then assert that format!("{e}") contains no 0x1b, 0x07 or 0x0a byte (expected to fail at ed718fb). Run it with cargo test -p rnk-rootfs names_with_control_bytes. End to end, in the disposable VM (just test-vm, T2) or the T2c rootful-Docker lane (marker-guarded, ADR-0063): start a loopback registry:2 inside the lane, push a one-layer dummy image localhost:5000/esc-test whose layer tar (written with Python's tarfile, no filter) holds the same entry name, build a context with a file f and a Dockerfile 'FROM localhost:5000/esc-test' then 'COPY f /f' (no RUN) with --no-push, capture stdout to out.txt and stderr to err.bin, and check with od -c err.bin for a raw 033 and 007 and for a second line starting with the injected INFO text; check that out.txt is empty and the exit code is 1. Repeat with --tar-path and a manifest whose layer mediaType holds \u001b to check the UnknownLayerType path.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, dummy image only: in a private test repository of each CI system that runs ranikust (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI), feed the same image and check whether injected stderr lines render as ranikust's own or are processed as workflow commands; on the operators' usual terminals, check whether OSC 52, OSC 8 or title-report sequences in ranikust's error line take effect.

title: Kaniko mode on / accepts a persistent store as its state directory and does not exclude persistent builds on it, so a Direct RUN reaches other builds' private build directories
description: In a default container, set_up_kaniko runs every RUN as Isolation::Direct (setup.rs:352-356). The Dockerfile author's command runs as root on the container's /, and the state directory is an ordinary path there (ADR-0051:14-16). statedir::prepare accepts a state directory that holds a regular .ranikust-state, and it does so in every mode (statedir.rs:191-197). ADR-0050:59-62 and kaniko-mode.md:399-401 state that rule with no exception for kaniko mode on /. So a volume that already holds a persistent store is opened with Store::open_anonymous (setup.rs:322-323). Such a store comes from overlay builds in a --privileged container, or from a host store bind-mounted into the container. open_anonymous only logs that 'a RUN can read what it holds' (store.rs:403-409), and main.rs:522 checks only is_anonymous(). open_anonymous takes an exclusive flock on the state directory (store.rs:376). Store::open (store.rs:290-323) never takes or tests that lock; it locks only builds/<id>.lock (register, store.rs:1308-1345). On a volume that already holds .ranikust-state, an anonymous build and persistent builds therefore run at the same time, whichever starts first. The gap needs that marker: on a volume first taken by an anonymous store, which holds only .ranikust-building, Store::open refuses NotAStateDir in check_marker (store.rs:1253-1283). While a persistent build runs, the Direct RUN is root with Docker's default capabilities on the same volume. It can list and read that build's private stage directories: builds/<id>/stages/<n>/diff-<k> and work-<k> (stage.rs:325-330, 488-500). They hold the other build's COPY'd context files and RUN output. The RUN can also create, change or delete entries there, under tmp/<id>, and in builds/<id>.lock. This contradicts four documents. ADR-0007:32 gives each build a private builds/<id>. threat-model.md:46 says only content-addressed data is shared with builds of another trust domain. ADR-0051:29-31 keeps persistent stores only where RUN has its own namespaces. ADR-0056:81-83 and how-it-builds.md:140-142 say a second build on a state directory in use is refused. Section 6 (threat-model.md:107-116) accepts a Direct RUN reading files mounted into the container, but only as something ranikust 'can only warn about'. Here ranikust recognises the directory as its own persistent store and could refuse it, as it refuses foreign non-empty directories. The operator picks the volume, but ranikust's own guidance makes sharing one volume between both modes a plausible slip. It gives '-v ranikust-state:/var/lib/ranikust' for overlay mode in a container (setup.rs:246-247, how-it-builds.md:64), and says a volume at /var/lib/ranikust works for kaniko mode on / (how-it-builds.md:140-141). Under --mode=auto, the same command with and without --privileged then shares one store. Relation to rnk-store/store.rs:published-entry-reuse-without-reverification: that candidate covers poisoned published blobs and layers that later builds reuse, and re-verifying them fixes it. This one covers access to other builds' unpublished, non-content-addressed state and the missing mutual exclusion, which re-verification does not close. Both need the same precondition, a Direct RUN on a persistent store, so refusing that also removes the sibling's main lower-trust writer. Variant at stage.rs:294-299: Overlay::base_layer reopens the published blob by path with File::open. That call follows symlinks and blocks on a FIFO. Store::get checked the entry's type through statx just before (store.rs:626-631, 1040-1059). Only a concurrent writer, the Direct RUN of this candidate, can swap the blob in that window. A planted FIFO then hangs the persistent build in open(2). Content poisoning is still stopped by the diff_id check, so the effect is availability. It belongs with the published-entry sibling, and its reachability depends on this candidate.
claimed_root_cause: Kaniko mode on / does not refuse a state directory that holds a persistent store. statedir::check_contents (crates/ranikust/src/statedir.rs:191-197) accepts .ranikust-state for every mode, and Store::open_anonymous (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:403-409) only warns. Separately, the state-directory flock that open_anonymous takes (store.rs:376) is not part of Store::open's protocol (store.rs:290-323): a persistent build neither takes a shared lock on it nor tests it. So a Direct RUN with no namespaces runs beside live persistent builds on one volume, with no isolation from their private builds/<id> and tmp/<id> directories.

trace.description: On / in a default container, each Dockerfile RUN runs as Isolation::Direct: the lower-trust command runs as root with Docker's default capabilities, with no namespace, on the container's /. Every path there, the state directory volume included, is in its reach.
A state directory holding a regular .ranikust-state, such as a persistent store on a shared volume, is accepted with no mode parameter. Kaniko mode on / goes through the same check (setup.rs:318).
On /, the accepted persistent store is opened with Store::open_anonymous. Nothing refuses a directory that holds another store's blobs, layers, tmp/ and builds/.
A non-empty state directory only logs 'a RUN can read what it holds' and the build continues. main.rs:522 later checks only is_anonymous().

The exclusive flock on the state directory excludes only other anonymous stores. Store::open (store.rs:290-323) neither takes nor tests it, so on a marked volume persistent builds start, and keep running, beside the anonymous build in either order.

Another build's upper and work directories, builds/<id>/stages/<n>/diff-<k> and work-<k> (made at stage.rs:325-330 and 488-489), are plain directories on the shared volume. The Direct RUN, root in its container, reads them (that build's COPY'd context and RUN output) and can alter or delete them while that build runs, together with tmp/<id> and builds/<id>.lock.

evidence.description: check_contents returns Ok(true) for a regular .ranikust-state marker (statedir.rs:191-197). prepare (statedir.rs:53-97) takes no mode, so kaniko mode on / inherits that acceptance.

Doc of open_anonymous: 'Anything else in the state directory is used as is, with a warning: a RUN can read what is there.' This acceptance exists only in code (added in 9e7001c without an ADR). No ADR or section-6 entry records it.

Store::open: create, canonicalize, check_marker, DIRS, warn_if_shared, register, cleanup. It takes no flock on the state directory itself; lock.rs:44-66 and lock_state_dir (store.rs:1238-1249) are used only by open_anonymous for the directory.

check_marker refuses a non-empty directory without .ranikust-state. An overlay build therefore cannot start on a volume an anonymous store took while it was empty; the concurrency gap needs a volume that already holds a persistent store.
Error::Busy is documented and produced only for the anonymous store's lock ('two containers sharing one volume'). Persistent and anonymous builds never get it from each other.
one_anonymous_store_at_a_time_per_state_directory covers two anonymous stores only. No test opens an anonymous store on a marked persistent store, or a persistent store beside an anonymous one.
'the store holds an exclusive flock on the state directory for its life, so a second build on it (another container on the same volume) is refused'. This holds only between two anonymous stores.
Overlay mode and kaniko mode on a host keep their persistent store because 'there RUN has its own namespaces'. Kaniko mode on / is meant to keep nothing a RUN can reach.
Each build gets a private builds/<build-id>/ directory for its context, upper directories and stage roots; shared content goes only through the store and its locks.

Other builds sharing the store may belong to another trust domain, and only content-addressed data is shared. Section 6 (threat-model.md:107-116) excuses only files mounted into the container that ranikust 'can only warn about'. Here ranikust can recognise the store and refuse it.

Overlay-mode guidance suggests '-v ranikust-state:/var/lib/ranikust'. how-it-builds.md:140-141 says a volume at /var/lib/ranikust also works for kaniko mode on /. One volume shared by privileged and default containers under --mode=auto is a plausible slip, and the one-per-container advice is not enforced across modes.

Variant: Overlay::base_layer reopens the published blob by host path with File::open, which follows symlinks and blocks on a FIFO, after Store::get's statx type check (store.rs:1040-1059). Only a concurrent writer, such as this candidate's Direct RUN, can swap it in that window. The effect is a hang or a misdirected open; diff_id verification still stops content poisoning. It belongs with the published-entry sibling.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run (no OS-enforced sandbox; the VM and T2c lanes have external network), so neither the concurrent start without Busy nor the cross-build read and write was observed.

Runtime fact: what a write into another build's mounted overlay upper directory, made from another container through the shared volume, does to that overlay and to the exporter. overlayfs leaves such a change undefined. Reading the directory and deleting entries are certain from source; whether a planted file reaches the victim's layer is not.

Deployment fact: whether operators mount one state volume, PVC or hostPath that holds a persistent store into both a default-capability kaniko-on-/ container and privileged or host builds of another trust domain. ranikust's docs advise one volume per container, and suggest the same volume name for both modes.

validation_plan.local: In the disposable VM (just test-vm, tier T2) or the marker-guarded T2c rootful-Docker lane (just test-container, ADR-0063). Use dummy images and contexts only, stop at the first observation, and remove the volume afterwards. (1) docker volume create rnkv. (2) Start an overlay build in a --privileged container with -v rnkv:/var/lib/ranikust, --mode=auto and a context holding secret.txt with a dummy string. Its Dockerfile is 'FROM busybox', 'COPY secret.txt /', 'RUN sleep 60'. This first build also writes .ranikust-state. (3) While it sleeps, start ranikust in a default rootful Docker container on the same volume, with no --privileged and --mode=auto. Its Dockerfile is 'FROM busybox' plus 'RUN ls /var/lib/ranikust/builds; find /var/lib/ranikust/builds -name secret.txt -exec cat {} +; touch /var/lib/ranikust/builds/*/stages/*/planted'. Expected today: the second build logs only the store.rs:406 warning and is not refused with Busy. Its RUN output prints the dummy string from the first build's diff directory, and a 'planted' file appears in the first build's stage directory. (4) Reverse order on the same, now marked, volume: start the default-container build with 'RUN sleep 60', then the privileged overlay build. Expected: Store::open succeeds while the anonymous LOCK_EX is held. (5) Control: on a fresh empty volume, start the default-container build first, then the privileged one. Expected: NotAStateDir from check_marker, which shows the gap needs an already-marked volume. T0 alternative for the lock gap alone, with no root needed: a test in crates/rnk-store/tests/store.rs. It runs Store::open then close() on a tempdir, so the dir is marked, then holds Store::open_anonymous on it, then asserts that Store::open on the same directory returns Error::Busy. It also asserts that open_anonymous on a marked directory is refused. Both assertions fail today.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: list the CI runner configs, docker-compose files and Kubernetes manifests that mount a ranikust state volume, PVC or hostPath (default path /var/lib/ranikust). Report any that mount it both into a workload without --privileged/CAP_SYS_ADMIN (kaniko mode on /) and into a privileged or host workload (overlay or per-stage), or into workloads of different tenants or projects. Also check the ranikust logs of such workloads for 'state directory ... is not empty: a RUN can read what it holds'.

title: Base image config is buffered in memory up to the size its manifest declares, with no cap
description: pull_image (crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:55) is called for every FROM base and every COPY --from image (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1093,1105). It parses the registry's manifest (pull.rs:75; ImageManifest::from_json at crates/rnk-oci/src/manifest.rs:68-77 checks only schema version and media type) and pulls manifest.config into a Vec<u8> (pull.rs:76-79). The only bound is Bounded at the descriptor's size (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:574), a u64 the manifest sets with no maximum (crates/rnk-oci/src/descriptor.rs:28). oci-client 0.18.0 (pinned at Cargo.lock:958-959; ~/.cargo/.../oci-client-0.18.0/src/client.rs:1370-1376) writes every chunk into the sink before it checks the digest at client.rs:1394, so the Vec grows (amortised doubling through tokio's AsyncWrite for Vec<u8>) to the declared size before any verification. A registry (tag reference) or the image publisher (digest-pinned reference) can therefore declare and serve a multi-GiB config, and ranikust holds it in RAM, before any RUN, in every mode, also in builds with no RUN. The project caps its sibling JSON inputs (manifest 4 MiB at client.rs:44, token body 1 MiB at token.rs:54, docker config.json 16 MiB at credentials.rs:35) but not the image config, and threat-model T15 asks to stream instead of buffering and fail cleanly on exhaustion. Growth is linear in bytes the attacker sends (no amplification; no transparent decompression), and the end is an allocation-failure abort (panic=abort, heuristic overcommit refusing a doubling) or an OOM kill, not a clean error. Calibration only: BuildKit (containerd content.ReadBlob, buildkit/vendor/github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/core/content/helpers.go:99-124, allocates ra.Size()) and kaniko share the pattern. Marginal reach: a hostile base image used by a build with RUN already runs code as that RUN, and a huge layer can already fill the store's disk; the distinct effect here is memory exhaustion of the builder host or pod from image data alone, ending uncleanly.
claimed_root_cause: No upper bound on the image config descriptor's size: pull_image passes manifest.config to Client::pull_blob with an in-memory Vec<u8> sink, and Bounded (crates/rnk-registry/src/io.rs:380-431) only enforces the declared size, which the registry or publisher chooses; nothing compares it with a cap before or during the download.

trace.description: The manifest of the Dockerfile-named image (FROM or COPY --from, build.rs:1093,1105) is pulled from a lower-trust registry; it carries the config descriptor (digest, size).
ImageManifest::from_json keeps manifest.config.size as given; no size check (manifest.rs:68-77).
client.pull_blob(&reference, &manifest.config, &mut config_bytes) with config_bytes a Vec<u8> created at line 76.
Bounded::new(&mut *out, blob.size): the limit is the attacker-declared size; oci-client 0.18.0 client.rs:1370-1376 then writes each response chunk before the digest check at 1394.
Each chunk under the declared size is forwarded to the Vec<u8> sink (BlobSink impl at io.rs:90), which grows in memory to the declared size before the digest is verified.

evidence.description: let mut config_bytes = Vec::new(); the config is held in memory, unlike layers, which stream to a store file or into the root.
Bounded refuses only bytes beyond its limit, which is the registry-declared size.
pub size: u64 with no maximum; manifest.rs:68-77 does not check it.
oci-client 0.18.0, whose pull_blob (src/client.rs:1344-1403) streams chunks into the sink and verifies the digest only at the end (1394).
Manifests get a 4 MiB cap; sibling caps exist for token bodies (token.rs:54, 1 MiB) and config.json (credentials.rs:35, 16 MiB); none for image configs.
T15 (A7): control 'Stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion'; section 6 (line 100 on) accepts no memory exhaustion from image data.
prepare_stage calls pull_image for the base and again at 1105 for each COPY --from image, before any RUN.

blockers: Execution of target code is not allowed in this run (no OS-enforced sandbox on the host; the VM and T2c lanes have network), so the in-memory growth is established from source only.
Whether exhausting the builder's memory affects anything beyond that build (shared impact) depends on the deployment's memory confinement and overcommit setting, which are outside the repository.

validation_plan.local: In the disposable VM (T2 lane; the test itself is unprivileged and uses only the loopback FakeRegistry and dummy data): add to crates/rnk-registry/tests/registry/main.rs a #[tokio::test] that starts FakeRegistry::start(Auth::Open), builds content = b"{}" followed by 256 MiB of b' ', registry.add_blob("app", &content), desc = descriptor(MediaType::OCI_CONFIG, &content), and calls client(&registry, Credentials::none()).pull_blob(&reference(&registry, "app"), &desc, &mut out) with out a Vec<u8>. Expected today: Ok(()) and out.capacity() >= 256 MiB (the sink holds the whole declared size before returning). Run it in the guest with `cargo test -p rnk-registry --test registry <name>`. After a fix (a config cap checked against desc.size before the request and enforced while streaming), the same call must fail with an error before out holds more than the cap. Optional end-to-end in the T2c lane with the ADR-0063 marker: a loopback registry:2 holding a dummy image whose manifest declares a 1 GiB config ('{}' plus spaces, correct digest), ranikust run in a container with --memory=512m on `FROM localhost:5000/big:1` + `COPY a /a` and --no-push; expect the container OOM-killed (docker inspect .State.OOMKilled=true, exit 137) and record peak RSS without --memory (/usr/bin/time -v) to see an allocation-failure abort or OOM kill rather than a clean error.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check per deployment: whether each ranikust process runs in its own memory cgroup (pod or container memory limit) that no other workload shares, and the node's vm.overcommit_memory; without a per-build limit, record whether a builder's memory spike can push the node into reclaim or OOM-kill or evict other workloads.

title: An anonymous realm token with a control character makes oci-client's apply_auth unwrap panic and abort ranikust, with no effect beyond a failed build
description: The source trace holds. For a Dockerfile-named registry with no credential (or one withheld), strategy() returns Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous) (client.rs:1342) and authorize() calls host.oci.auth (client.rs:1179). In oci-client 0.18.0 (Cargo.lock:959) auth() stores the anonymous authorization, _auth GETs the challenge realm, deserialises a 200 body {token} or {access_token} with no character check and caches it (oci-client src/client.rs:804-833, 903-911); a token that is not JWT-shaped gets the default lifetime (token_cache.rs:195-208), and an uncacheable JWT-shaped one is fetched again and still returned by get_auth_token (src/client.rs:446-452). auth() also returns the token string to ranikust, which only counts requests at client.rs:1181-1185 and drops it. pull_manifest_once then calls pull_manifest_raw (client.rs:441), whose _pull_manifest_raw runs apply_auth, where `token.bearer_token().parse().unwrap()` (oci-client src/client.rs:2432) panics when the token holds a byte below 0x20 other than tab, or 0x7f (http 1.5.0, Cargo.lock:532, src/header/value.rs:563-565). Release builds abort (Cargo.toml:138). Base pulls start for all stages up front (rnk-sched/src/lib.rs:4-5), so the realm can pick the moment by delaying its answer. Corrections to the candidate: ranikust does receive the token; the panic message still reaches stderr and the metrics report is still written, with exit status "panic", by the panic hook (rnk-metrics/src/lib.rs:256-268, tested by crates/ranikust/tests/metrics.rs:91); only the 'ranikust: error:' line and exit status 1 are replaced by the panic text and SIGABRT.
claimed_root_cause: The header-validity check on registry tokens (token.rs:138-144, is_ascii_graphic) runs only on tokens ranikust fetches itself (token::exchange, token::fetch). The token that oci-client fetches for Strategy::Oci (anonymous, or basic credentials against a Bearer challenge) at client.rs:1179 is cached by oci-client and reaches the unwrap in its apply_auth unchecked, although auth() hands the same string back to ranikust.

trace.description: The stage's base image named by the Dockerfile is pulled (COPY --from images at line 1105 take the same path); prepare jobs for all stages start up front.
client.pull_image_manifest for the Dockerfile's reference.
pull_manifest, then pull_manifest_once, which sets up the host and calls authorize (line 415).
A Bearer challenge with no credential gives Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous); the realm may name any host.
host.oci.auth fetches the realm; oci-client caches the token unchecked and returns it as Ok(Some(String)); ranikust ignores the value and records the scope as authorized.
pull_manifest_raw runs oci-client apply_auth, whose HeaderValue parse unwrap (src/client.rs:2432) panics on a control byte; with panic = "abort" the process gets SIGABRT.

evidence.description: The comment says oci-client unwraps the header it builds from the token and an invalid token would abort; the guard at line 140 covers only ranikust's own token fetches.
The Strategy::Oci path delegates the realm fetch to oci-client and drops the returned token string without checking it.
oci-client 0.18.0: apply_auth does token.bearer_token().parse().unwrap() at src/client.rs:2432; _auth caches the realm's 200 token at src/client.rs:903-911 and 814-818.
http 1.5.0: HeaderValue is_valid is b >= 32 && b != 127 || b == b'\t' (src/header/value.rs:563-565).
The release profile's comment: cleanup must not rely on unwinding because the build has to survive SIGKILL and OOM kills; panic = "abort" at line 138.
The panic hook prints the panic and writes the metrics report with status panic before the abort, so the outcome is not lost.
A build is alive while it holds the flock on builds/<id>.lock; Store::open removes builds/ and tmp/ of every build that is not (store.rs:973-977).
ranikust enters a private mount namespace (then / becomes a recursive slave), so build mounts vanish with the aborted process (T9).
Kaniko mode on /: a build killed mid-RUN while not PID 1 is detected by the building marker and later builds in that container keep no named state (ADR-0066).
T16 asks for no panics reachable from input and for cleanup that survives an abort (T8-T10); the latter is what bounds the effect here.

reason: Not a vulnerability: the panic is real in source, but its effect does not cross a trust boundary beyond what the same principals can already do. (1) The registry or realm that sends the token can already end the same build at the same point with a clean error (any non-200 realm, manifest or blob answer), so the abort removes no availability it lacked; the operator still sees the panic text and the metrics outcome "panic". (2) An abort leaves only what SIGKILL, an OOM kill or a CI cancel leaves, which the design requires recovering from (Cargo.toml:132-137) and implements: build mounts live in ranikust's private mount namespace (setup.rs:35, T9); RUN children get PR_SET_PDEATHSIG and are PID 1 of their own PID namespace (T8); stubs are journaled and cleaned at the next start (T10); store entries are published by atomic rename under per-digest locks (T13); a dead build's builds/<id> and tmp/<id> are removed by the next Store::open once its flock is gone (rnk-store/src/lib.rs:20-22, store.rs:973-977), while concurrent builds keep their own locked directories.
