(3) In kaniko mode on /, emptying / is ranikust's own planned step, so an abort can only delete less than planned; a Direct RUN (root in the same PID namespace) can already SIGKILL ranikust; RUN processes left when ranikust is not PID 1 are handled by the cut-short marker (store.rs:377-402, ADR-0066), and that container is the accepted boundary (threat-model section 6). Nobody other than the operator whose build fails is affected, and not beyond a failed build. A gap in crash recovery would be a separate root cause in the sandbox and store units. Residual: this contradicts the intent at token.rs:138-139 and T16's 'no panics reachable from input', so it deserves a robustness fix outside the vulnerability list: check the string host.oci.auth returns (client.rs:1179) with the same is_ascii_graphic rule and return Error::Auth before any oci-client request uses its cache, or fetch anonymous tokens through token.rs, plus a fake.rs test whose realm returns a token holding a newline.

title: Under --network=none, a registry named by the Dockerfile can make ranikust GET any internal http(s) URL as its anonymous token realm from the host network namespace; the build may then reveal a token-shaped 200 body or a 200-character excerpt of an error body
description: Scope after verification: this matters only for a Full-sandbox build (overlay mode, or kaniko mode with per-stage directories) run with --network=none. With the default host network, ADR-0010 (lines 28-29) has RUN reach whatever ranikust itself can reach, and threat-model section 6 (lines 140-149) accepts RUN reaching host services and the metadata service. A RUN can already send any method and headers there, read full bodies and exfiltrate them, so the realm path adds nothing in that case. Kaniko mode on a container's / refuses --network=none (cli.rs:376-378, ADR-0057), so RUN always shares ranikust's network there. Under --network=none, only the RUN child gets a new network namespace: CLONE_NEWNET in its clone flags (spawner.rs:1132-1134), or, where that needs a user namespace, a helper-made namespace the child joins with setns (spawner.rs:1020-1029, child.rs:360-366). ranikust itself stays in the host namespace (setup.rs:35 unshares only NEWNS), and the Dockerfile author still chooses which registry it contacts (FROM, COPY --from: build.rs:1093,1105; no allowlist). The attack: that registry answers ranikust's GET /v2/ with 401 Bearer and a realm such as http://10.0.0.5:8080/any/path?q. The operator has no credential for that host, so strategy() returns Strategy::Oci(Anonymous) without examining the realm. The only realm rule (client.rs:1332) requires a credential, and the unit test at client.rs:1657 pins this. authorize() (client.rs:1179) calls oci-client 0.18.0 auth(). Its _auth re-pings /v2/ and GETs challenge.realm verbatim, appending scope and service (oci-client src/client.rs:883-901). It follows reqwest 0.13.5's default redirects (Policy::limited(10), src/redirect.rs:160-164; https_only false), because neither client sets a policy (client.rs:997, 1067). Two read-backs follow. (1) A 200 JSON body with a top-level lowercase `token` or `access_token` (untagged serde enum, token_cache.rs:13-28) is cached and sent as Authorization: Bearer on the next manifest or blob request to the attacker's registry (client.rs:441, 575). (2) A non-200 body becomes AuthenticationFailure, then Error::Auth with excerpt(&reason) (error.rs:155-159; 200 characters, control characters blanked), printed by report() (main.rs:166,180) and put in the metrics outcome (main.rs:169). A 200 that is not token-shaped reflects nothing: the decode error carries serde's message, not the body (oci-client client.rs:907-908). Example: AWS IMDSv1 credential JSON uses `Token`, so it is not echoed. Without a 30x or a realm, FROM with a non-loopback host sends only GET /v2/ over HTTPS (client.rs:1035-1063). A 30x on a manifest GET reaches channel (2) through ServerError (error.rs:164-165), but a 200 manifest body is not echoed (raw_manifest, client.rs:1430-1462). No threat-model row, ADR or crate-card invariant covers ranikust's own fetches of URLs a registry chooses under --network=none. Section 3 (threat-model.md:43-45) calls registry responses hostile to ranikust's own code. Calibration only: BuildKit's vendored containerd also GETs the realm verbatim (core/remotes/docker/auth/fetch.go:168-212) and uses the anonymous token as Bearer, but ErrUnexpectedStatus.Error() leaves out the body (core/remotes/errors/errors.go:42-44), so the error-body excerpt is specific to ranikust. Net effect: a header-less GET with a chosen scheme, host, port, path and query, from ranikust's own namespace, with a small read-back. Impact needs a target that answers in one of these two shapes, and channel (2) also needs the Dockerfile author to read ranikust's stderr or metrics. The candidate itself notes that the main metadata credential endpoints appear to answer in neither shape.
claimed_root_cause: No destination policy applies to URLs a registry chooses (the Bearer realm and 30x Location targets) for anonymous access. strategy() checks the realm only when credential.is_some() (client.rs:1332), and neither reqwest client sets a redirect policy or https_only (client.rs:997-1018; the ClientConfig at 1067-1081 has no redirect field). ranikust's own requests leave from the host network namespace even when --network=none takes RUN off the network. Fetched bytes come back as a forwarded Bearer token or as an error excerpt.

trace.description: The base named by the Dockerfile's FROM is pulled by its reference (and each COPY --from image at line 1105), with no registry allowlist; the Dockerfile author is a lower-trust principal.
client.pull_image_manifest(&reference, platform) is called for the Dockerfile-named host.
The registry's 401 WWW-Authenticate becomes Ping::Bearer(Challenge); the realm is an unchecked string.
The non-https realm refusal runs only if credential.is_some(); without a credential no scheme, host or address-class check applies.
None => Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous).

host.oci.auth(oci_ref, auth, op): oci-client 0.18.0 _auth (src/client.rs:836-917) re-pings /v2/ and GETs challenge.realm verbatim with scope and service added, from ranikust's (host) network namespace, following reqwest's default 10 redirects.
Non-200 realm answer: AuthenticationFailure(body) becomes Error::Auth { reason: excerpt(&reason) }, up to 200 characters of the internal response.
The failure message is written to stderr as 'ranikust: error: ...' (called at line 166); line 169 also puts it in the metrics outcome.

200 realm answer: pull_manifest_raw runs with the token oci-client cached from the internal response (src/client.rs:813-818), sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <value>' on the manifest GET to the attacker's registry.

evidence.description: if credential.is_some() && scheme == "https" && !challenge.realm.starts_with("https://"): the only realm check, which needs a credential.
The unit test credentials_never_go_to_a_plain_http_realm asserts that realm http://auth.example/token on an https registry without a credential gives Ok(Strategy::Oci(RegistryAuth::Anonymous)).
reqwest::Client::builder() has no .redirect(...) or .https_only(...); reqwest 0.13.5 defaults to Policy::limited(10) (src/redirect.rs:160-164).
The oci-client ClientConfig has no redirect setting; oci-client 0.18.0 TryFrom<ClientConfig> (src/client.rs:331-389) builds reqwest with the default redirect policy.

Pins oci-client 0.18.0 (reqwest 0.13.5 at Cargo.lock:1192). Its _auth GETs challenge.realm verbatim (src/client.rs:895-901). It decodes a 200 body only as top-level token or access_token (token_cache.rs:13-28); otherwise the decode error carries serde's message, not the body (src/client.rs:907-908). A non-200 body becomes AuthenticationFailure (913-915).
reason: excerpt(&reason): the realm's non-200 body (200 characters, control characters blanked, error.rs:229-242) goes into the user-visible Error::Auth.
The same excerpt of a ServerError body: the channel a plain FROM reaches when its registry answers a manifest GET with a 30x to an internal non-2xx URL.
Outcome::error(..., &failure.message): the excerpt also lands in the metrics report.
ranikust's own process unshares only NEWNS, so its registry traffic stays in the host (or container) network namespace.
CLONE_NEWNET is added only to RUN's clone flags when spec.network == Network::None.
--network is 'Network of RUN', and 'none' is refused in kaniko mode on a container's / (lines 377-378). There RUN always shares ranikust's network, so the candidate adds nothing in that mode.
Default: RUN 'reaches what ranikust itself can reach'. Under the default network, RUN reaches every realm or redirect target with any method and headers and full bodies, which dominates this path.

Accepted risk: RUN shares the host network and can reach host services and the metadata service. This acceptance covers the default-network case. Line 149 names --network=none as the mitigation, and nothing there covers ranikust's own fetches of registry-chosen URLs under --network=none.
Registry responses are 'Hostile'; line 43 has ranikust's own code treat Dockerfile-derived input as hostile. The realm is a hostile registry response that ranikust's own code acts on.
raw_manifest: a 200 body from a redirect target on a plain FROM is not echoed (only a parse error kind or a mediaType excerpt), so reflecting a 200 body is unique to the realm token.

blockers: No target-controlled execution in this run (no OS-enforced sandbox on the host; the VM and T2c lanes have external network). The anonymous realm fetch in oci-client 0.18.0, its redirect following and its token forwarding are traced from source (oci-client src/client.rs:836-917, 2408-2449; reqwest 0.13.5 src/redirect.rs:160-164) but not observed.

The finding is live only for Full-sandbox builds run with --network=none. With the default host network, which kaniko mode on / always uses, the accepted RUN reach (ADR-0010, threat-model.md:140-149) already covers the same targets with full bodies. Whether deployments build untrusted Dockerfiles with --network=none is an owner fact.

Impact needs a deployment fact outside the repository: a service reachable from ranikust's namespace that answers an unauthenticated, header-less GET either with 200 JSON holding a top-level lowercase token or access_token, or with sensitive data in the first 200 characters of a non-2xx body. AWS IMDSv1 credentials use 'Token', which is case-sensitive, so they do not match and the decode error does not echo the body. GCE and Azure IMDS need a Metadata-Flavor or Metadata request header that oci-client does not send. This is provider behaviour, not observed here.
Channel (2) needs the Dockerfile author to be able to read ranikust's stderr or metrics report, which is a deployment fact; the token channel (1) does not.

validation_plan.local: In the disposable VM (just test-vm), loopback only, with dummy data. title: No read timeout or deadline on registry blob pulls: a stalling Dockerfile-named registry holds the shared store's per-digest lock and blocks other builds
description: Registry requests have no idle or overall deadline. ClientOptions::default sets read_timeout None (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:105); client_options starts from it and never sets a timeout (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:651-670); Client::connect applies a read timeout only when one is set (client.rs:1013-1015) and passes the same None to oci-client (client.rs:1078); pull_blob_once has no tokio::time::timeout around host.oci.pull_blob (client.rs:575) and retries only after an error, which a stall never produces; reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:1191) defaults timeout and read_timeout to None (reqwest-0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:314-315), and its TCP keepalive (15 s) and TCP_USER_TIMEOUT (30 s) do not end a peer that ACKs but sends nothing. The project's own test relies on this: with ClientOptions::default (crates/rnk-builder/tests/outputs/support.rs:198) a registry that never answers makes an upload 'run forever' (crates/rnk-builder/tests/outputs/main.rs:205; crates/rnk-registry/tests/registry/fake.rs:234, included there through #[path]). In overlay mode every base layer goes through the store, since the Overlay snapshotter keeps the default streamed_layer None (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:187); in kaniko mode off '/' only when a Docker tar or OCI layout output needs blob files (crates/rnk-builder/src/output.rs:109-111). pull_blob returns early only when the blob is already published (crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:195); otherwise the download runs inside Store::fill (pull.rs:206-214), which takes the cross-process per-digest flock (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:665) and keeps it while the fill closure runs (store.rs:675). A registry named by build A's Dockerfile can serve a manifest that lists, as a layer, the digest D of a popular base layer not yet published in the state directory, then stall the blob GET before or after the headers. Build A then holds lock(D), and build B on the same state directory that needs D blocks in a blocking flock (store.rs:1030; crates/rnk-store/src/lock.rs:119-126) with no bound. Concurrent builds share one store by decision and by default (ADR-0007 line 27; default --state-dir /var/lib/ranikust, crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:138), and threat-model section 3 says they may belong to another trust domain; no accepted risk in section 6 or any ADR covers a stalled holder, and section 8 rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings Medium. A first SIGINT or SIGTERM to A does not end the stall: await_pulls waits for the pull even after cancel (build.rs:1118-1133) and cancel_on_signals exits only on a second signal (build.rs:992-1013), so the lock is released only when the registry ends the stall or A's process exits (second signal, SIGKILL, job timeout). The window closes once any build publishes D, so the effect is a repeatable, bounded denial of service against other builds, not persistence. Not affected: kaniko mode on '/' (anonymous store, one build per state directory, store.rs:376; fill_anonymous locks in-process only, store.rs:715). A read timeout alone would not close it: a registry dripping one byte per interval against a large manifest-declared size keeps the lock; the fix needs an overall transfer deadline or minimum rate, or downloading outside the cross-process lock (lock only to publish), or a bounded lock wait after which the waiter downloads itself. The hunter's within-build point (Client::host keeps the hosts mutex across connect, client.rs:982-990) stalls only the Dockerfile author's own build, crosses no boundary, and is not part of this finding. Calibration: kaniko has no store shared between builds, so it does not share the cross-build lock pattern.
claimed_root_cause: No read timeout or overall deadline on registry requests (crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs:89,105,1013-1015,1078; crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:651; reqwest 0.13.5 defaults None), combined with Store::fill holding the cross-process per-digest flock across an unbounded transfer from an untrusted registry (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:665,675; crates/rnk-builder/src/pull.rs:206-214) and Store::lock waiting for that flock without a bound (store.rs:1019-1033; lock.rs:119-126).

trace.description: Build A's Dockerfile FROM names a hostile registry; its manifest, listing as a layer the digest D that build B also needs, is fetched here.

Layers are not streamed: the Overlay snapshotter returns None from streamed_layer (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:187), and kaniko mode sets keep_blobs for tar or OCI-layout outputs; each layer goes to pull_blob (line 104).
D is not yet published (store.get at line 195), so the download runs inside store.fill(EntryKey::Blob(D), ...) on a spawn_blocking thread.
The per-digest flock for D is taken before the fill closure runs (line 675) and held until it returns.
client.pull_blob runs under handle.block_on inside the fill closure, so the lock is held for the whole network transfer.
host.oci.pull_blob streams the body with no deadline; the retry loop acts only on an error, which a stall never produces.
read_timeout is applied only when set; ClientOptions::default (line 105) and client_options (build.rs:651) leave it None, so neither reqwest nor oci-client (line 1078) bounds the stalled request.
Build B, another process on the same state directory needing D, blocks in lock::lock (blocking flock, EINTR retried) until A's request ends or A's process exits.

evidence.description: ClientOptions::default sets read_timeout: None (connect_timeout is 30 s, line 104).
client_options starts from ClientOptions::default and sets no read timeout before returning (lines 651-670).
reqwest 0.13.5; its ClientBuilder defaults read_timeout and timeout to None (reqwest-0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs:314-315), tcp_keepalive 15 s and tcp_user_timeout 30 s only (lines 304-308).
Default streamed_layer returns None and the Overlay impl (line 290) does not override it: overlay mode always pulls base layers through Store::fill.
needs_blob_files (Docker tar or OCI layout) is passed as keep_blobs (build.rs:1099), which sends kaniko mode off '/' through Store::fill too.
lock() loops on blocking flock(LOCK_EX), retrying EINTR, with no timeout.

The project's test states that with ClientOptions::default (crates/rnk-builder/tests/outputs/support.rs:198) a registry that never answers makes an upload 'run forever' (crates/rnk-registry/tests/registry/fake.rs:234, included through #[path], stalls with future::pending).
await_pulls waits for a pull to end even once cancel fires; cancel_on_signals exits only on a second signal (line 1011), so one SIGTERM does not release A's lock.
Default --state-dir /var/lib/ranikust, shared by every build on the host that does not name another.
Accepted decision: concurrent builds on one machine share one store, coordinated by per-digest locks.
Other builds sharing the store may belong to another trust domain.
Rating: denial of service from untrusted input with default settings is Medium; section 6 accepts no stalled-lock risk.
Design assumption: 'A build that waited finds the entry published and uses it.'
Kaniko mode on '/' uses an anonymous store with one build per state directory, so the cross-build effect does not apply there.

blockers: Runtime behaviour is unobserved (no target execution allowed in this run): that Client::pull_blob through oci-client 0.18.0, reqwest 0.13.5 and hyper 1.12.0 with read_timeout None never returns while a registry keeps the TCP connection open and stalls before or after the response headers, and that a second ranikust process on the same state directory stays blocked on the per-digest flock for that whole time and proceeds once build A exits.

Deployment facts that set exposure and duration, not whether the defect exists (the threat model already treats builds sharing a store as possibly another trust domain): whether operators run concurrent builds of different trust domains on one state directory (the default /var/lib/ranikust or a shared volume), and which job timeout and kill grace bound a build stalled in a pull, given that a single SIGTERM does not end it.

validation_plan.local: Run in the disposable VM (just test-vm, T2) or the T2c lane, loopback only, dummy data, each step under timeout 120 and in a fresh temporary state directory. Step 1 (T0 inside the VM): add a fake-registry mode to crates/rnk-registry/tests/registry/fake.rs that answers GET /v2/<repo>/blobs/<D> with 200, Content-Length 1048576, one 1 KiB chunk and then a body stream whose next frame stays pending (socket kept open); build a Client from ClientOptions::default with insecure = {fake host}; run client.pull_blob(ref, Descriptor{digest: D, size: 1048576}, &mut Vec) under tokio::time::timeout(20 s) and expect Elapsed; repeat with the existing pre-header stall (state.stalled). Step 2 (T0 inside the VM): run the stalling fake from step 1 on its own tokio runtime (FakeRegistry::start returns no task handle and serves each connection in a separately spawned task, fake.rs:97-113, so aborting its accept loop would not close the stalled connection); open two Store instances on the same state directory (separate opens, so their flocks conflict); thread 1 runs store_a.fill(EntryKey::Blob(D), |tmp| ...) whose closure block_ons stalling_client.pull_blob(...) into the temporary file on a second runtime; after 500 ms thread 2 runs store_b.fill(EntryKey::Blob(D), ...) whose closure pulls D from a second fake that serves D's real bytes; assert after 20 s that thread 2 has not returned and that a non-blocking exclusive flock (rustix NonBlockingLockExclusive on a new descriptor; lock::try_lock is crate-private) of <state>/locks/blobs/sha256/<hex of D> fails with EWOULDBLOCK; then end the stall by shutting down the stalling fake's runtime (shutdown_background drops its listener and connection tasks, so the client's retries are refused within seconds under the default RetryPolicy of 3 attempts, 1 s then 3 s); assert thread 1 returns Error::Fill and thread 2 publishes D (store_b.get(&EntryKey::Blob(D)) is Some). Step 3 (T2 end to end, overlay mode as root in the VM): start two fakes on 127.0.0.1:5001 (stalling: manifest with one layer of digest D, any config with one diff_id, blob GET for D stalls) and 127.0.0.1:5002 (serves a real image whose single layer is D); start ranikust build A (FROM 127.0.0.1:5001/evil:1) and wait until 5001 logs GET /blobs/D; start build B (FROM 127.0.0.1:5002/base:1) with the same --state-dir; after 60 s assert B is still running and 5002 has logged its manifest and config but no GET /blobs/D; send one SIGTERM to A and assert A still runs 10 s later; SIGKILL A and assert B completes within 30 s. Clean up: kill both fakes, remove the state directory.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check: whether CI runners or shared hosts run concurrent ranikust builds of different projects or tenants with the default /var/lib/ranikust or one shared --state-dir volume, and what per-job timeout plus kill grace (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL) ends a build stalled in a registry pull; and whether user documentation tells operators to give each trust domain its own store (today said only for cache mounts, threat model T14).

title: A credential for a dot-less, port-less registry spelled with an uppercase letter is sent to Docker Hub because oci-client re-parses the reference as docker.io
description: rnk_oci::Reference::parse treats a first path component that contains an uppercase letter, but no '.' or ':', as the registry (crates/rnk-oci/src/reference.rs:202; test at :548 'LOCALDOMAIN/fooo' -> registry LOCALDOMAIN), as distribution's normalize.go does. rnk-registry uses that registry name to pick the connection, to ping it, to check the realm, and to look up credentials (Client::host and Client::connect, client.rs:413, 982-1132). It then gives oci-client a reference converted through its string form (oci_reference, client.rs:1411, ADR-0026). oci-client 0.18.0 parses with oci-spec 0.10.0, whose split_domain (oci-spec-0.10.0/src/distribution/reference.rs:349) counts a first component as a domain only if it contains '.' or ':' or equals 'localhost' (case-sensitive). Its regex accepts an uppercase domain component, so 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian:latest' becomes registry docker.io, repository 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian', and resolve_registry() becomes index.docker.io (reference.rs:180). credentials.rs:245 lowercases the lookup key, so the operator's credential for 'localdomain' is selected. The credential is not withheld: the private host was reached over verified TLS. Client::authorize (client.rs:1179) then calls host.oci.auth(oci_ref, ...), which acts on index.docker.io, not on LOCALDOMAIN. (a) Basic credential: auth() stores it for index.docker.io (oci-client client.rs:810), and _auth GETs https://index.docker.io/v2/ (client.rs:844). It then GETs the realm from Docker Hub's own challenge with apply_authentication(Basic(user, password)) (client.rs:899). The username and password therefore go to Docker Hub's token service; ranikust's HTTPS-realm rule (client.rs:1332) only judged LOCALDOMAIN's challenge. (b) registrytoken: _auth returns the static bearer without a request. The token is cached under (index.docker.io, 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian'), and pull_manifest_raw (client.rs:441) sends it to index.docker.io. (c) identitytoken: the refresh token goes only to LOCALDOMAIN's checked realm. The access token minted there is inserted under the docker.io key (client.rs:1210) and sent as a Bearer token to index.docker.io by client.rs:441. That works because pull_manifest_raw stores an Anonymous auth for index.docker.io, so get_auth_token finds the cached token. The blob pull (client.rs:544) and the push paths (client.rs:637, 695, 707, 916) share the re-parse; push destinations and cache repositories are typed by the trusted operator. The 'LOCALHOST/app' spelling is a variant: rnk_oci makes 'LOCALHOST' the registry, oci-spec makes it Docker Hub, and a port-less 'localhost' credential is selected. Because rnk_oci sends a lowercase single-label component other than 'localhost' to Docker Hub, the uppercase spelling is the only way to address a single-label, port-less private registry other than 'localhost'. Legitimate use of such a registry therefore leaks too, not only a hostile Dockerfile. Conditions: the operator has a credential for a single-label, port-less host (for example an in-cluster 'registry' service on 443, or 'localdomain'). That host answers /v2/ over verified HTTPS with a Basic or Bearer challenge; an open registry gets Strategy::None, so nothing is sent. Egress to index.docker.io and auth.docker.io must be possible. The trust store always includes the webpki roots (tls.rs:46), so Docker Hub's TLS verifies. Under these conditions the recipient is Docker Hub over verified TLS, never a host the Dockerfile author chooses, and the author does not receive the credential. (Variant: with --skip-tls-verify-pull or --skip-tls-verify-registry naming the spelled registry, and outside the verified-credentials-only setting, withheld_because still lets the credential go (client.rs:301-320), and oci-client's accept_invalid_certificates (client.rs:1073) then also covers index.docker.io and the realm in its challenge, so whoever answers those names on the path receives it; this sits next to the skip-verify risk that threat-model section 6 accepts for the registry itself.) Impact: a protected asset (A3, an operator registry credential or token) is disclosed to a third party outside its audience. The diverted pull then probably fails, and gives no image substitution beyond what the author could already name with FROM. Likely low severity.
claimed_root_cause: rnk-registry assumes that oci_reference(reference.to_string() / reference.name()) yields an oci_client::Reference whose resolve_registry() is the registry it connected to, checked the realm of, and selected credentials for. rnk_oci (distribution v0.6.0 rules) and oci-spec 0.10.0 split_domain disagree on whether an uppercase, dot-less, port-less first component is a registry. Nothing compares the converted reference's resolve_registry() with Host.name or its endpoint (client.rs:1021) before credentials or tokens reach oci-client's auth store and token cache.

trace.description: Reference::parse receives the FROM (or COPY --from image) string written by the Dockerfile author, for example 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian'. prepare_stage passes it (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1093, 1105), and with_default_tag adds ':latest'.
A first component with an uppercase ASCII letter is taken as the registry: registry 'LOCALDOMAIN', repository 'debian'. Display (reference.rs:164-175) yields 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian:latest'.
self.host(reference.registry()) creates the Host for 'LOCALDOMAIN'. connect() pings https://LOCALDOMAIN/v2/ with ranikust's own reqwest client and parses that challenge.

self.credentials.get("LOCALDOMAIN") lowercases the key through canonical_host (credentials.rs:245), so an operator credential for 'localdomain' is selected. It is not withheld because the transport is verified TLS (withheld_because, client.rs:301-320).
The HTTPS-realm rule judges LOCALDOMAIN's challenge only. Strategy::Oci(Basic or Bearer), or Strategy::Identity, is built for that Host.

oci_reference(&reference.to_string()) re-parses 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian:latest' with oci-spec 0.10.0: registry docker.io, repository 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian', resolve_registry() index.docker.io. No check compares it with Host.name.

host.oci.auth(oci_ref, auth, op) stores the LOCALDOMAIN credential for index.docker.io. With Basic it GETs https://index.docker.io/v2/, then sends Basic(user, password) to the realm in Docker Hub's challenge (oci-client 0.18.0 client.rs:810, 844, 899). A static registrytoken is cached under the docker.io key.

Identity strategy: the access token that LOCALDOMAIN's checked realm minted is inserted into oci-client's token cache under oci_ref, which is keyed (index.docker.io, 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian') per oci-client token_cache.rs:128-129.

pull_manifest_raw(&oci_ref, Anonymous, ...) stores an Anonymous auth for index.docker.io. apply_auth then finds the cached registrytoken or identity access token and sends it as 'Authorization: Bearer' to https://index.docker.io/v2/LOCALDOMAIN/debian/manifests/latest.

evidence.description: Test asserts that 'LOCALDOMAIN/fooo' parses to registry 'LOCALDOMAIN', repository 'fooo' in rnk_oci. validate_names (reference.rs:478-479) also accepts 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian'.

oci_reference() converts with text.parse() into oci_client::Reference (oci_spec::distribution::Reference, re-exported in oci-client lib.rs:19). It does not check that the parsed registry equals the Host's registry or endpoint.

Cargo.lock pins oci-spec 0.10.0. In its source, oci-spec-0.10.0/src/distribution/reference.rs:349, split_domain counts a first component as a domain only if it contains '.' or ':' or equals 'localhost' (case-sensitive). REFERENCE_REGEXP (line 18, no case-insensitive flag) accepts an uppercase domain component, so 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian' becomes docker.io/LOCALDOMAIN/debian. resolve_registry maps docker.io to index.docker.io (line 180).

This call site hands the ranikust-selected credential to oci-client 0.18.0 Client::auth. In the locked oci-client source, auth() first stores that credential for resolve_registry() (oci-client-0.18.0/src/client.rs:810). _auth then GETs <scheme>://<resolve_registry>/v2/ (client.rs:844), parses the Bearer challenge itself, and GETs its realm with apply_authentication(authentication) (client.rs:899). get_auth_token (client.rs:445) and token_cache.rs:128 also key on resolve_registry().
oci-spec 0.10.0 is the locked version: the parser oci-client uses.
oci-client 0.18.0 is the locked version whose auth/_auth/pull_manifest_raw source was reviewed.
canonical_host lowercases the registry name, so 'LOCALDOMAIN' (or 'LOCALHOST') selects an operator credential stored for 'localdomain' (or 'localhost').
The Host endpoint is the registry name itself except for docker.io. Nothing maps it to or compares it with oci_ref.resolve_registry().
The trust store always adds the embedded webpki roots, so oci-client's TLS to index.docker.io and auth.docker.io verifies. TLS failure does not stop the disclosure.

The only realm test exercises strategy() on a hand-built challenge. No test checks that the host oci-client addresses matches the host whose challenge and credential were checked. ADR-0026 and threat-model section 6 do not accept this divergence.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run (no cargo test, no ranikust binary). The oci-spec parse result, and the host that receives the credential-bearing requests, come from reading the locked dependency source, not from observation.

End-to-end observation needs index.docker.io and auth.docker.io answered by a local fake, through a hosts override and a throwaway test CA, in the isolated VM. No network or VM is permitted in this run.

Deployment facts outside the repository set the real-world reach: whether operators keep credentials for single-label, port-less registry hosts; whether build hosts can reach Docker Hub; and how Docker Hub answers an uppercase repository scope. The disclosure precedes that answer.

validation_plan.local:
T0, no network, maintainer machine: add a unit test to the tests module of crates/rnk-registry/src/client.rs. For each of 'LOCALDOMAIN/debian:1', 'LOCALHOST/app:1' and 'Registry/team/app:1', it parses rnk_oci::Reference and converts it with both oci_reference(&r.to_string()) and oci_reference(&r.name()). Name it oci_reference_keeps_the_registry. It asserts that oci_ref.resolve_registry() equals, case-insensitively, the endpoint connect() derives for r.registry() at client.rs:1021 ('index.docker.io' for docker.io, else the registry name). Run `cargo test -p rnk-registry oci_reference_keeps_the_registry`. Expected under the claim: the assertion fails, with resolve_registry() == 'index.docker.io' and registry() == 'docker.io'. T2 in the disposable VM only (`just test-vm`, dummy data, no real credentials):
1. Generate a throwaway CA and point SSL_CERT_FILE at it.
2. Start a minimal TLS listener for 'localdomain' on 127.0.0.2:443 (VM /etc/hosts), with a certificate from that CA. It answers /v2/ with 401 'WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="https://localdomain/token",service="x"'. Do not use the rnk-registry FakeRegistry (crates/rnk-registry/tests/registry/fake.rs) unchanged: it serves plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1 with a random port, and its Bearer realm is http://, which strategy() (client.rs:1332) refuses to send a credential to.
3. Start a second logging TLS listener for index.docker.io and auth.docker.io (VM /etc/hosts 127.0.0.3). Its certificate is signed by the same CA. It answers /v2/ with 401 'Bearer realm="https://auth.docker.io/token",service="registry.docker.io"' and logs every Authorization header.
4. Set DOCKER_AUTH_CONFIG='{"auths":{"localdomain":{"auth":"ZHVtbXk6ZHVtbXk="}}}'.
5. Run `ranikust build` on a Dockerfile containing only 'FROM LOCALDOMAIN/debian' with --no-push.
Expected under the claim: the second listener logs 'Authorization: Basic ZHVtbXk6ZHVtbXk=' on GET /token with the URL-encoded query scope=repository%3ALOCALDOMAIN%2Fdebian%3Apull&service=registry.docker.io. Repeat with {"registrytoken":"dummy-token"} and expect 'Authorization: Bearer dummy-token' on GET /v2/LOCALDOMAIN/debian/manifests/latest. Fix to validate: in Client::pull_manifest_once, pull_blob_once, the push paths and the mount source, compare oci_ref.resolve_registry() with the Host endpoint (case-insensitively). Fail with Error::Reference before authorize() on a mismatch. Alternatively, build oci_client::Reference from parts (Reference::with_tag / with_digest(registry, repository, ...)) instead of re-parsing text, and lowercase the registry for DNS and TLS. Add the T0 test above as a regression test.

Also list whether any Dockerfile, --destination or --cache-repo in use spells such a registry with an uppercase letter, and whether those builds pass --skip-tls-verify-pull or --skip-tls-verify-registry for it. For any such registry, rotate its credential if the build host could reach index.docker.io or auth.docker.io.

title: Registry manifest, token-service and error bodies are buffered whole by oci-client before ranikust's 4 MiB / 1 MiB caps apply
description: A registry that serves a reference named by the Dockerfile (FROM, COPY --from) is lower-trust (threat-model.md:45, 'Registry responses: Hostile: verified by digest'). ranikust delegates the manifest GET to oci-client 0.18.0 (client.rs:439-443). oci-client _pull_manifest_raw reads the whole response with reqwest Response::bytes() (oci-client src/client.rs:1176), which in reqwest 0.13.5 is an unbounded http_body_util collect (src/async_impl/response.rs:290,433). Only afterwards does it check the status (1178) and the digest (1181). raw_manifest then applies MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES to the body that is already in memory (client.rs:1431). The same unbounded read happens to oci-client's token-service answer on the Strategy::Oci path: anonymous or basic-credential Bearer registries reach it through host.oci.auth (client.rs:1179), and _auth reads the realm's 200 or error body with Response::text() (oci-client 905,913). It also happens to non-2xx bodies of blob requests: ranikust's pull_blob_once calls oci-client pull_blob (client.rs:575), which reads an error body with Response::bytes() (oci-client 1363). ranikust's own token reads stop at 1 MiB while streaming (token.rs:124-130), but these paths have no such bound. ranikust sets no total request timeout, and read_timeout defaults to None (client.rs:105,1013; crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:651-669). A registry can therefore stream an arbitrarily large body and grow ranikust's heap about 1-2x the bytes sent until the response ends or the process is OOM-killed. This holds even for a digest-pinned reference, because the digest is checked after buffering. Calibration: for a tag reference the registry already controls the base image that RUN executes, and ranikust gives RUN no memory cgroup, so the added capability is mainly for digest-pinned references and RUN-less builds. There the registry could otherwise only refuse or stall. The cost to the attacker is linear in bytes sent, with no amplification. The effect is transient: memory is released when the process exits, and flock-based store locks are released with it. Threat-model T15 lists 'Stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion' as its control (threat-model.md:92). Section 8 rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings as Medium (threat-model.md:202). Section 6 and the ADRs do not accept it. The crate card records it only as a known pitfall (docs/agents/crates/rnk-registry.md:167-169). Whether the exhaustion reaches beyond the build depends on the deployment's memory cgroup.
claimed_root_cause: rnk-registry hands manifest, token-service and error-body reads to oci-client 0.18.0, which collects whole responses with reqwest Response::bytes()/text(). No Content-Length pre-check, limited body or chunked read wraps those calls. MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES (client.rs:44, checked at client.rs:1431) and the error excerpt in error.rs bound only what is parsed or reported, after the body is fully buffered.

trace.description: A FROM or COPY --from reference from the Dockerfile (crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:1093,1105 via prepare_stage) is pulled with client.pull_image_manifest. The hostile bytes come from the registry that serves this reference.

Strategy::Oci (anonymous or basic credential on a Bearer registry, client.rs:1342-1345) calls host.oci.auth. oci-client _auth GETs the registry-named realm and reads its answer with Response::text() with no limit (oci-client 0.18.0 src/client.rs:905,913).

oci-client pull_manifest_raw (src/client.rs:1059-1069, then _pull_manifest_raw 1159-1184) reads the whole manifest or error body with Response::bytes() at 1176, then validates the status (1178) and the digest (1181) before it returns.
The 4 MiB cap is checked on a body that is already fully in memory, so it does not bound the memory a registry can make ranikust hold.

evidence.description: MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES = 4 << 20, 'distribution's own limit'. It is applied only in raw_manifest (client.rs:1431).
bytes_in += body.len() records the full received length before raw_manifest runs. The spans test (tests/spans/main.rs:68) observes this field.

Sibling control: ranikust's own token reads (identity-token exchange, mount token) stop at MAX_BODY = 1 MiB while streaming (token.rs:54,124-130). oci-client's token path used by Strategy::Oci has no equivalent.

read_timeout is applied only when set. It defaults to None (client.rs:105), crates/ranikust/src/build.rs:651-669 never sets it, and no total request timeout is set. A per-read timeout would not bound a fast stream anyway; it matters only for a drip-fed body.

oci-client 0.18.0. Its _pull_manifest_raw (src/client.rs:1176), _auth (905, 913) and pull_blob error path (1363, reached from rnk-registry client.rs:575) call Response::bytes()/text(). reqwest 0.13.5 (Cargo.lock:1191) implements these as BodyExt::collect with no limit (src/async_impl/response.rs:290,433).
T15 control: 'Stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion' (A7, availability of host memory).
Section 8 rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings (T15, T16) as Medium. Section 6 (lines 100-160) contains no acceptance of registry-driven memory exhaustion.

The crate card's Pitfalls already notes that oci-client 'reads manifest bodies whole' and that manifests over 4 MiB 'are rejected only after reading'. This is a known limitation, not an ADR or a threat-model section 6 acceptance.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run: there is no OS-enforced sandbox on the host, and the VM and T2c lanes have external network. The full buffering is established from the oci-client 0.18.0 and reqwest 0.13.5 sources pinned in Cargo.lock, not observed.

Decisive deployment fact: whether ranikust runs in its own memory cgroup in each supported deployment, so an OOM stays within the build. Inside a pod or container memory limit, the effect equals the registry refusing service, which it can already do. On a bare host or CI runner without a limit, memory pressure, swap thrash and the OOM killer reach other workloads (A7). The repository cannot show this.
