For each supported deployment, record whether a single ranikust process is confined by its own memory cgroup, so that an OOM caused by a hostile registry stays within that build: a Kubernetes pod with resources.limits.memory, a CI host running ranikust as root directly (systemd scope or none), and a Docker container without --memory. Also record the memory available to it and whether swap is enabled. The finding is a shared-impact Medium (threat-model section 8) only where no per-build memory limit exists; elsewhere it is hardening against T15.

title: copy_filtered keeps two full paths per directory level with no depth or path-length bound, so a RUN-made deep tree costs the builder quadratic memory
description: The source trace holds: Copier::walk joins the full source and destination paths for every entry (copy.rs:301-302) and moves both into each pushed Frame (copy.rs:345), so a chain of D directories with n-byte names keeps about (n+1)*D*(D+1) bytes, roughly 0.95 GiB at D=2000 with 255-byte names. Nothing bounds depth except RLIMIT_NOFILE, at two fds per level. The copy is reached from FROM <stage> (stages.rs:429 -> copy_stage :153), the hand-over fallback (:400), keep and restore on the kaniko shared root (root.rs:825, :531) and COPY --from (stage.rs:965). Refutation: the only principal that can make a tree deeper than PATH_MAX is the RUN process. Layer extraction resolves each entry's parent with one openat2 of the whole path (extract.rs:992-995 -> root.rs mkdir_all/resolve_dir_in -> openat2 at root.rs:271), which fails with ENAMETOOLONG past PATH_MAX, so a base image without RUN cannot push the frames past a few MB. A context tree is created on the host by someone who already writes there. By accepted decision (ADR-0003 rejected default cgroup limits), the RUN already has unbounded memory: ranikust sets only RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE for RUN (spec.rs:44-94), creates no cgroup (ADR-0007, sched memory.rs:5-6), and T15 bounds RUN only by the outer cgroup. That outer cgroup is shared by ranikust and its RUN children. So the copy's growth gives the author no memory, host-availability or cross-tenant effect that a one-line RUN allocation lacks. In Direct mode the RUN shares ranikust's PID namespace as root and can kill ranikust outright. The only distinct effect is that ranikust, not the RUN, dies, and that fails only the author's own build. The leftover builds/<id> is removed by the next start's Store::cleanup (store.rs:322, 977-1003), which T16 requires to survive an abort. Any persistent effect from such a tree comes from delete.rs, whose Frame keeps the same per-level path (delete.rs:336-340), and the walk (walk.rs); both are separate root causes, and both process the tree whether or not the copy runs. What remains is hardening: bound depth or path length in the copy, or drop the full paths from Frame, and correct the rootfs.md:222-224 wording that memory stays 'bounded by the depth'.
claimed_root_cause: Copier::walk (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:276-357) stores the full `from` and `to` paths, built with Path::join for every entry, in each stack Frame. Copier::node stores a full destination path for each multi-link inode in `links` (copy.rs:521). Neither has a depth or path-length bound, and the only bound the code relies on is RLIMIT_NOFILE (two fds per level), which kaniko mode raises to the hard limit (main.rs:416).

trace.description: A stage built FROM a RUN-made parent copies the parent's root with copy_stage. The parent was not walked when its layers are not needed (stages.rs:491-496). The tree is made by the parent's RUN, the only principal that can exceed PATH_MAX.
copy_filtered(from, "", into, "", skip_special) runs over the whole stage root, filtered only by the ignore list.
The top directory starts Copier::walk with an explicit Frame stack.
For every entry, from = top.from.join(&name) and to = top.to.join(&name) (lines 301-302). There is no length or depth check.

Each subdirectory pushes a Frame that owns both full paths and two fds until its subtree is done. This uses quadratic memory inside ranikust, in the same process tree and cgroup whose memory the RUN can already exhaust without limit.

evidence.description: The Frame doc names RLIMIT_NOFILE as the only cost of depth. The fields from and to (copy.rs:235-236) hold full paths for each level. This part of the claim is correct.
The option to always enforce cgroup limits on RUN was considered and not chosen (Decision Outcome, lines 27-30). RUN memory is unbounded by ranikust by accepted decision.

Only RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE are managed for RUN. There is no RLIMIT_AS or memory cgroup, and ranikust only reads cgroups (rnk-sched/src/memory.rs:5-6, ADR-0007). The RUN and ranikust share the outer cgroup.
T15: fork bombs and other RUN-side exhaustion are bounded only by the outer cgroup, the same bound that applies to the copy's growth inside ranikust.

T16 requires cleanup that survives an abort. After an unclean exit, the next start's Store::cleanup removes builds/<id> (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:322, 977-1003), so the copy's failure does not persist.

Layer extraction makes each parent with RootPath::mkdir_all, which resolves the whole path with one openat2 (root.rs:271, through resolve_dir_in at root.rs:286). That fails with ENAMETOOLONG past PATH_MAX, so a base image cannot create a tree whose frame paths reach the claimed sizes. Only a RUN can.

The deletion Frame also keeps a full path per level (delete.rs:339-340, join at :225 and :423). Every RUN-made tree in a per-stage root is deleted this way whether or not it was copied, so any persistent or cross-build effect belongs to that separate root cause, not to the copy.

The statement that 'memory and fds stay bounded by the depth' (lines 222-224) is imprecise: memory is quadratic in depth times name length. This is a documentation and hardening item, not a boundary crossing.

reason: Source supports the growth, but no boundary is crossed. Only a RUN can build a tree past PATH_MAX, because layer extraction resolves full paths with one openat2. That RUN already has unbounded memory in the same process tree and cgroup by accepted decision (ADR-0003; T15 bounds it only by the outer cgroup; spec.rs sets no memory limit), and in Direct mode it can kill ranikust directly. So the copy's quadratic memory gives the Dockerfile author no new capability and no shared impact. Its only distinct effect is that the author's own build fails uncleanly, and the next start's cleanup recovers (T16). Any persistent effect would come from delete.rs or walk.rs, which are separate root causes. RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION rule 1 applies: a missing limit without concrete shared impact is hardening (bound depth or path length in Copier, keep names instead of full paths per Frame, fix rootfs.md:222-224).

title: COPY reads context files with root's DAC authority and no owner or link-count check, so a root-only host file hardlinked into a lower-trust account's context can enter the image
description: Attacker: a local unprivileged account that owns or can write a build-context directory which a separate, trusted root operator (for example a root CI runner or build service) later builds with ranikust, on a host where fs.protected_hardlinks=0 and the context shares a filesystem with the target file. The attacker runs `ln /etc/shadow ctx/s` (or any root-only file: /root/.docker/config.json, an SSH host key) and the context's Dockerfile says `COPY s /s`. ranikust builds as root only (crates/ranikust/src/setup.rs:132), and COPY runs in the main process, which keeps every capability: enter_build_namespace only unshares NEWNS (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22) and no capability is dropped outside the RUN child. The context walk reports the hardlink as an ordinary regular file (sources.rs:78-83, Kind::Other); copy_like takes the context RootPath as source (stage.rs:905) and forces owner 0:0 (stage.rs:934); Copier::run pins the name with O_PATH inside the context (copy.rs:247; copy.rs:307 for a directory COPY); Copier::node uses st.nlink only to re-link later names of the same inode inside this copy (copy.rs:486,520); copy_node reopens the pinned inode O_RDONLY through ranikust's own /proc/self/fd (copy.rs:662 -> meta.rs:275-278) with root's credentials, so CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE passes the 0600 check, and copy_data writes the bytes into the stage root (copy.rs:671), keeping the source mode (copy.rs:611) under 0:0. The content then reaches the layer, the pushed image or tar, and the build log through a later `RUN cat /s`; the RUN sandbox (pivot_root) that would stop RUN itself from reading the host file is bypassed because the read happens in COPY. Variant with the same root cause: a Dockerfile inside the context that is a hardlink to a root-only file is read as root through open_regular (build.rs:596), and an unknown first keyword is echoed verbatim as `unknown instruction: <keyword>` (instructions.rs:516). RESOLVE_IN_ROOT confinement stops names from escaping the context, not an inode shared with a host file. The only peer control is the kernel's fs.protected_hardlinks=1 (set by systemd's sysctl defaults on mainstream distributions), which stops an unprivileged account from creating a hardlink to a file it neither owns nor can read and write; ranikust itself has none. Not a boundary when the root operator builds a context they own, or when the lower-trust account can itself choose ranikust's flags (it could then name any --context), and no new reach in kaniko mode on a container's / where a Direct RUN reads that filesystem anyway. Calibration only: any root-run builder that walks a local context with root's DAC shares this pattern; that is not grounds to dismiss.
claimed_root_cause: rnk-rootfs copy_node (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/copy.rs:661-671) reopens every pinned regular source file through ranikust's own /proc/self/fd (meta.rs:275-278) with the full credentials of the root build process. Nothing on the context path binds that read to the authority of the context's owner: rnk-context records no owner of the context root (source.rs:50) and its EntryMeta has no link count (walk.rs:25-46); rnk-builder copy_like (stage.rs:905-981) and Copier::node (copy.rs:466-523, where nlink only preserves links between copied names) make no owner, link-count or access check; and nothing in crates/ looks at fs.protected_hardlinks.

trace.description: The root build process opens the --context directory, whose entries a lower-trust local account may have written (including hardlinks to host files on the same filesystem).
RootPath::open on the canonical context path; the owner of the context root is neither recorded nor used later.
The walk classifies a hardlinked regular file as Kind::Other like any regular file; it is kept unless .dockerignore excludes it.
COPY/ADD without --from uses the context RootPath as the source root.
rnk_rootfs::copy is called with owner 0:0 (line 934) and the source mode (copy_filtered at line 963 for a directory source); no owner or link check precedes it.
The source name is pinned with O_PATH inside the context root; a hardlink is a plain directory entry, so it resolves inside the root.
st.nlink > 1 only looks up an earlier copy of the same inode within this copy; the first name falls through to copy_node.
The Regular branch reopens the pinned inode O_RDONLY; the file type is the only check made.
openat of /proc/self/fd/N with the root process's credentials; CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE satisfies the 0600 permission check.
copy_data writes the root-only content into the stage root, from where it is encoded into the layer and the output image.

evidence.description: `let src = meta::reopen(pin, OFlags::RDONLY, path)?;` is the only step before reading the source, and it follows only a file-type match.
nlink is read but used only to keep hardlinks between copied entries (also line 520), never as a sign that another name lies outside the context.
EntryMeta records stx_uid but has no link-count field, and no decision uses the owner.
Context files get owner 0:0 (Docker's rule), and mode_of (copy.rs:611) keeps the source permission bits, so the copied host file keeps its 0600/0640 mode in the image.
NEEDS_ROOT: ranikust builds as root only and tells users to run it with sudo, so on a host the context is always read as root.
enter_build_namespace only unshares NEWNS; capability trimming exists only for RUN children, so the main process that copies the context keeps CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE.

A Dockerfile inside the context is read with open_regular as root; with instructions.rs:516 (`unknown instruction: {}` with the keyword as written), the first token of a hardlinked root-only file reaches stderr.

ranikust's code that reads the build context (COPY, .dockerignore) treats it as hostile; section 3 names no context owner distinct from the operator, T1/T2 cover only name escapes and layer hardlinks, and section 6 accepts only that a kaniko-mode RUN on / reads the context like any file on / (lines 119-122), nothing about ranikust's own root-authority reads of context files.
In scope: ranikust reading outside the places it should 'because of a crafted layer, build context or Dockerfile: ... symlinks, hardlinks' (lines 39-44).
RUN --mount=type=bind is refused for now, so outside kaniko mode on / (where a Direct RUN reads the context on / anyway) the root COPY/ADD read is the only path from a context file to the image.

The repository only names fsutil as BuildKit's context transfer; whether Docker or BuildKit read a local context with the invoking user's authority is not stated (parity is calibration for the maintainer's ruling, not a defence).

blockers: No target-controlled execution and no OS-enforced sandbox in this run: the root read of a hardlinked root-owned 0600 file through the /proc/self/fd reopen, and its arrival in the output layer, are unobserved.

Deployment fact outside source: exploitation needs fs.protected_hardlinks=0 (systemd's sysctl defaults set 1; the kernel's own default is 0), the context on the same filesystem as the target file, and a trusted root operator building a context written by another account whose output that account can read; how often ranikust runs that way is not source-visible.

Policy fact: threat-model.md section 3 (line 43) does not say whether a local build-context owner is a principal distinct from the root operator; SECURITY.md:39-44 puts crafted-context hardlinks in scope, but no ADR accepts or rejects root-authority context reads, so the maintainer must rule (BuildKit/Docker parity, settled through upstream-oracle, is calibration only).

validation_plan.local:
T2 in the disposable VM (a one-off root shell in the tests/vm guest), dummy data only, no registry push. (1) As root in the guest: `sysctl -w fs.protected_hardlinks=0`; `useradd -m ctxowner`; `printf 'DUMMY-ROOT-ONLY-7f3a
' > /srv/h42-secret && chown root:root /srv/h42-secret && chmod 0600 /srv/h42-secret`; confirm `stat -c %d /srv /home/ctxowner` prints the same device. (2) As ctxowner: `mkdir ~/ctx && ln /srv/h42-secret ~/ctx/s && printf 'FROM scratch
COPY s /s
' > ~/ctx/Dockerfile`; confirm `cat ~/ctx/s` fails with EACCES. (3) As root with cwd / (so the relative --dockerfile resolves inside the context, build.rs:561-567): `ranikust build --context /home/ctxowner/ctx --dockerfile Dockerfile --destination example.invalid/h42:test --no-push --tar-path /root/h42.tar`. (4) Unpack /root/h42.tar into a fresh directory, list the layer blob with `tar -tvf` (with -z or --zstd as its media type says) and print /s. The finding holds if /s contains DUMMY-ROOT-ONLY-7f3a with owner 0:0 and mode 0600. Control: with fs.protected_hardlinks=1, step 2's ln must fail with EPERM. Dockerfile variant: replace ~/ctx/Dockerfile with a hardlink to a root-owned 0600 dummy whose first line is `DUMMYTOKEN-9c1e`, rerun step 3, and check stderr for `unknown instruction: DUMMYTOKEN-9c1e`. Afterwards remove the user, the files and the sysctl change (the VM is disposable).
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: for each host class where ranikust runs as root on contexts written by other accounts (self-hosted CI runners, build services), record `sysctl fs.protected_hardlinks`, whether context directories share a filesystem with /etc and /root, and whether the context's writer can read the built image or build log. The maintainer records in threat-model.md section 3 whether the local context owner is a distinct, lower-trust principal.

title: Deleting a RUN-made deep directory chain uses memory quadratic in its depth; an OOM kill leaves the tree for every later build's start-up cleanup to hit again
description: In overlay mode and in kaniko mode off / (per-stage directories, persistent store), a RUN writes freely below builds/<id>/stages/<n>/: the overlay upper diff-<k> (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:489-511) or the stage rootfs (kaniko/stages.rs). With mkdir+chdir it can build one chain of D directories with 255-byte names. That costs D directories, about 4 KiB of disk each, and no descriptor held by the RUN. Every deletion of the tree goes through rnk_rootfs::delete_contents -> remove_below -> remove_below_seen. That happens first when the build releases its stages (build.rs:349 release_all -> OverlayStage::release, stage.rs:571; kaniko/stages.rs:295 or prune at :367). It happens again at Store::close -> remove_build (store.rs:969), and after a process death in the next build's Store::open -> cleanup -> remove_if_dead -> remove_build. The walk is iterative, but it pushes one Frame per directory level (delete.rs:455), and each frame owns its full relative path, child = top.path.join(&name) (delete.rs:423). That path is used only for statx/open error messages; open_name and statx_at work on (parent fd, name) (root.rs:913-918). In a single chain nothing is removed until the bottom is reached, so the live frames hold about (L+1)*D^2/2 bytes. That is about 4.6 GB at D=6000 and 12.8 GB at D=10000 with L=255. The allocated capacity is about twice that: Path::join copies the parent path at its exact length, then pushing the separator doubles the buffer (std 1.99.1 path.rs _join/_push); how much of the untouched half is resident depends on the allocator. The only depth bound is RLIMIT_NOFILE (delete.rs:29-30). Kaniko mode raises the soft limit to the hard limit before opening the store (main.rs:416, statedir.rs:370-384), commonly 524288 or more. Overlay mode inherits whatever ranikust started with. A soft limit of 1024 makes the walk fail with EMFILE at depth ~1000 (about 128-256 MB): a returned error, logged and skipped. A high soft limit, as container runtimes often set, lets the depth reach the memory limit. Export refuses entry paths past PATH_MAX (export.rs:601-609) and fails the step, but it deletes nothing. In kaniko mode off /, the diff walk after the RUN (kaniko/stages.rs:498 end_layer -> diff_in) runs before any deletion and also keeps one full path per new entry (kaniko/walk.rs:699-700 Changed.path, and DirOut.path per directory), not bounded by descriptors per level, so there the first kill may come in that walk; it leaves builds/<id> the same way. That walk runs only in the build that ran the RUN and is a separate root cause; the persistence across builds goes through the deletion walk alone. If ranikust is OOM-killed (or aborts on allocation failure) while deleting the chain, builds/<id> stays and its flock is released. Every later Store::open on the same state directory then runs cleanup (store.rs:322) before anything else, reaches the same tree and dies the same way. cleanup's contract (store.rs:973-976) catches returned errors only. So one RUN can keep every later build that shares the state directory from starting, until an operator removes builds/<id> by hand. Threat-model T15 lists deep trees with the mitigation 'fail cleanly on exhaustion' (threat-model.md:92). Section 3 says other builds sharing the store may belong to another trust domain (threat-model.md:46). No ADR or section 6 entry accepts unbounded deletion memory. T14's 'give each trust domain its own store' covers cache mounts only. The same per-frame path pattern is in prune's PruneFrame (delete.rs:179, 225, 249-255), used for the kaniko per-stage hand-over. It is also in the Direct-mode emptying of / (kaniko/root.rs:471), where the anonymous store keeps nothing and the effect stays within the one build.
claimed_root_cause: rnk-rootfs delete.rs keeps one Frame (and one PruneFrame in prune) per directory level for its iterative deletion walk, and every frame owns a fresh copy of its full relative path built with top.path.join(name), kept only for error messages. Live memory is therefore O(L*D^2) in the tree depth D. Only descriptors were treated as the depth cost (delete.rs:29-30); neither delete_contents nor rnk-store's close and start-up cleanup bounds depth or memory, and cleanup's per-build error isolation does not cover process death.

trace.scope: OverlayStage::begin_layer: the RUN's writable upper builds/<id>/stages/<n>/diff-<k>
trace.description: Each RUN layer gets an upper directory under builds/<build-id>/stages/<n> (rel built at stage.rs:325), mounted as the RUN's root (stage.rs:500-511). A RUN (Dockerfile author, lower-trust) creates one chain of D directories with 255-byte names by mkdir and chdir per level. In kaniko mode off / the RUN writes the same way into builds/<id>/stages/<n>/rootfs.

trace.scope: export::child, overlay upper export after the RUN
trace.description: An entry path longer than PATH_MAX is refused with Error::Export and the step fails; nothing is deleted here, so the chain stays below builds/<id>.

trace.scope: run_with: release_all after the build, whatever its result
trace.description: Stages are released; OverlayStage::release unmounts and calls delete_contents on the stage directory (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:571), the first deletion of the chain. If ranikust dies there, builds/<id> and its lock file stay, the flock released.
If release returned an error (for example EMFILE), Store::close -> remove_build (rnk-store/src/store.rs:969) deletes builds/<id> through the same delete_contents.

trace.scope: Store::open of every later build on the same --state-dir
trace.description: store.cleanup()? runs right after registration, before the build does anything else.
For the dead build id, remove_if_dead takes its now free flock and calls remove_build (store.rs:1014). Only returned errors are logged and skipped (store.rs:996-999).
remove_tree(tmp/<id>) then remove_tree(builds/<id>), which calls remove_dir_tree for a directory (store.rs:1378).
After the mount and identity checks, delete_contents(&sub, &IgnoreList::new()) on builds/<id>.
Opens the root and calls remove_below, which calls remove_below_seen.

child = top.path.join(&name) allocates the full relative path. For a directory it is moved into a new Frame pushed on the stack (delete.rs:452-462). In a single chain nothing is unlinked before the bottom, so D frames hold paths of about (L+1), 2(L+1) ... D(L+1) bytes: about (L+1)*D^2/2 bytes resident, bounded only by RLIMIT_NOFILE (one fd per frame).

evidence.description: The contract names descriptors as the only depth cost: 'Depth is unlimited by PATH_MAX, but one fd is held per level: the caller raises RLIMIT_NOFILE for deep trees.'
Frame.path is an owned PathBuf, the directory's full cleaned relative path, kept in every live frame.
stack.push(Frame { fd, path: child, name, names, .. }) for every directory to delete; no depth or byte bound.
open_name works on (dirfd, name) with RESOLVE flags; its doc says `path` is only for error messages, so a long path never stops the descent early (statx_at likewise, meta.rs:170).
Same pattern in prune_walk: child = top.path.join(&name) is pushed into PruneFrame.path (delete.rs:179, 249-255), used by the kaniko per-stage hand-over.
The deep-tree test uses DEPTH 3004 with 10-byte names (about 50 MB of frame paths) and asserts only that the tree is gone; memory is never measured.

Kaniko mode raises RLIMIT_NOFILE to its hard limit before set_up_kaniko opens the store, so descriptors do not stop a depth of many thousands of levels. Overlay mode has no such call and inherits the starting soft limit.
raise_nofile_limit sets the soft limit equal to the hard limit.

cleanup's contract: anything that fails for one build is left with a warning and must not stop this build. It is enforced only for returned errors (store.rs:995-1000); a process death repeats at every start.
A refused or failed release drops the stage, unmounted, and its directories stay until the store closes, so the RUN-made tree always reaches a delete_contents call.
Kaniko per-stage directories under builds/<id>/stages are deleted through the same delete_contents.

T15 names deep trees as a threat to host availability (A7), with the mitigation 'fail cleanly on exhaustion'. Section 6 does not accept this risk, and section 8 rates DoS from untrusted input with default settings Medium.
Other builds sharing the store may belong to another trust domain, so a build that blocks every later Store::open crosses a boundary.
The Direct-mode emptying of / uses the same walk; the anonymous store keeps no builds/<id>, so there the effect stays within one build.

blockers: No target-controlled execution in this run: the peak memory of delete_contents on a deep chain, including PathBuf capacity slack, was not measured.

Whether an OOM kill comes before EMFILE depends on the deployment's RLIMIT_NOFILE and memory limit. Kaniko mode off / raises the soft limit to the hard limit (main.rs:416). Overlay mode inherits its starting soft limit; with 1024 the walk fails cleanly with EMFILE at depth ~1000.
The runtime effect was not observed: that an OOM kill during release or close leaves builds/<id> with a free lock, and that the next build on the same --state-dir is killed in rnk_store.cleanup.

validation_plan.local: T0, no root, in a worktree: add an #[ignore] test next to deletes_a_tree_deeper_than_path_max in crates/rnk-rootfs/src/delete/tests.rs. It raises the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE as that test does. Then, in the Fixture tempdir, it builds one chain of D directories, each named with 255 'd' bytes, with mkdirat/openat on O_PATH fds (dropping the previous fd), and runs delete_contents(&f.root, &IgnoreList::new()). D is read from an environment variable. Build once (cargo test -p rnk-rootfs --no-run), then run the printed test binary directly for D=500, 1000 and 2000 under /usr/bin/time -v as '<binary> --ignored --exact delete::tests::<name> --test-threads=1' (no '--' when the binary is run directly: libtest would read what follows as name filters and run nothing), and read 'Maximum resident set size'. If the claim holds, RSS above baseline grows about 4x per doubling: about 32, 128 and 512 MB, up to 2x more with capacity slack. Repeat D=2000 under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=256M to see a kill instead of an error. The tempdir goes with the fixture; if killed, remove it with rm -rf. Then T2 in the disposable VM (just test-vm), two lanes. (a) --mode=kaniko off /. (b) overlay mode after ulimit -Sn 65536, which emulates a container runtime's high soft limit; a run at the default 1024 should show the clean EMFILE path instead. Use a dummy Dockerfile FROM busybox whose RUN executes a COPYed static helper that mkdirs and chdirs 2500 levels of 255-byte names. Run ranikust under systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=512M with a fresh --state-dir. Observe the kill inside rnk_snapshot.release or rnk_rootfs.delete in lane (b); in lane (a) it may come earlier, in the diff walk after the RUN (rnk_snapshot.walk, a debug span), which holds its own full-path list. In both lanes check that builds/<id> is left with its lock free. Run a second trivial build on the same --state-dir under the same limit and observe the kill inside rnk_store.cleanup. Finally remove the state directory. The T2c lane can repeat (b) in a privileged rootful container with --memory=512m and --ulimit nofile=65536 and the state dir on a throwaway volume. Fix check: frames keep only their name (one shared PathBuf pushed and popped per level, or the path rebuilt from the stack for messages), the same in PruneFrame. Optionally, a depth cap leaves the tree with a warning. The T0 test must then show linear RSS.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: for each CI host or pod that shares one --state-dir in overlay mode or in kaniko mode off /, record the ranikust process's soft and hard RLIMIT_NOFILE (cat /proc/<pid>/limits, or ulimit -Sn and ulimit -Hn in its environment) and its cgroup memory.max. Kaniko mode uses the hard limit; overlay mode uses the soft one. With 255-byte names, an OOM comes before EMFILE once that limit exceeds about sqrt(memory_bytes/128): about 4100 for 2 GiB and about 8200 for 8 GiB. Also record whether builds from different trust domains share the state directory.

title: Overlay-mode hardlink copy-up has no image-wide byte budget across a layer stack (rejected: same exhaustion the same principal already has, handled as T15 requires)
description: Source confirms the mechanics: in overlay mode pull_image extracts each manifest layer with every earlier layer as a lower; extract_overlay copies a hardlink target that is absent from the current layer out of the nearest lower layer, and dedups copies only within one layer (Extractor::copied, keyed by lower index and inode, created per extract_with call). A base-image publisher can therefore stack small layers, each holding only hardlink entries, so that each entry writes a whole lower file into <state>/layers. On a non-reflink state-dir filesystem (ext4, tmpfs), copy_data copies every data range. The copy bytes are not part of decoder.tar_size(), the size reported to Store::fill. This is not a vulnerability. The per-layer bound the design documents holds. T15's required mitigation for decompression bombs and huge files is 'stream; fail cleanly on exhaustion', and this path meets it. The same principal already reaches the same resource (the state-dir filesystem), with the same blast radius, persistence and recovery, through the decoder, which has no output cap, and through any RUN, which executes the image's own binaries as root into upper directories in the state directory with no quota (ADR-0007). The copy-up only lowers an attacker cost that is already trivial. On reflink filesystems it adds almost nothing physically. An image-wide extraction budget that counts copy-up bytes is hardening.
claimed_root_cause: Extractor::copied, the only dedup of copy-up bytes, is created per extract_with call and keyed by lower-layer index (extract.rs:212, 282, 622). Every later layer can therefore copy each visible lower inode again, including earlier layers' copies. Copy-up bytes are not counted in the size extract_layer returns to Store::fill (layer.rs:128, 145). pull_image applies no layer or byte budget (pull.rs:114-127). MAX_LOWERS is checked only at mount time (mount.rs:68).

trace.description: Each layer of the base-image publisher's manifest is extracted in order. Every earlier extracted layer is passed as 'below' (line 116), and no layer-count or byte budget applies.
Overlay mode opens the pulled blob and calls layer::extract_layer. Overlay keeps the trait's default streamed_layer None (stage.rs:187), so every base layer takes this path.
Inside Store::fill, the lower layer directories, nearest first, become extract_overlay's lowers. The size returned to the store is decoder.tar_size() (line 128), which excludes copy-up bytes.
A fresh 'copied' map is created for each layer, so copy-up dedup never spans layers.
find_lower locates a hardlink target that is absent from this layer in the nearest lower layer that shows it. The per-layer key (line 622) misses on the first link to each lower inode in a layer.
copy::copy_node copies the whole lower file for a zero-size hardlink entry. The bytes count only toward the rnk_rootfs.extract span's bytes_written.

Where FICLONE is refused (ext4, tmpfs), each data range of the lower file is written into the new layer's tmp entry in the store. Lower files are dense because extraction writes them with std::io::copy (extract.rs:457). An ENOSPC from copy_file_range or pwrite is returned as an error (copy.rs:843).

evidence.description: T15 lists decompression bombs and huge or very many files, which are small inputs that cause large writes. The required mitigation is 'Stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion'. It sets no byte cap. This path streams (an in-kernel clone or copy, with a 128 KiB buffer at most) and fails cleanly on ENOSPC.

When the fill closure fails (for example an ENOSPC from copy_data), Store::fill drops the entry, removes the tmp directory, and returns Error::Fill. Nothing partial is published, which satisfies T15's clean failure.

The documented bound is per layer: copies are keyed by lower layer and inode, 'so the bytes written stay bounded by the lower layers' size'. The code holds that bound (key at line 622, insert at line 655). No stated invariant promises an image-wide bound.
The design states the same per-layer bound: 'however many names a layer links'. It is aimed at name multiplicity within one layer, and the implementation matches it.

The decoder bounds memory only and has no output cap. The same base-image publisher can therefore already fill the same state-dir filesystem with an ordinary zstd or gzip bomb (zstd RLE blocks reach about 32768:1, roughly 32 MiB of blob per TiB written), with the same per-layer publication and persistence.

Accepted decision: 'ranikust cannot limit a RUN's resources itself; that is left to the environment'. In any build with a RUN, the image's own binaries (for example /bin/sh) run as root and can write without a quota into the stage's upper directories under the state directory.

The overlay upper directories (diff-<k>) live in the stage directory <state>/builds/<id>/stages/<n>/ (stage.rs:365-366, 327-330), on the same filesystem as <state>/layers. A RUN filling it exhausts the resource the candidate targets.
copy_data tries FICLONE first. On reflink filesystems (XFS with reflink=1, btrfs) the copy-ups share extents with the lower file and add almost no physical usage.

Correction to the candidate: this sentence ('They stay on disk until prune') refers to entries of the old v1 layer layout. Retention of current layers until a prune that does not exist yet is described in docs/design/cache-and-store.md:100, and it applies equally to decompression-bomb layers and to large legitimate images.

every_name_of_a_lower_inode_shares_one_copy covers only the intra-layer bound the design promises. No test covers copy-up bytes across layers, which is consistent with no cross-layer bound being promised.

reason: The source trace is accurate, but it does not establish a vulnerability. (1) No stated invariant is broken. The bound documented at extract.rs:145-147 and rootfs.md:140-144 is per layer, and the code holds it. T15 (threat-model.md:92), the row for small inputs that cause large writes, requires only 'stream; fail cleanly on exhaustion', and this path meets that: an in-kernel copy, ENOSPC returned as an error (copy.rs:843), and Store::fill discarding the tmp entry without publishing (store.rs:677-683). (2) There is no incremental boundary effect. The same lower-trust principal already exhausts the same state-dir filesystem, with the same blast radius, persistence and recovery, through the uncapped decoder (decoder.rs:21) at trivial blob cost. In any build with a RUN, it can also do so through its own binaries writing without a quota into upper directories under <state> (ADR-0007:50-51, accepted; stage.rs:365, 521). Cheaper amplification of an already trivial and already available disk fill changes neither reachability, scope nor recovery. On reflink filesystems FICLONE (copy.rs:737) removes even the physical cost. (3) The argument that a future decoded-size cap would miss copy-up bytes depends on a control that is neither implemented nor planned, since T15 plans no cap. Under the resource-exhaustion rule, a missing image-wide limit without concrete incremental shared impact is hardening. Any future image-wide extraction budget should count copy-up bytes, and that belongs with the decoder-output and store-retention work rather than in a separate finding.

title: Image-supplied trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE, written with ranikust's capabilities, can leave directories root cannot delete on XFS (store tmp/, kaniko stage dirs; with CAP_SYS_ADMIN kept, a container's '/' and COPY --from views)
description:
Layer extraction writes every PAX SCHILY.xattr.<name> record of a registry layer verbatim and strictly. header_meta (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:517) keeps the raw name and value. xattr_name (:687-701) escapes only user.overlay.* in the overlay form and returns every other name unchanged for Overlay, Apply (kaniko live roots) and Literal. apply() calls apply_with with no skip list (meta.rs:500-501), so setxattr runs with ranikust's own capabilities (meta.rs:617, :662) and any refusal fails the extraction. Nothing filters trusted.*, security.* or system.*. On XFS, trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE is the raw on-disk access ACL. By kernel source as recalled (not observed in this run), xfs_xattr_set stores it unvalidated and only drops the cached ACL (xfs_forget_acl: the caller must supply valid data).

Attack (lower-trust base-image publisher, no RUN needed): a directory owned by a non-root uid, with tar mode 0775 and a malformed SGI_ACL_FILE (4 bytes declaring 5 entries, which xfs_acl_from_disk rejects with EFSCORRUPTED). The directory is made 0700 (DIR_PENDING_MODE, extract.rs:58, :441) and gets owner and xattrs at once (dir_meta, :705-730). While its children are written no ACL is consulted, so root's DAC override applies. finish() then chmods it (extract.rs:1106 for store roots, :1119 for live roots; chmodat at meta.rs:671). XFS commits i_mode before posix_acl_chmod reads the ACL, so the chmod fails, the extraction fails and the group bits stay. From then on any permission check by a non-owner, root included, reaches check_acl. generic_permission returns its decode error before it tries CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. Deletion opens each directory O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY (delete.rs:453, open_dir_checked :496-528) and has no chmod or xattr-strip fallback (delete.rs:31-35).

Variants, each re-checked against source at ed718fb:
(A) Overlay mode as host root (the default on a host). Store::fill extracts into tmp/<build>/<n> (rnk-snapshot layer.rs:116-127). On failure, discard (store.rs:680, :1092-1096), Store::close through close_store (build.rs:373) and the next start's cleanup (store.rs:977-1003) only warn. tmp/<build> stays in the shared state dir with up to the layer's uncompressed content and its lock file, once per build attempt. That breaks the fill contract (store.rs:646) and T15's 'fail cleanly' (A7).
(B) Kaniko mode with per-stage directories (ADR-0059: host root that can mount, off '/'). KanikoStage::fill runs extract_blob, then extract_checked, then extract_live (stages.rs:424, kaniko/root.rs:995-1012). A failed fill's stage.remove only warns (stages.rs:247-249). delete_stage_dir (stages.rs:294-298) stops at the poisoned directory. Store::close's remove_build error is only logged (store.rs:959-969, :1350-1362, build.rs:373), and the startup cleanup only warns (store.rs:998). builds/<id>/stages/<n>/rootfs keeps whatever delete_contents had not reached, once per build.
(C) Kaniko mode on a container's '/' (Isolation::Direct) when ranikust holds CAP_SYS_ADMIN but cannot mount. The project's own experiment 13 records that docker run --cap-add SYS_ADMIN under docker-default AppArmor cannot mount (EACCES) and lands in kaniko mode. can_mount is enter_build_namespace (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:22-46, main.rs:239-247), so refuse_unsafe_slash (main.rs:462-504) passes. direct_caps (caps.rs:139-153) drops SYS_ADMIN only from the RUN child (spawner.rs:1655-1668); ranikust keeps it while it extracts. The image publisher thus gets a privileged xattr written that the trimmed Direct RUN could not write itself. mark_slash creates /ranikust/.built before the first extraction (kaniko/root.rs:651, :312-347), and Kaniko::finish leaves '/' as it is (:276-277). Every later build in that container therefore calls empty_root (:658-659), which propagates delete_contents' error (:471) through new_base and prepare (:577) and fails. A poisoned './' entry is applied to '/' itself (extract.rs:405-408, RootPath::set_meta root.rs:756) and chowns it to the layer's uid. Unverified host-side effect: on an XFS upper directory, overlayfs forwards the xattr to the upper inode, and the runtime's removal of the container's writable layer may then fail on the host. The in-container part is weak on its own: threat-model section 6 (line 130) says builds one after the other in one container trust one another, and ADR-0051 puts denial of service by a RUN out of scope. What this variant adds is a route that needs no RUN and a possible host-side leak.
(D) COPY --from=<image> on '/', under the same conditions as (C). KanikoRoot::unpacked extracts the image into a prefixed directory of the state directory (kaniko/root.rs:1053-1102, make_dir :717). clear_views and remove_view propagate the deletion error (:423-466), and Kaniko::finish's failure is only logged (build.rs:274-278). The next Store::open_anonymous calls anon::remove_leftovers with '?' (store.rs:377; anon.rs:291-311 calling remove_dir_tree at store.rs:1393-1413). Every later build on that state directory then fails to start until it is repaired by hand, including on a volume reused by later containers.

Not affected: overlay mode in a user namespace, and kaniko mode on '/' without CAP_SYS_ADMIN (Docker's default). There setxattr(trusted.*) gets EPERM and the strict extraction fails before anything is poisoned. extract_live_literal is not a separate vector: it only receives ranikust's own stage tars, which keep only security.capability (kaniko/export.rs:213-216, lowers.rs:50-54). No output image is affected, because exported layers keep only security.capability. Calibration: kaniko restores only security.capability from SCHILY.xattr (per the hunter, outside this repository; not re-read here). The sibling control ADR-0041 (extract.rs:377-381) refuses device nodes in live roots because ranikust would create privileged objects from layer data. Xattrs have no equivalent policy, and no test checks trusted.* in extraction. No ADR and no threat-model section 6 entry accepts unfiltered privileged xattr namespaces. The effect is availability only: no host file write and no image poisoning, and the operator can recover by hand (chmod 0700 the directory or remove the xattr, then delete it). On the threat model's own ladder this is at most Medium (T15-style denial of service). It needs a hostile base image and either XFS under the state dir (A, B) or CAP_SYS_ADMIN with mounts denied (C, D).
claimed_root_cause: Extractor::header_meta (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:517) and Extractor::xattr_name (:687-701) pass image-chosen xattr names in privileged namespaces unchanged, for Overlay, Apply and Literal alike. They reach the strict meta::apply_with (meta.rs:500-501, :588, :617, :662), which runs with ranikust's full capabilities. Those are real root in overlay mode and in kaniko per-stage mode. On a container's '/' they are the set ADR-0051 trims only from the RUN child (rnk-sandbox caps.rs:139, spawner.rs:1662). No namespace policy matches ADR-0041's device-node refusal, so an untrusted layer reaches a filesystem interface (XFS trusted.SGI_ACL_*) whose contract leaves validation to the privileged caller. The deletion paths (rnk-rootfs delete.rs:453, :496-528, used by store.rs:1393-1413, kaniko/stages.rs:294-298 and kaniko/root.rs:452-471) cannot recover a directory that refuses root with an error other than EACCES. Store and stage cleanup only warn, while empty_root behind the .built marker and anon::remove_leftovers at Store::open_anonymous carry the error into every later build.

trace.description: A registry layer blob from the lower-trust base-image publisher is filled into the shared store by Store::fill under tmp/<build-id>/<n> and decoded into extract_overlay (line 127). The diff_id check at line 130 runs after extraction and covers the publisher's own bytes, so it does not stop this. The kaniko-mode entries (KanikoStage::fill stages.rs:424, Kaniko::prepare kaniko/root.rs:577-579, KanikoRoot::unpacked :1102) reach the same Extractor through extract_checked -> extract_live (kaniko/root.rs:1012).
Each PAX key starting with SCHILY.xattr. becomes (xattr_name(name), raw value bytes) in Meta.xattrs. Nothing checks the namespace or the value.
Only user.overlay.* is escaped, and only in the overlay form. trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE is returned unchanged in Overlay, Apply (kaniko live roots) and Literal modes.

The directory is created with DIR_PENDING_MODE 0700. dir_meta (line 705; set_meta_at at line 718, or RootPath::set_meta for the layer's './' entry, line 405-408) at once applies the tar's uid/gid (non-root) and the xattrs, and defers mode and times to finish().

setxattr through ranikust's /proc/self/fd magic link (XattrTarget::MagicLink, meta.rs:412-414) with CAP_SYS_ADMIN. skipped is None (meta.rs:500-501), so any refusal aborts the extraction. A successful set is stored as is.

set_dir_meta (or set_meta_at at line 1119 in a live root) reaches the chmodat at meta.rs:671 with the tar mode (0775). By kernel source (unobserved), XFS commits i_mode and then posix_acl_chmod fails to decode the ACL. The extraction returns an error, and the directory keeps its group bits and the corrupt ACL.

The fill closure fails and discard(&tmp) is called. discard (line 1092) calls remove_tree, then remove_dir_tree, which calls delete_contents (line 1411). The kaniko variants reach the same delete_contents through delete_stage_dir (stages.rs:294-298), empty_root (kaniko/root.rs:471) and anon::remove_leftovers (anon.rs:301).

Deletion opens the poisoned directory O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW (line 505). The ACL decode error is returned before CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE is tried, so the open fails and the error is passed up. discard (store.rs:1094), close (store.rs:969, only warned by build.rs:373) and the startup cleanup (store.rs:998) only warn, so the entry and its content stay in the shared state dir. On a container's '/' the same error fails every later empty_root and every later Store::open_anonymous (store.rs:377).

evidence.description: if let Some(name) = key.strip_prefix(PAX_XATTR) { xattrs.push((self.xattr_name(name), ext.value_bytes().to_vec())); }: no namespace filter.
Whiteouts::Overlay | Whiteouts::Apply | Whiteouts::Literal => OsStr::from_bytes(name).to_owned(): names other than user.overlay.* pass through unchanged.
DIR_PENDING_MODE = 0o700: a directory has no group bits while its children are written, so its access ACL is first consulted after finish() sets the final mode.
extract_live = extract_with(dst, tar, Whiteouts::Apply, &[], Some(keep)): kaniko-mode base layers and COPY --from images take the unescaped branch of xattr_name.
Sibling control (ADR-0041): live extraction skips device nodes and FIFOs, which are privileged objects ranikust would create from layer data. Privileged xattr names have no equivalent check.
The layer's './' entry goes to dir_meta(path, None) and RootPath::set_meta on the root itself: on a container's '/', '/' is chowned to the layer's uid and given the layer's xattrs.
apply() calls apply_with(h, m, path, None): extraction is strict, so a refused setxattr is an error (xattr_result, meta.rs:578-580), and an accepted trusted.* value is kept.
The final mode is applied with chmodat through /proc/self/fd after the owner and xattrs (order: owner, xattrs, mode, times).

open_dir_checked opens with OFlags::RDONLY | DIRECTORY | NOFOLLOW and returns any error other than LOOP/NOTDIR/XDEV/NOENT. The doc at delete.rs:31-35 says there is no path-based fallback and 'whatever is left stays'.
discard: a failed remove_tree is only logged ('state directory: {} not removed').
cleanup: 'leftovers of build {id} not removed' is a warning. Nothing chmods or strips xattrs to recover (overlay tmp/ and kaniko builds/<id>/stages alike).
The fill contract says Error::Fill is returned 'after its temporary entry is removed'. This path breaks that.
close_store only logs Store::close's remove_build error (store.rs:969, :1350-1362), and the build goes on to exit.

Per-stage (ADR-0059): after a failed fill (extract_blob at stages.rs:424), stage.remove() only warns ('removing a stage directory after a failure'). delete_stage_dir (line 294) cannot delete the poisoned tree.
direct_caps decides only what the Direct RUN child drops (applied at spawner.rs:1662). ranikust itself keeps CAP_SYS_ADMIN while it extracts on '/'.

refuse_unsafe_slash refuses only can_mount, --network=none and a writable /proc/sys. can_mount is enter_build_namespace (unshare NEWNS plus a recursive MS_SLAVE change, rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:22-46). The comment at line 464 equates CAP_SYS_ADMIN with may-mount.

Measured: with --cap-add SYS_ADMIN alone, mount returns EACCES under AppArmor docker-default, and that container lands in kaniko mode (line 7). So kaniko mode on '/' with CAP_SYS_ADMIN in ranikust is a documented configuration, not a contrived one.
new_base calls mark_slash, which makes /ranikust/.built before the first extraction. The next build in the container sees it and calls empty_root (line 659).
empty_root propagates delete_contents' error with '?', so prepare (line 577) fails for every later build in that container.

On '/', COPY --from=<image> unpacks the verified image with Spooled::extract -> extract_checked -> extract_live into a prefixed directory of the state directory (make_dir, line 717). remove_view (line 452) propagates a deletion failure, and Kaniko::finish's error is only logged (build.rs:274-278).
Store::open_anonymous runs anon::remove_leftovers(...)?. A view it cannot delete (anon.rs:301, remove_dir_tree) fails the start of every later build on that state directory.

layer_xattrs keeps only security.capability in exported layers (ADR-0032, Q-025), and kaniko-mode export uses it too (kaniko/export.rs:213-216). Dropping trusted.* and other security.* names at extraction would lose no output content.
Strongest related control: the userxattr overlay option makes image trusted.overlay.* inert. It does not cover other trusted.* names that the underlying filesystem itself interprets.

T15 (A7) requires failing cleanly on exhaustion. Section 6 accepts nothing about privileged xattr namespaces in extraction, and section 3 puts only kernel bugs out of scope, not a documented interface contract.

Accepted risk: builds one after the other in one container trust one another. ADR-0051 (line 17-19) also puts denial of service by a RUN out of scope. This weakens the in-container part of variant (C), but it does not cover the shared store (A, B), a state volume reused across containers (D) or a host-side leak.

blockers: No target or kernel execution is allowed in this run, and no kernel source is available locally. Unobserved: whether current XFS with CONFIG_XFS_POSIX_ACL accepts setxattr('trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE', malformed) from CAP_SYS_ADMIN without validation and only invalidates the cached ACL (xfs_xattr_set, then xfs_forget_acl).

Unobserved: whether XFS chmod commits i_mode before posix_acl_chmod fails with EFSCORRUPTED. Also unobserved: whether generic_permission then returns check_acl's decode error to uid 0 without the CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE/CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH fallback, so that openat(O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) on the directory fails for root.

Variants (C) and (D): unobserved with the current probe that enter_build_namespace (unshare NEWNS plus the recursive MS_SLAVE change) fails under docker-default AppArmor with --cap-add SYS_ADMIN. Experiment 13 measured mount EACCES there, but before ADR-0054's refusal existed. Also unobserved: that overlayfs forwards a container process's setxattr('trusted.SGI_ACL_FILE') to the XFS upper inode, and that the poisoned upper directory blocks the runtime's removal of the container layer on the host.

Deployment facts outside source: whether --state-dir (A, B, D) or the container runtime's storage (C) is on XFS on the intended hosts (for example the RHEL/RHCOS default /var). Also whether any kaniko-mode build container or pod is given CAP_SYS_ADMIN under an LSM profile that denies mount.

title: Kaniko-mode extraction (Whiteouts::Apply) keeps the path of every entry and parent directory a layer creates until the layer ends, even those the same layer deletes, so memory grows with entry count and depth while disk stays flat
description: Whiteouts::Apply is used in production only by extract_live (the non-live extract with Apply appears only in crates/ranikust/examples/smoke-build.rs). Kaniko mode calls extract_live for base layers (on a container's / after the layer is spooled and verified, root.rs:885-891; in per-stage directories on a host, stages.rs:424) and for the layers of a `COPY --from=<image>` source: when the root is /, they are unpacked on first read into a scratch directory of the state directory (root.rs:1102); elsewhere into a keep-area directory (root.rs:615). For every entry it creates, Extractor::entry calls mark_created (extract.rs:489), which inserts the entry's path into `created` and every ancestor not yet recorded into `ancestors` (extract.rs:1085-1097). The sets exist only for apply_opaque (extract.rs:947-970) and are dropped with the Extractor when extract_with returns, but nothing removes a path during the layer: an Apply-mode whiteout unlinks a file (extract.rs:907) or removes a directory tree (extract.rs:904-906, whose remove_dir_tree prunes only `dirs`, extract.rs:807), and both sets keep the deleted names. In a live root the stored path is physical: parent_dir resolves the parent with RootPath::resolve_dir_in, which follows symlinks inside the root (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/root.rs:286), reads its /proc/self/fd link through Live::physical (extract.rs:1176-1189), and appends each missing parent it creates itself (extract.rs:1036), parents the layer never lists. A publisher of a base image or a COPY --from image can therefore pair each create with a whiteout of the same name, so disk use stays flat and the disk exhaustion that bounds T15 bombs never stops the build, while memory grows. Estimates from source, not measured: (a) under a ~3.8 KB directory chain named with PAX paths, a create/whiteout pair costs about 10 KiB of decompressed tar for about 3.8 KiB retained; (b) once the layer has made a symlink `s` to that chain, plain 512-byte headers `s/f<i>` and `s/.wh.f<i>` store the same ~3.8 KiB physical path, about 3.7 times the decompressed bytes; (c) an entry `s/a<i>/x/x/.../f` whose parents are missing adds one physical path of about 3.8 KiB per missing level to `ancestors` (about 46 levels in a 100-byte name, about 125 with a ustar prefix), and one 512-byte whiteout `s/.wh.a<i>` removes the tree from disk, so roughly 0.2-0.5 MB is retained per KiB of decompressed tar. Retained memory can thus exceed the decompressed bytes by two orders of magnitude; amplification against downloaded bytes also depends on compression, which should be strong for such repetitive headers. Hash-set and allocator overhead adds roughly 40 bytes per retained path. No source-visible control caps entries, retained paths or decompressed bytes: rnk_layer::Decoder has no output cap, the rnk-sched memory gate (memory.rs:1-6, 23-24) only admits stage starts and always admits one when none runs, and ranikust sets no memory rlimit on itself. Calibration and scope: (1) for entries that survive, memory proportional to the root's entries is by design in kaniko mode (the walk keeps a Record per entry, walk.rs:205), so the distinct defect is memory kept for entries and parents the layer itself deleted, which contradicts ADR-0055 ('nothing in memory scales with a layer's size') and T15 ('fail cleanly on exhaustion'); (2) when the build runs a RUN on that image, the same publisher already controls the binaries that run, and RUN gets only RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE (child.rs:568-580), so its memory is bounded only by the outer cgroup. The extra exposure is therefore builds that never run the image's code: a COPY --from=<image> source, or a stage with only COPY on a base without a shell; (3) kaniko keeps a similar list (kaniko@44aa7ddc0 pkg/util/fs_util.go:226-288 appends every extracted name and never prunes it), but one lexical name per entry, with no ancestor set and no physical path, so variants (b) and (c) retain far more here than kaniko would for the same layer. This is separate from Q-056 (extension headers read whole but freed after each entry) and remains after extension headers are capped; variants (b) and (c) need no extension header after the chain. Overlay mode is not affected: Whiteouts::Overlay (and Literal) make mark_created return early (extract.rs:1086-1088), and `dirs` is pruned. If validated with a shared effect, it is a T15-class denial of service (threat-model section 8: Medium); when a memory cgroup confines the build, the effect is the build job's own OOM kill, which is hardening.
claimed_root_cause: Extractor.created and Extractor.ancestors (extract.rs:289-290) are filled by mark_created (extract.rs:1085-1097) for every created entry and pruned nowhere during a layer. The Apply-mode whiteout (extract.rs:904-907) and remove_dir_tree (extract.rs:807, which prunes only `dirs`) leave them as they are, so they record every name the layer ever created rather than the entries still present. No limit applies to entry count, retained bytes or decompressed bytes.

trace.description: The publisher-controlled compressed layer is wrapped in rnk_layer::Decoder, which caps neither output bytes nor entries. It is reached for a base layer on / through extract_base_layer (root.rs:579, 885-891, after Spooled::of verifies the digest and diff ID the publisher chose), for per-stage directories through extract_blob (stages.rs:424), and for a COPY --from image through Spooled::extract into a state-directory scratch directory when the root is / (root.rs:1102) or extract_blob into a keep-area directory elsewhere (root.rs:615).
extract_live(root, &mut decoder, ignore) is called; the diff ID is only checked after the whole tar is extracted.
Calls extract_with with Whiteouts::Apply and the ignore list. extract_with builds one Extractor with empty `created` and `ancestors` sets (extract.rs:204-212) that lives for the whole layer.
Iterates archive.entries() over the attacker-shaped tar with no limit on the number of entries.

After creating a directory, file, symlink or hardlink (device nodes and FIFOs are skipped earlier in a live root), the entry's path is passed to mark_created; in a live root it is the physical path from parent_dir, with symlinks in the root followed and missing parents appended.

self.created.insert(path) keeps the full path; the loop at line 1091 inserts every ancestor not yet in `ancestors`, one full path per new parent level. Nothing removes them until the Extractor is dropped at the end of the layer.

evidence.description: `created: HashSet<PathBuf>` and `ancestors` (line 290) are documented as 'entries this layer created, and their ancestors, which an opaque whiteout must not remove'. A grep finds no created.remove or ancestors.remove anywhere.

An Apply-mode whiteout unlinks the target, including one this layer just created, without removing it from `created`. A whiteout of a directory goes through remove_dir_tree (lines 904-906), which prunes only `dirs` (line 807).

apply_opaque is the only reader of the sets. It decides for entries that the deletion walk finds on disk, so a deleted path can never match and dropping it from `created` when it is unlinked would not change behaviour.

Live::physical builds the stored directory path from the /proc/self/fd link (read_fd_link, line 1198), so a parent reached through a short name and a symlink is stored at its full physical length, bounded by the kernel's ~4 KiB link limit, plus the entry name.

parent_dir creates every missing parent with mkdirat and pushes its name onto the physical path. These implicit parents never enter `dirs`, but mark_created adds each one to `ancestors` (line 1091), so a single entry adds one full path per missing level.

resolve_dir_in, which parent_dir and the Apply whiteout use for the entry's parent, follows symlinks inside the root, so a symlink the layer created lets short entry names land under a long directory chain.
Per-stage directories (kaniko mode on a host, outside a container) also extract every base layer through extract_blob, extract_checked and extract_live.

When the root is /, the layers of a COPY --from=<image> source are unpacked on first read into a scratch directory of the state directory through Spooled::extract, which calls extract_checked and extract_live. None of the image's code ever runs, so its publisher has no RUN through which to use memory.
On a root other than /, prepare_source extracts the layers of a COPY --from image into a keep-area directory with extract_blob, which also reaches extract_live.

The RUN child sets only RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE (line 579); its memory is bounded only by the outer cgroup. So a base-image publisher whose binaries run in a RUN can already use unbounded memory, which limits the extra exposure to builds that never run the image's code.

The memory gate only decides whether another stage may start, and it always admits a stage when none is running (lines 23-24). Cgroups are only read (ADR-0007), so nothing stops an extraction that is already running.

The kaniko walk keeps a Record per entry of the root for the next walk. Memory proportional to entries that survive is therefore by design, and the distinct defect is memory kept for entries and parents that were deleted.
Accepted ADR: 'Every pipeline uses fixed-size buffers; nothing in memory scales with a layer's size.' Paths kept for deleted entries scale with the layer's entry count and depth, not with the root.
T15 (A7, host memory included) names 'huge or very many files' and requires 'stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion'. Section 6 does not accept memory exhaustion by layer contents.
Section 8 rates denial of service from untrusted input with default settings (T15, T16) as Medium.
Q-056 (no bound for tar extension headers for now) is a separate memory cause that frees each header after its entry. It does not cover the per-entry sets, which remain after a header cap.

blockers: This run allows no target-controlled execution, so the memory retained per created-then-whited-out entry and per implicitly created parent, and the compressed bytes per pair that give the amplification against downloaded bytes, are estimates from source and were not observed.

Whether exhaustion affects anything beyond the build depends on deployment, which source does not show. ranikust only reads cgroups (ADR-0007) and sets no memory limit. Kaniko mode on / runs in a container, where a memory cgroup, if set, confines the OOM kill to the build job. Per-stage directories run as root on a host outside a container. There, whether a memory cgroup (a systemd slice or a CI runner cgroup) confines ranikust, its oom_score_adj, and which workloads share the host's memory are not visible in source.

For every deployment of kaniko mode with per-stage directories (root on a host, outside a container), record: the cgroup ranikust runs in (`cat /proc/<pid>/cgroup`); that cgroup's memory.max, memory.swap.max and memory.oom.group; ranikust's /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj compared with the co-located workloads'; and which other jobs share the host's memory. title: Base-layer tar extension headers (GNU long name/link, PAX 'x') are buffered whole in memory, so a small compressed layer can make ranikust allocate gigabytes
description: Every base layer ranikust extracts goes rnk_layer::Decoder -> rnk_rootfs Extractor::run -> tar 0.4.46 Archive::entries(): overlay mode (rnk-snapshot layer.rs extract_layer, from Overlay::base_layer / base_layer_from) and kaniko mode on / and with per-stage directories (kaniko/root.rs extract_checked -> extract_live). For an entry of type 'L' (GNU long name), 'K' (GNU long link) or 'x' (PAX local), tar's next_entry calls EntryFields::read_all, which read_to_end's the body into a Vec through Take(size), with size taken from the header (octal up to 8 GiB, base-256 beyond). ranikust adds no cap; no memory limit (RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_DATA or a memory cgroup) is set anywhere in the crates: only RLIMIT_CORE and RLIMIT_NOFILE are touched (rnk-sandbox), and rnk-sched only reads memory.max for scheduling. The decoder bounds only its own window (zstd 128 MiB, gzip 32 KiB) and not its output, so a highly compressible body (one repeated byte) of gigabytes fits in a blob of a few MiB with gzip (about 1:1000) and far less with zstd. The diff ID is compared only after extraction (layer.rs:130, root.rs:1013-1014), and the publisher sets it anyway. In kaniko mode on /, the spool step (root.rs:934) decompresses without parsing the tar, so it does not stop this. Lower-trust input: the base-image publisher of any image the Dockerfile names in FROM or COPY --from=<image>, or a tag later replaced. Peer controls checked: Rust's read_to_end grows with try_reserve, so an allocation the kernel refuses outright ends as a clean Error::Tar; but under overcommit or a memory cgroup the pages are committed as bytes arrive, and the kernel OOM-kills the process instead, which is not the 'fail cleanly on exhaustion' T15 requires. Store leftovers are removed at the next start (store.rs:377), so the effect does not persist. Calibration: kaniko and BuildKit read layers with Go archive/tar, which caps these headers at 1 MiB (maxSpecialFileSize, mirrored on ranikust's writer side by header.rs MAX_PAX_SIZE); ranikust's reader is less bounded than that baseline. Not excused: Q-056 ('no bound for now; revisit with fuzzing in Phase 6') is a deferral, not a threat-model section 6 accepted risk, and the behaviour contradicts T15 ('Stream instead of buffering') and ADR-0055 ('nothing in memory scales with a layer's size'); section 8 rates DoS from untrusted input with default settings (T15, T16) Medium. Scope of new exposure: when a RUN executes the base image's own binaries, the publisher already has code running as root that can use memory up to the outer cgroup (T15), so the incremental exposure is stages with no publisher-controlled RUN: COPY-only or FROM-only final stages (for example a distroless base plus COPY --from=builder) and COPY --from=<image>.
claimed_root_cause: Extractor::run (crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:305-306) hands the unbounded decompressed stream to tar 0.4.46 Archive::entries(). Its next_entry (tar-0.4.46 src/archive.rs:418,429,440) calls EntryFields::read_all (src/entry.rs:297-301), which read_to_end's the whole 'L', 'K' or 'x' body through Take(size) (src/archive.rs:360), so memory equals the size the layer declares and supplies. Neither rnk-layer's Decoder nor rnk-rootfs's extractor caps extension-header size (Q-056 deferral).

trace.scope: Overlay::base_layer (overlay mode, base layer blob from the store)
trace.description: The pulled blob of an image named by the Dockerfile, whose compressed digest matches the publisher's own manifest, is opened and passed to layer::extract_layer with the publisher-chosen diff ID.
The blob is wrapped in rnk_layer::Decoder::new.
zstd streaming decoder with libzstd's default 128 MiB window limit (gzip is MultiGzDecoder). Nothing limits how many bytes come out.
Hands every decompressed byte to the caller and hashes it for the diff ID; no output byte count is enforced.
extract_overlay(root, &mut decoder, &refs) parses the tar from the decoder; the diff ID is compared only afterwards (line 130).
tar::Archive::new(tar) over the decoder stream, with no Take or size limit around it.

Each step runs tar 0.4.46 next_entry; for an 'L', 'K' or 'x' header (tar src/archive.rs:418,429,440) it calls EntryFields::read_all (src/entry.rs:297-301), which read_to_end's the whole declared body into a Vec before ranikust's entry() sees anything.

evidence.description: Code comment (lines 338-339): 'Extension headers stay unbounded for now (Q-056).' Only GNU sparse entries are refused.
Design text (lines 116-118): 'GNU long names and PAX headers are read whole into memory by the tar crate, with no bound for now (Q-056, answered: revisit with fuzzing in Phase 6)'.
Q-056 answered 'no bound for now' and deferred to cargo fuzz in Phase 6: a deferral, not among the threat-model section 6 accepted risks.

T15 (decompression bombs) requires 'Stream instead of buffering; fail cleanly on exhaustion'. Line 202 rates DoS from untrusted input with default settings (T15, T16) Medium; section 6 (lines 100-161) does not accept this.
Accepted ADR: 'Every pipeline uses fixed-size buffers; nothing in memory scales with a layer's size.'
MAX_PAX_SIZE = 1 MiB, 'Largest PAX extended header Go's archive/tar reads (maxSpecialFileSize)': the writer side and the kaniko/BuildKit readers are bounded; ranikust's reader is not.
'Memory stays bounded whatever the blob holds' holds only for the decoder's window; its consumer buffers without limit.
Kaniko-mode sibling: extract_checked feeds the same Decoder into extract_live, which uses the same Archive::entries() loop. The spool check at line 934 decompresses but does not parse the tar.
tar = 0.4.46 (Cargo.lock:1812-1815), reading only. Its read_all caps only the preallocation (128 KiB), not the total read.
Store::open removes leftovers of a build that died, so an OOM kill leaves no persistent damage in the state directory; the effect is availability only.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run, so the peak RSS of extraction on a crafted 'L', 'K' or 'x' entry, the real compressed size of such a layer, and the termination mode were not observed: whether ranikust fails cleanly (std read_to_end's try_reserve returning OutOfMemory, mapped to Error::Tar) or is OOM-killed under overcommit or a memory cgroup decides whether T15's 'fail cleanly on exhaustion' is violated.

Whether the exhaustion reaches beyond the build is a deployment fact the source does not show: a memory cgroup on the build pod or runner confines it to the build, while an overlay-mode or per-stage-directory build on a host with no cgroup limit puts host memory (asset A7) and co-located workloads under pressure.

validation_plan.local: Run in the disposable VM (tier T2 lane, `just test-vm`) or as T0 non-root inside it; dummy data only, no network. (1) Add `extension_header_memory_is_bounded_*` tests to crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract/tests.rs using the existing Tar helper: a header from Tar::header(b"././@LongLink", EntryType::GNULongName, 0o644, 64 << 20) with set_cksum, then build the stream lazily so the test does not hold the body itself: Cursor(header bytes).chain(io::repeat(b'a').take(64 << 20)).chain(Cursor(an ordinary Tar::file("f", 0o644, b"x") entry plus two zero blocks)). Reset the peak first by writing "5" to /proc/self/clear_refs (Linux 4.0+; VmHWM is a per-process peak, so without the reset the second and third tests in one test process would show almost no growth and read as fixed), then read VmHWM from /proc/self/status, call extract(&f.root, stream, Whiteouts::Overlay), read VmHWM again. (2) Termination mode: in crates/rnk-snapshot/tests/layers.rs, with the existing snapshotter() helper, stream the same 'L' layer with a 3 GiB body through flate2 GzEncoder (Compression::best, written in 1 MiB chunks into a Vec) and its streamed sha256 as diff ID, then call s.base_layer_from(&id, gz.as_slice(), &[]); record the blob size (amplification) and run the test binary once under `prlimit --as=2147483648` (expect a clean Err if try_reserve catches the refusal) and once, as root in the VM only, under `systemd-run --scope -p MemoryMax=1G -p MemorySwapMax=0` (record exit status 137 and oom_kill in memory.events if killed, or a clean Err). Print the TempDir path before extracting (a killed process does not remove it), then open a Store on that state dir and confirm the temporary entry is removed. (3) For the zstd ratio, in crates/rnk-layer/tests/it/decoder.rs compress the 64 MiB stream with zstd::stream::encode_all(level 19), record the blob size, and decode it through rnk_layer::Decoder::new to check the diff ID.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, no probing: for each supported deployment (overlay mode on a CI host, kaniko mode on / in a Kubernetes pod or Docker container, per-stage directories on a host), record whether ranikust runs under a memory cgroup limit (memory.max of its cgroup), what else shares that cgroup or the host's memory, vm.overcommit_memory and swap. This settles whether exhaustion is confined to the build or reaches co-located workloads, and which termination mode users will see.

title: RUN --mount=type=cache bind is remounted through a second name lookup, so a symlinked target sends the nodev/ro remount to another mount and leaves the cache bind dev-capable (T18 bypass)
description: In the full sandbox (overlay mode, kaniko mode with per-stage directories), the child binds each RUN --mount directory onto the first openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS) resolution of its target (child.rs:661-666). It then drops that descriptor, resolves the same target string again (child.rs:669) and applies MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND|NODEV[|RDONLY] to whatever mount root the second lookup reaches (child.rs:670-674). The recursive nodev of the root (child.rs:392-398) ran before the bind existed, so the bind's nodev comes only from that remount; a bind otherwise keeps the source mount's flags, here the state directory's. Neither spec validation (spec.rs:348, absolute and clean only) nor the journal's ensure (journal.rs:183-235, which follows symlinks) refuses a symlinked target. Source-predicted attack, all under the Dockerfile author's control: (1) RUN --mount=type=cache,id=k,target=/x ln -s / /x/w; (2) RUN mkdir /t && ln -s /t /t/w && ln -s /t/w /c; (3) RUN --mount=type=cache,id=k,target=/c .... In step 3, ensure walks /c -> /t/w -> /t and accepts it. The first lookup ends at the root's /t, and the cache is bound there. The second lookup of /c enters /t, which is now the cache, follows the cache's w -> / and ends at the root bind's root. The root bind is a mount root, so the remount succeeds and the child goes on. The cache bind at /t keeps the state directory's flags: without nodev unless that filesystem is mounted nodev, and writable even when the mount asked for read-only. The RUN keeps CAP_MKNOD (caps.rs:19) in the initial user namespace, and ranikust installs no device cgroup (child.rs:384 relies on nodev instead). So `mknod /t/n b <maj> <min>` and an open of the node would give raw access to a host block device, which T18 (threat-model.md:95) and design/sandbox.md:131 ('Every bind is remounted nodev') say must not happen. The same lookup lets the author pick which earlier mount root gets the remount. Two variants follow from source and are unverified. With w -> /sys and a read-write cache, the sysfs mount would lose its MS_RDONLY. With w -> /dev/null, the read-only bind of the host's /dev/null would become writable, so chmod or chown could reach the host inode (T18, second clause). Scope corrections to the hunter's record: mount_secrets (child.rs:731-753) has the same code shape, but its own bind cannot make the two lookups differ, because the bind point is a regular file that a later lookup cannot traverse as a directory. Only a concurrent writer of a shared cache on the target's path (a RUN of a parallel stage) could, and then the remount sets ro, nosuid, nodev and noexec wherever it lands while the secret bind keeps its source tmpfs's nodev (child.rs:695), so no boundary effect follows; the same fix should still cover it. The heredoc /dev/pipes claim is not established: any re-routing of /dev through the fresh /dev tmpfs fails in the /dev re-resolution before populate_dev (child.rs:641-643) before pipes exists. Ignoring a read-only request is self-impact; the boundary effect is the device-node escape to the host, plus the sysfs and /dev variants.
claimed_root_cause: mount_one's ChildMount::Bind arm (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs:654-675) applies its security remount to a second name-based resolution of a target path that the RUN and the cache contents control. It does not apply the remount to the mount it just created. It never checks that the remounted mount is the new bind: there is no mount-id comparison (statx STATX_MNT_ID against the fd from the bind), and no open_tree(OPEN_TREE_CLONE) + mount_setattr(nodev[,rdonly]) on the detached tree before move_mount onto the first-resolved descriptor. The root's recursive nodev (child.rs:392-398) runs before these binds exist. Targets may be symlinks (spec.rs:348 and journal.rs:183-235 accept them). mount_secrets (child.rs:731-753) repeats the pattern; its regular-file bind cannot make the lookups diverge (only a concurrent writer of a shared cache on the target's path could), and its fixed ro/nosuid/nodev/noexec remount and nodev source tmpfs leave no boundary effect.

trace.description: A Dockerfile `RUN --mount=type=cache,id=k,target=/c` (Dockerfile author) becomes BindMount{source: <state>/caches/<key>, target: mount_target("/c") = "/c" (lexically cleaned only, mounts.rs:309-316), kind: Directory, read_only}
journal.ensure("/c") follows the root's symlinks /c -> /t/w -> /t (journal.rs:197-210) and accepts the target without a stub; the plan keeps the original string "/c" (plan.rs:214-219)
Remount flags = BIND|NODEV[|RDONLY] plus the source mount's statvfs flags (plan.rs:226); the bind itself carries no nodev
First openat2(IN_ROOT) lookup of /c ends at the root's /t; the cache directory is bound there (child.rs:662-666), keeping the state directory mount's flags
Second lookup of /c by name crosses into the new cache mount at /t, follows the cache's own w -> / and ends at the root bind's root (or /sys, /dev/null... per w)
MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND|NODEV[|RDONLY] is applied to that other mount root; the cache bind at /t keeps no nodev (and stays writable) when the RUN executes with CAP_MKNOD

evidence.description: Recursive nodev on the root's bind (mount_setattr AT_RECURSIVE, line 395) runs before the mount_one loop at line 427, so later binds are not covered
Comment 'Resolved again, it is the bind, not the directory under it' states the unverified assumption; nothing compares the mount reached with the new bind
resolve(): openat2 with RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS only; symlinks, including absolute ones inside the just-mounted cache, are followed and mount crossings are allowed (no NO_XDEV, no NO_SYMLINKS)
Mount targets are checked only for being absolute and clean and not '/'; a symlinked target is not refused
ensure follows symlink hops inside the root (up to MAX_SYMLINKS), so /c -> /t/w -> /t reaches the child
CAP_MKNOD (27) is in the kept Docker default set
Comment: Docker gets device protection from its device cgroup; ranikust relies on nodev alone (no device cgroup in rnk-sandbox)
T2 red-team test mknods in a RUN --mount bind and expects the open to fail only through the remount; its target is the direct path /cache (line 2858), never a symlinked one
T18: nodev on every RUN --mount bind is the control against device nodes a RUN creates with CAP_MKNOD; not listed among the accepted risks of section 6
Design invariant: 'Every bind is remounted nodev (ADR-0032)'
