blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run (there is no OS-enforced sandbox on the host, and the VM and T2c lanes have network). Two kernel facts decide the outcome and need real mounts as root in the disposable VM (T2). First, that the second openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT) crosses into the just-made cache mount and follows its absolute symlink to the root bind. Second, that MS_REMOUNT|MS_BIND then succeeds on the root bind's root, so the child does not fail.

Deployment conditions for the device-node impact. The state directory's filesystem must not be mounted nodev, because the bind inherits its flags. No device cgroup or BPF device policy may restrict the ranikust process: this holds on a plain host or in a privileged container or pod. A rootless user-namespace overlay mode is excluded, because mknod of devices needs CAP_MKNOD in the initial user namespace.

validation_plan.local: In the T2 VM (`just test-vm`; dummy data only), add an ignored T2 test next to red_team_no_mount_of_the_root_tree_lets_a_device_node_open (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:2783). Build it the same way: own thread, unshare(FS|NEWNS), every mount private, TestMounts on a tempdir, the root with the /usr bind and the bin/lib symlinks. First assert with statvfs that the tempdir's mount lacks ST_NODEV, or the test proves nothing. In the root, create directory t, symlink t/w -> /t and symlink c -> /t/w. In the host cache dir, create symlink w -> /. Case A: BindMount{source: cache, target: "/c", kind: Directory, read_only: true} with script `cat /proc/self/mountinfo; mknod /t/made c 1 3 && echo x > /t/made && echo OPENED; touch /t/rw && echo WROTE`. Char 1:3 is /dev/null, so no host disk is touched. If vulnerable, the RUN succeeds, OPENED and WROTE print, and mountinfo shows /t without nodev and / as ro (the remount landed on the root bind). If refuted, the child fails at Remount or ResolveTarget, or the open fails with EACCES. Case B: cache w -> /sys, read_only false, script `grep ' /sys ' /proc/self/mountinfo`: expected 'ro' if safe, 'rw' if the variant holds; do not write sysfs. Case C: cache w -> /dev/null, read_only false, script `grep ' /dev/null ' /proc/self/mountinfo`: 'ro' if safe, 'rw,nodev' if the variant holds; do not chmod. Control: target "/cache" directly (the existing test) must refuse the open and the write. Optional e2e in the same VM, overlay mode, --state-dir on the VM's ext4, output to a scratch tar, no push: FROM busybox; RUN --mount=type=cache,id=k,target=/x ln -s / /x/w; RUN mkdir /t && ln -s /t /t/w && ln -s /t/w /c; RUN --mount=type=cache,id=k,target=/c,ro sh -c 'grep -E " /t | / " /proc/self/mountinfo; mknod /t/n c 1 3 && echo x > /t/n && echo OPENED'.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner records, for each place ranikust runs in the full sandbox, three facts. First, the state directory's mount options (`findmnt -T <state-dir> -o TARGET,OPTIONS`: is nodev absent?). Second, whether a device cgroup or BPF device program restricts the ranikust process (cgroup v2: `bpftool cgroup show /sys/fs/cgroup/<ranikust cgroup>` shows a device program; privileged Docker or Kubernetes pods have none). Third, whether overlay mode runs as real root rather than in a rootless user namespace. The device-node impact needs no nodev, no device policy and real root.

title: A symlinked /proc in the stage root makes the full sandbox skip every read-only and masked /proc path (T17 bypass)
description: In Isolation::Full (overlay mode, and kaniko mode with per-stage directories) nothing requires /proc, /sys or /dev in the stage root to be ordinary directories. The parent's Journal::ensure follows symlinks inside the root to place stubs (journal.rs:179-235, called from spawner.rs:1142-1143), and the child's mount_one resolves the proc target with openat2(IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS), which follows symlinks (child.rs:593-606, 958-973). The child then mounts sysfs over /sys and the /dev tmpfs (child.rs:608-641), the /etc files and the RUN --mount binds, and only afterwards (child.rs:433) does protect_kernel_files re-resolve /proc/bus, /proc/fs, /proc/irq, /proc/sys, /proc/sysrq-trigger and the ten masked /proc paths by name; resolve_existing maps ENOENT to None (child.rs:988) and each path is skipped with `continue` (child.rs:789-791, 814-816). A root holding /proc -> /sys/up/realproc, /sys/up -> / and a directory /realproc (for example FROM scratch plus COPY of a context directory, whose symlinks are copied as symlinks, stage.rs:963; or a base-image layer in overlay mode, extract_overlay has no ignore list, extract.rs:158) gets procfs mounted at /realproc; the sysfs mount then hides /sys/up, every /proc/... lookup returns ENOENT, and none of the read-only or /proc masks is applied (only /sys/firmware and /sys/devices/virtual/powercap are still masked). The same works through /dev (/proc -> /dev/up/realproc, hidden by the /dev tmpfs) or a RUN --mount=type=cache target. After pivot_root the RUN (uid 0 in the initial user namespace, Docker's 14 capabilities, no user namespace) holds a procfs with writable /realproc/sys and /realproc/sysrq-trigger, which threat T17 says reach the host kernel (kernel/core_pattern, kernel/modprobe, sysrq) with uid 0 and no capability. No peer control was found: RunSpec::validate (spec.rs:313-393) only checks mount and secret targets for being absolute and clean, no code in rnk-builder, rnk-snapshot or rnk-rootfs checks that the root's /proc is a directory, the T17 smoke check (tests/smoke/lib.bash:13) uses an ordinary /proc, and runc, the ADR-0003 baseline, refuses to mount proc or sysfs on anything but an ordinary directory. The lower-trust Dockerfile author or base-image publisher controls the input and the effect crosses into the host kernel; threat-model section 6 and ADR-0003 accept only retained-capability and kernel-bug residuals, not this.
claimed_root_cause: protect_kernel_files (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs:787-848) re-resolves /proc/... by name from the root fd, through symlinks the image or a COPY controls, after later mounts (sysfs, the /dev tmpfs, RUN --mount binds) changed what those symlinks lead to, and resolve_existing (child.rs:977-993) treats any ENOENT as 'the kernel lacks this path'. The proc, sysfs and /dev targets themselves may be symlinks: resolve (child.rs:958-973) has no RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS, Journal::ensure (journal.rs:179-235) follows them, and RunSpec::validate (spec.rs:313-393) has no check. The masks are not applied relative to the proc mount just made (for example from an fd of the mount root), and nothing requires /proc and /sys to be ordinary directories as runc does.

trace.description: COPY of a context directory copies its entries into the stage root with symlinks kept as symlinks, so a Dockerfile author can place /proc -> /sys/up/realproc, /sys/up -> / and /realproc (FROM scratch avoids an existing /proc directory); in overlay mode a base-image layer can carry the same entries (extract_overlay, crates/rnk-rootfs/src/extract.rs:158, applies no ignore list)
A later RUN builds a RunSpec on that root and sets spec.isolation = b.cx.isolation, Isolation::Full in overlay mode and in kaniko mode with per-stage directories
Called for /proc, /sys, /dev from place (spawner.rs:1142-1143); symlinks on the way are followed inside the root, so the symlinked /proc is accepted and /realproc is used or stubbed
resolve(root, "/proc") with IN_ROOT|NO_MAGICLINKS follows /proc -> /sys/up/realproc -> /realproc, and proc is mounted there (nosuid, nodev, noexec, not read-only)
sysfs is mounted over /sys, hiding the root's /sys/up, the hop the /proc symlink goes through (the /dev tmpfs at line 624 does the same for a /dev/up hop)
protect_kernel_files runs only after every mount_one and mount_secrets
/proc/sys now resolves to /sys/up/realproc/sys inside sysfs, which has no 'up': ENOENT is returned as None

None means continue: /proc/sys, sysrq-trigger, irq, bus and fs are not bound read-only and kcore, keys, timer_list and the other /proc masks (line 814) are not applied; pivot_root follows (line 441) and the RUN execs with a writable procfs at /realproc

evidence.description: resolve uses ResolveFlags::IN_ROOT | NO_MAGICLINKS only: symlinks, a symlinked /proc included, are followed (resolve_existing uses the same flags at line 985)
Each READONLY_PATHS entry is skipped with `continue` when resolve_existing returns None; MASKED_PATHS likewise at line 814
mount_plan order: proc, sysfs, /dev, the three /etc files, then RUN --mount; protect_kernel_files comes after all of them (child.rs:430-433)
READONLY_PATHS and MASKED_PATHS (line 78) are absolute /proc/... and /sys/... names, resolved again from the root, not from the proc mount just made
ensure documents that symlinks on the way, dangling ones included, are followed inside the root so the stub lands where the mount resolves the target
RunSpec::validate checks mount and secret targets are absolute, clean and not /; nothing about /proc, /sys or /dev in the root being real directories
Design intent: 'A path the kernel lacks is skipped'; the code skips any ENOENT, including one caused by a symlink the image controls
T17: writing kernel/core_pattern, kernel/modprobe or /proc/sysrq-trigger needs uid 0 and no capability; the read-only and masked paths after mounting proc and sysfs are the control
extract_overlay takes no ignore list, so an overlay-mode base layer can carry a /proc symlink
The only T17 check greps for a read-only /proc/sys mount with an ordinary /proc; no test covers a symlinked /proc, /sys or /dev in the root

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run: whether the RUN reaches a writable procfs needs a root run of the full sandbox (namespaces, mounts, pivot_root), which only the disposable VM (T2) may host

Kernel behaviour is inferred from source, not observed: that openat2 RESOLVE_IN_ROOT from the root fd crosses into the freshly mounted sysfs (or /dev tmpfs) and returns ENOENT for /sys/up, and that the proc instance mounted at /realproc then accepts a uid-0 write under /realproc/sys

validation_plan.local: In the T2 VM only (`just test-vm`, dummy data, never on the host), add an #[ignore = "T2 ..."] test in crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs modelled on a_mount_below_the_root_is_nodev_in_the_run (spawner.rs:2630): its own thread, unshare(FS | NEWNS), every mount private, TestMounts on a tempdir, /usr bound read-only into root/usr with bin, lib, lib64, sbin symlinks to usr/<l>, Runner::new(&top.join("sandbox"), Some(RootEntry::PivotRoot)). Case A (sysfs hop): in the root create dirs realproc and sys, symlink sys/up -> /, symlink proc -> /sys/up/realproc. Case B (/dev hop): dirs realproc and dev, symlink dev/up -> /, symlink proc -> /dev/up/realproc. Control: a root with an ordinary proc directory. For each, run RunSpec /bin/sh -c 'grep -E " /realproc(/sys)? " /realproc/self/mountinfo; if [ -w /realproc/sys/kernel/hostname ]; then echo WRITABLE; fi; echo rnk-test > /realproc/sys/kernel/hostname && echo WROTE' (for the control use /proc instead of /realproc). kernel.hostname is per UTS namespace and the RUN has CLONE_NEWUTS, so the write touches only the RUN's own namespace; never write core_pattern, modprobe, sysrq-trigger or any other global sysctl. Expected if vulnerable: a proc line for /realproc, no read-only /realproc/sys line, and WRITABLE and WROTE printed; the control must print neither (EROFS). Also assert after the run that the journal removed every stub (root/realproc unchanged) and that no mount is left under the tempdir. A rejection: the RUN fails at Step::ResolveTarget or MountProc, or /realproc/sys is read-only.

title: A default Isolation::Full RUN runs with no syscall filter, so where the host allows it, it can create its own user namespace and hold capabilities over namespaces it makes
description: Source confirms the trace: a default RUN in overlay mode or kaniko mode with per-stage directories (Isolation::Full, host network) is cloned with NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC, gets no seccomp program (the only one, seccomp::userns_network, is built only for a --network=none RUN under --allow network.none-userns), has no no_new_privs, and execs with Docker's 14 capabilities. Where the host's own policy lets a process without CAP_SYS_ADMIN create a user namespace (no outer seccomp, unprivileged_userns_clone=1, no AppArmor userns restriction), the RUN can run unshare -Urn and hold CAP_NET_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_ADMIN over the network and mount namespaces it made, reaching nf_tables, xfrm, tc and rtnl-link module autoload. Docker's and BuildKit's default seccomp profiles refuse this without CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Refuted as a vulnerability: it is the accepted consequence of ADR-0003 (default isolation without seccomp; --seccomp is opt-in, Phase 3; kernel bugs reachable from RUN are the accepted residual for untrusted Dockerfiles built without hardening). It crosses no ranikust boundary by itself: the self-made namespaces give only kernel attack surface that the same host already gives every unprivileged process, and mount locking keeps the stage-root, /etc, /proc/sys and nodev mounts in place. What remains is a documentation-accuracy gap (threat-model section 6, sandbox.md Differences from Docker, the book), not a security finding.
claimed_root_cause: clone_flags (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1123-1137) never adds CLONE_NEWUSER for a Full RUN, and the only seccomp program is built only when hold_network is set (spawner.rs:1043-1054) and installed only when present (child.rs:470-472). There is no default profile, no no_new_privs and no --seccomp flag yet. The capability drop to Docker's 14 (caps.rs:7-22, child.rs:474) does not govern user-namespace creation, which the kernel allows without a capability where unprivileged user namespaces are enabled.

trace.description: A RUN instruction from the lower-trust Dockerfile is dispatched to run_command.
The RunSpec takes the build's isolation (Isolation::Full in overlay mode and kaniko mode with per-stage directories); line 783 sets the RUN's network, the host network by default.
Clone flags come from clone_flags(spec); hold_network stays false unless line 1020 sees a Full --network=none RUN and the probe picks NetMode::UserNs (the --allow network.none-userns path).
Full RUN: CLONE_NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC|SIGCHLD, plus CLONE_NEWNET only for --network=none; never CLONE_NEWUSER.
seccomp is Some(seccomp::userns_network()) only when hold_network is set; a default RUN gets None.
install_filter runs only when args.seccomp is Some, so a default RUN installs no filter.
drop_capabilities keeps Docker's 14 capabilities (no CAP_SYS_ADMIN); no no_new_privs is set anywhere on this path.

The RUN execs with no syscall filter; whether unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) succeeds is left to the host's user-namespace policy and any outer seccomp or AppArmor profile. Inside a self-made user namespace it holds capabilities only over namespaces it created, with the inherited mounts locked.

evidence.description: Accepted decision: default RUN isolation roughly equivalent to docker build, and users who build untrusted code tighten it with --seccomp and --userns. The default list (lines 32-36) has namespaces, pivot_root, the 14-capability drop and PR_SET_PDEATHSIG, and no seccomp; line 37 makes --seccomp an opt-in.
The ADR's problem statement names the accepted risk: a hostile Dockerfile could use a retained capability or a kernel bug to reach the host.
Accepted consequence: the host-safety risk remains real for users who build untrusted code without hardening; documentation carries that burden. Line 73 defers --seccomp and --userns to Phase 3.
Mode table, overlay as root: seccomp and user namespace are optional, and the stated strength is that a kernel bug or a retained capability crosses it.

Section 6 accepts that RUN runs as root in a sandbox about as strong as docker build, citing ADR-0003. Line 137 records keyrings as one Docker-profile gap until --seccomp; it does not list user-namespace creation, which is a documentation gap, not a narrower acceptance than ADR-0003.

T20 is scoped to the network namespace ranikust itself puts a RUN in under --allow network.none-userns (Modes column: overlay, with the flag). Refused by default refers to that mechanism, not to namespaces a RUN creates under the host's own user-namespace policy.

The ADR's concern is the surface handed to Dockerfiles on hosts that block unprivileged user namespaces; it treats hosts that allow them as already giving that surface. Line 111 (by default no RUN gains a capability it would not have under Docker) is a consequence of refusing option (c) by default, not a sandbox-wide invariant.
The CLONE_NEWUSER rule belongs to the opt-in filter for the flagged path, whose user namespace ranikust creates; the module doc (lines 1-2) scopes it to --allow network.none-userns.

Calibration: Docker's default.json gates unshare/clone3/setns on CAP_SYS_ADMIN and masks clone with 0x7E020000, including CLONE_NEWUSER; Podman's profile (line 144) allows unshare unconditionally. The divergence from Docker is the known effect of ADR-0003's opt-in seccomp.
Optional hardening lists --seccomp as opt-in. The Differences from Docker section (lines 236-248) omits the missing default filter; a docs-accuracy follow-up.
User documentation tells operators to build untrusted Dockerfiles in a disposable VM or a single-use container, as ADR-0003 requires documentation to carry the residual risk.

reason: The source trace is accurate, but the behaviour is the accepted consequence of ADR-0003, implemented as accepted. ADR-0003:28-37 makes the default RUN sandbox namespaces plus pivot_root plus the 14-capability drop, with seccomp only as an opt-in (--seccomp, Phase 3), and ADR-0003:12,50 and threat-model.md:58,104 accept that a kernel bug reachable from such a RUN crosses it for untrusted Dockerfiles built without hardening. The candidate itself concedes that no default seccomp is accepted. Its carve-out does not hold: T20 (threat-model.md:97, Modes: overlay, with the flag) and ADR-0033 concern a user-namespace-owned network namespace that ranikust creates and hands to a RUN, and ADR-0033:34-36 confines that concern to hosts that block unprivileged user namespaces. ADR-0033:111 is the consequence of refusing option (c) by default, not a sandbox-wide invariant. A namespace the RUN creates under the host's own policy grants no access to any ranikust-protected asset: it only exposes kernel attack surface (nf_tables, xfrm, tc, rtnl-link autoload) that the same host already gives every unprivileged process, and turning that into a boundary crossing needs a separate kernel bug, the residual ADR-0003 accepts. Mount locking on a copy into a less privileged user namespace keeps the stage-root bind (pivot_root or MS_MOVE), the /etc binds, read-only /proc/sys and the masked paths, and nodev in place (T5, T6, T17, T18), and the RUN gains no capability over namespaces ranikust owns. No crate Boundaries or rules.md invariant is contradicted. Residual non-security follow-up: threat-model section 6 (which names only keyrings), sandbox.md Differences from Docker and the book's about-docker-build wording should say that, until --seccomp, a default RUN may create user namespaces where the host allows them.

title: Full-sandbox RUN child chdirs to WORKDIR, and resolves exec candidates, through /proc/self/fd magic links while it still holds every ranikust directory descriptor
description: In Isolation::Full (overlay mode, and kaniko mode with per-stage directories), the RUN child is cloned on the rnk-sandbox-spawner thread of the ranikust process itself (spawner.rs:163) with clone_flags NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC(|NEWNET)|SIGCHLD and no CLONE_FILES (spawner.rs:363, 1123-1137), so it gets a copy of the whole process descriptor table. Directory descriptors in that copy that name directories outside the RUN root: Store.state, the O_PATH state directory (store.rs:302), and Context.root, the O_PATH host build context (source.rs:50), both held in Shared for the whole build (build.rs:85-86); the builder's stage RootPath, borrowed across sandbox.run (stage.rs:767-801); the RootPath Runner::prepare opens on spec.root_dir and moves into the Journal (spawner.rs:837, 908). The last two name the stage root as a mount of the build namespace, a different vfsmount from the child's pivoted bind, so '..' from them is not stopped by the child's root. In a parallel build, other stages' root descriptors open at the clone instant are copied too. Other inherited or child-opened descriptors are not directories: stdio, the error pipe, the stdio relay pipes, the netns descriptor, the outer /proc/self/stat file (ParentCheck, child.rs:357), the child's own root O_PATH descriptor (inside the root, closed at child.rs:461). Verified order in child::run and switch_user_and_exec: ParentCheck::open (357); death signal; optional setns; mounts made private; bind and nodev remount of the root; chdir(root_dir) (399) and O_PATH open of the root; mount_one for the plan, procfs of the new PID namespace at /proc first (427, plan.rs:196), so /proc is mounted BEFORE pivot_root; /dev with fd -> /proc/self/fd (plan.rs:59); secrets; masked paths; fchdir(root) (435); pivot_root (441) and umount2 DETACH (448), or MS_MOVE (456) and chroot (457); chdir('/') (460); drop(root) (461); sethostname; loopback; seccomp only for the netns-userns case (471), a deny list of setns, io_uring, user-namespace clone/unshare and socket options that does not filter chdir, openat or execve (seccomp.rs:197-230); drop_capabilities to Docker's 14, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE included (474); setsid (531); session keyring; chdir(workdir) by path (538) as uid 0; setgroups, setresgid, setresuid (543-557); chdir again by path only on EACCES (559); death signal; set_stdio (564); reset_process_state with close_range(3, ~0, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) (565 -> 1390-1393), which only marks; setrlimit; execve of each candidate (1484), moving on after ENOENT/ENOTDIR. No earlier close, no exec trampoline (execve runs the command directly), no seccomp rule, no getcwd or inside-root check, and no openat2 resolution of the workdir exists on this path; the sibling mount-target resolution does use RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS (child.rs:966). PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 (main.rs:101) does not apply because procfs fd links are checked against the task itself (same thread group). The workdir value is only lexically checked (spec.rs:316, 425-439): a WORKDIR instruction, a base image's config WorkingDir, a parent stage's config, or an image symlink such as /w -> /proc/self/fd/N reaches chdir as written; make_workdir resolves it in the build namespace where the stage root's /proc is a plain image directory, so it creates directories instead of refusing (stage.rs:1225). The exec candidates (plan.rs:271-287) are resolved the same way, and the loop skips ENOENT/ENOTDIR, so a PATH list of /proc/self/fd/N prefixes does not need the right number. The MS_MOVE + chroot fallback changes nothing here: it shares the descriptor table and the chdir, and a chroot does not bound a lookup that a magic link moved to another mount. Expected effect, unobserved in this run: the RUN command starts with its cwd on a build-namespace mount (the host's mounts, setup.rs:35-43, or the outer container's), where relative '..' paths reach the host or outer-container root, the state directory (A3) and credential files (A2), as uid 0 with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE; with USER set, the cwd is taken before setresuid. This is the runc CVE-2024-21626 pattern, which runc 1.1.12 (used by docker build) closed, so the accepted risk 'about as strong as docker build' (threat-model.md:104) does not cover it, and it contradicts T1 (WORKDIR under RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS) and T7 (an inherited descriptor must not open a path outside the root). Kaniko mode on a container's '/' (Isolation::Direct) is out of this record: its RUN already shares ranikust's root and the container is the accepted boundary. Fix: (1) in child::run, right after ParentCheck::open and before the first lookup of a root-relative or attacker-chosen path, really close every descriptor except err_w, the ParentCheck stat descriptor, the netns descriptor, the ChildStdio::Fd sources and the script memfd (close_range over the gaps of a sorted fixed-size keep array, no allocation, as close_all_but does for one descriptor); everything kept is a non-directory; (2) resolve the workdir with openat2(root, workdir, O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC, RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS) before pivot_root and fchdir to it afterwards (keeping the EACCES retry after setresuid); (3) as runc 1.1.12, after the chdir check with the raw getcwd syscall that the path does not start with '(unreachable)' and fail at Step::Workdir otherwise; (4) a lexical refusal of /proc or /dev/fd in RunSpec::validate alone is not enough (image symlinks bypass it); (5) update T7, T1 evidence and design/sandbox.md step 8 to cover lookups between clone and execve, and add the T2 regression tests of the validation plan.
claimed_root_cause: switch_user_and_exec resolves the workdir (chdir at child.rs:538, retry at 559) and the exec candidates (execve at child.rs:1484) with plain path lookups that follow procfs magic links, while the child still holds a copy of ranikust's whole descriptor table (clone without CLONE_FILES at spawner.rs:363, flags at 1123-1137), including O_PATH directory descriptors outside the RUN root (Store.state, Context.root, the stage root as a build-namespace mount). The fresh procfs at /proc (mounted before pivot_root) exposes them as /proc/self/fd/<n> and /dev/fd/<n>. Nothing closes inherited descriptors before these lookups (close_range at child.rs:1390-1393 only sets close-on-exec and runs after the chdir), nothing refuses magic links on this path (unlike resolve() at child.rs:958-973), and nothing checks after the chdir that the cwd is inside the root.

trace.description: A Dockerfile WORKDIR string from the lower-trust Dockerfile author is dispatched to Builder::workdir. The same value can come from a base image's config WorkingDir (stage.rs:367) or a parent stage's config (stage.rs:388), which never pass make_workdir.
An absolute WORKDIR is kept as written (edit.rs:354-355); ConfigEdit::validate has no case for Workdir (edit.rs:196).
The config WorkingDir is joined onto '/' unchanged, so '/proc/self/fd/<n>' or '/dev/fd/<n>' stays as is.
spec.workdir = workdir (taken at stage.rs:707). The builder's stage RootPath stays borrowed while b.cx.sandbox.run(spec) runs (stage.rs:801).
Only absolute_clean (spec.rs:425-439): absolute, no '.' or '..', no NUL. argv[0] is checked only for being empty and for NUL (spec.rs:317-325). Called from Runner::run at spawner.rs:745.
The RootPath opened on spec.root_dir (spawner.rs:837) is moved into the Journal and stays open across the clone: another O_PATH directory descriptor of the stage root as a build-namespace mount.
workdir becomes a CString in ChildArgs with no resolution in the root; the exec candidates come from plan::exec_candidates (plan.rs:271-287).

SYS_clone with clone_flags (spawner.rs:1123-1137) and no CLONE_FILES, on the spawner thread of the ranikust process (spawner.rs:163): the child copies every descriptor of the process, including the O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY RootPath descriptors (root.rs:190) of the state directory, the build context and the stage root.

procfs of the RUN's PID namespace is the first mount, made by mount_one (child.rs:427) before pivot_root; /dev/fd is a symlink to /proc/self/fd (plan.rs:59). /proc/self/fd/<n> becomes a magic link to the child's inherited descriptor n.

pivot_root then umount2 DETACH (child.rs:448), or MS_MOVE and chroot (child.rs:456-457); chdir('/') (460); drop of the child's own root descriptor (461). Seccomp is installed only for the netns-userns case (471) and does not filter chdir or execve; drop_capabilities (474) keeps Docker's 14 capabilities, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE included. No inherited descriptor is closed.

chdir(workdir) by path, as uid 0 before setresuid (child.rs:556), follows a /proc/self/fd/<n> magic link to the inherited directory on a build-namespace mount. The EACCES retry (559) is path-based too; no getcwd or inside-root check follows.
close_range(3, ~0, CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC) only marks descriptors; it runs after the chdir and closes them only inside a successful execve. The cwd taken through one of them stays.

execve(candidate) resolves each candidate while the inherited descriptors are still open and skips ENOENT/ENOTDIR (1486-1488). On success the RUN command starts with the cwd chosen above, which survives execve, on a build-namespace mount where '..' is not bounded by the process root.

evidence.description: chdir(workdir) by path; nothing closes inherited descriptors before it and no getcwd or inside-root check follows (the retry at 559 is by path too).
The only descriptor sweep of the RUN child passes CLOSE_RANGE_CLOEXEC (1393), marking rather than closing, and runs after the chdir.
Sibling control in the same child: mount targets are resolved with openat2 RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS (resolve, child.rs:958-973). WORKDIR and the exec candidates are not.
close_all_but really closes every other descriptor, but only the netns helper uses it; the RUN child has no such step.
Full-sandbox clone flags: NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC|SIGCHLD (plus NEWNET for --network=none), no CLONE_FILES.
The spawner is a std::thread of the ranikust process, so the cloned child copies the descriptor table every ranikust thread shares.
RootPath descriptors are O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC: close-on-exec acts only inside execve, so they are open during chdir and during execve's own path lookup.
Store.state is a RootPath on the host state directory, held for the store's lifetime (field at store.rs:251).
Context.root is a RootPath on the host build-context directory.
Shared holds the store (line 85) and the context (line 86) for the whole build, so both directory descriptors exist at every RUN clone.

The build mount namespace is unshare(CLONE_NEWNS) with '/' made a recursive slave (setup.rs:41-44): directories reached through inherited descriptors, and '..' above them, are the host's (or outer container's) file systems.
PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 is the only procfs restriction; it guards ranikust's /proc entries against other processes, not a task resolving its own /proc/self/fd links.
/dev/fd -> /proc/self/fd: a second spelling that passes RunSpec::validate.
An argv[0] containing '/' is the only candidate; otherwise each PATH entry is joined unchecked. Both are resolved by execve while the inherited descriptors are open.

make_workdir resolves the WORKDIR through RootPath in the build namespace, where the stage root's /proc is a plain image directory: it creates /proc/self/fd/<n> as directories rather than refusing a magic link.
The only seccomp filter the child installs (netns-userns case) denies setns, io_uring, user-namespace clone/unshare and some socket options; it does not touch chdir, openat or execve.
T1 puts WORKDIR under openat2(RESOLVE_IN_ROOT|RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS); the child's chdir does not apply it.

T7: an inherited ranikust descriptor must not open a path outside the root; the mitigation as built (close-on-exec, a /proc/self/fd listing after execve) leaves the window between clone and execve, which holds the chdir, open.
The accepted risk is a sandbox about as strong as docker build; runc since 1.1.12 closes leaked descriptors and checks the cwd after chdir (CVE-2024-21626), so this is not accepted.
Step 8 documents the chdir to WORKDIR before the close-on-exec pass.

Descriptor tests count descriptors only after execve: this one is Direct-only, and the sandboxed smoke check (tests/smoke/lib.bash:16) lists /proc/self/fd inside the RUN command; no Isolation::Full test uses a workdir or exec candidate through /proc/self/fd.

The smoke suite's T7 check (T1 rootless podman, T2 VM smoke) counts /proc/self/fd entries inside the RUN command, after execve has closed the close-on-exec descriptors; it cannot see a cwd taken through one of them before execve.

blockers: Run constraint: no target-controlled execution, no OS sandbox on this host, and no VM or T2c run in this audit. The decisive kernel behaviour is unobserved here: whether chdir through /proc/self/fd/<n> of the RUN's own fresh procfs, after pivot_root and the old-root detach (or MS_MOVE + chroot), to an O_PATH directory descriptor opened in the build namespace succeeds and leaves the cwd outside the new root with '..' climbing the build namespace's mount tree, as in runc CVE-2024-21626.

Not visible in source: the descriptor numbers of the directory descriptors (Store.state, Context.root, the builder's and the Journal's stage-root RootPaths, other stages' roots) at clone time in a real build. A wrong number in a WORKDIR fails that RUN at Step::Workdir; the exec-candidate variant skips ENOENT/ENOTDIR and does not depend on it.

Deployment fact outside source: whether an LSM profile (AppArmor or SELinux) confines ranikust or its RUN children on hosts that run overlay mode or kaniko mode with mounts, and the kernel versions in use.

validation_plan.local: Tier T2 in the disposable VM (just test-vm), ranikust at ed718fb, dummy data only; record uname -r. (a) Sandbox-level T2 test next to a_mount_below_the_root_is_nodev_in_the_run (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:2630), same set-up: own thread, unshare(FS|NEWNS), mounts private, TestMounts tempdir with root/ (read-only bind of /usr, bin/lib symlinks). Beside root/ create outside/ holding a dummy file rnk-v38-canary ('dummy'). The test opens outside/ with O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC (descriptor n) and keeps it open across runner.run. For Runner::new with Some(RootEntry::PivotRoot) and with Some(RootEntry::MoveMount), and for workdir /proc/self/fd/n and /dev/fd/n, run argv [/bin/sh, -c, 'if test -e rnk-v38-canary; then echo outside; else echo inside; fi > /verdict'], which writes only inside the root by absolute path. Secure: Error::Setup at Step::Workdir, or root/verdict reads 'inside'. Defect present: 'outside'. (b) Same set-up, workdir '/': put a dummy executable rnk-v38-probe in outside/ (a #! /bin/sh script that writes 'ran' to /verdict-exec, an absolute path inside the root; outside/ on an exec-capable file system) and run argv ['rnk-v38-probe'] with env PATH=/proc/self/fd/n:/usr/bin. Secure: Step::Exec with ENOENT and no root/verdict-exec. Defect present: root/verdict-exec reads 'ran'. (c) Descriptor inventory: as VM root, build FROM a dummy base image served by a loopback registry in the VM (ranikust pulls a base only from a registry, plain HTTP to loopback unasked; an OCI layout is an output only, --oci-layout-path) with 'RUN sleep 20' in overlay mode, state directory and context under a tempdir; while it sleeps, record ls -l /proc/<ranikust pid>/fd and note which entries are directories (state directory, context, stage roots) and their numbers. Read-only. (d) Builder-level e2e on the same dummy base: put a dummy file rnk-v38-canary in the state directory, then 'WORKDIR /proc/self/fd/<state-dir n from (c)>' and 'RUN if test -e rnk-v38-canary; then echo outside; else echo inside; fi > /verdict', output with --no-push --tar-path=<tempdir>/out.tar (there is no --tar flag, and without a destination --no-push is required, crates/ranikust/src/config.rs:280), read /verdict from the tar. Repeat with a dummy base whose image config WorkingDir is /proc/self/fd/<n> and no WORKDIR line, with a dummy base holding a symlink /w -> /proc/self/fd/<n> and WorkingDir /w (both pushed to that loopback registry), with 'FROM <stage>' of a parent stage whose WORKDIR is /proc/self/fd/<n> (stage.rs:388), and in kaniko mode with per-stage directories. Delete the VM afterwards. Keep (a), (b) and (d) as T2 regression tests after the fix; with the fix every case fails at Step::Workdir or Step::Exec or reports 'inside'.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on hosts that run overlay mode or kaniko mode with mounts (on a host or in a privileged container): record the kernel version and whether an AppArmor or SELinux profile confines ranikust or its RUN children. Neither is visible in source; either can change whether a cwd taken through an inherited descriptor takes effect, but not the source defect.

title: Full-mode non-root RUN is dumpable in the initial user namespace: a host account with its uid/gid can read its environ (env= secrets) and reach its root through /proc/<pid>
description: In overlay mode and kaniko mode off / (Isolation::Full), a RUN after USER runs with the Dockerfile's raw uid/gid in the initial user namespace (no CLONE_NEWUSER) and, after execve, is dumpable with an empty permitted capability set. Its host pid stays in the host /proc. A non-root host account whose fsuid/fsgid equal the RUN's ids would pass ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) [kernel behaviour, inferred, not observed] and could, while the RUN lives: read /proc/<pid>/environ, which holds every env= secret; read a secret file mounted with uid=<that uid>, write files of that uid or world-writable directories of the root being built, and write a cache mount owned by that uid, all through /proc/<pid>/root. The root-owned 0700 state directory is not traversed, because /proc/<pid>/root starts at the RUN's root. Setuid gain from image files is blocked: the mounts belong to another mount namespace, so the kernel treats them as nosuid. Variant (Isolation::Direct, kaniko mode on a container's /): no namespaces at all (spawner.rs:1125), so a non-root RUN is an ordinary dumpable process of the container. A host account with the same uid outside the container reads its environ (env= secrets are allowed there) the way it reads any process of a container without user-namespace remapping. Inside the container, the only processes with that uid are the RUN's own tree (one build per container, leftovers swept), and ranikust itself is not dumpable.
claimed_root_cause: The Full sandbox never creates a user namespace (spawner.rs:1123-1137 clone_flags), and switch_user_and_exec (child.rs:546-557) sets the Dockerfile USER's ids directly in the initial user namespace before execve (child.rs:1484). The kernel makes the exec'd image SUID_DUMP_USER when uid==euid and gid==egid. A non-root RUN has an empty permitted set after setresuid, so ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS), which Yama does not restrict for READ, admits any host process with the same fsuid/fsgid. PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0 covers only ranikust (main.rs:101).

trace.description: A RUN --mount=type=secret,env=NAME from the Dockerfile pushes the operator's --secret value into the RUN's environment (RunMounts.env). A file secret instead takes the mount's uid=/gid= (mounts.rs:426, default 0).
Secret variables are appended last to the RUN's env, which becomes spec.env at stage.rs:780.
spec.user is the Dockerfile USER from self.user() (stage.rs:762), resolved by rnk_rootfs::lookup_user.
The USER's uid and gid (spawner.rs:1071-1072) and supplementary gids go into ChildArgs as raw host ids, with no mapping.
The flags are NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC, plus NEWNET only for --network=none, and never CLONE_NEWUSER. In Isolation::Direct (spawner.rs:1125) the flags are SIGCHLD only.

set_thread_groups, set_thread_res_gid and set_thread_res_uid (child.rs:546-557) switch to the USER's ids in the initial user namespace. A non-root uid loses its permitted capabilities here (child.rs:1258-1263).

execve with envp carrying the env= secret. The new image runs with uid==euid, so the kernel would make it dumpable (SUID_DUMP_USER) and a same-fsuid/fsgid host process could open /proc/<pid>/environ and /proc/<pid>/root [inferred, not observed].

evidence.description: This accepted ADR records as a Bad consequence that, while a RUN runs as a non-root USER, a host user with the same uid can open /proc/<pid>/root and reach the build root past the private ancestor. It says Docker without userns-remap behaves the same, that overlay mode has it too, and that only user namespaces or nosuid close it. The candidate's root writes, uid= secret file read and cache-mount writes are all instances of that reach.

ADR-0050 supersedes ADR-0047 only in part, by moving the private chain to the 0700 state directory. It does not lift the accepted /proc/<pid>/root consequence, and the code still creates no user namespace.

Section 3 lists the trusted and lower-trust inputs: operator, Dockerfile and context, base images, registry responses, other builds sharing the store, and the kernel and outer runtime (trusted). It has no row for other local accounts on the build host.

Section 4 rates overlay root at about docker build with a root daemon and lists the user namespace as optional (not built: --userns is Phase 3). docker build without userns-remap runs a USER RUN under the same host uid, with BuildKit env= secrets in its environment.

T11 requires env= secrets to be 'a variable of that RUN alone, as BuildKit'. The code meets this: only the asking RUN gets the variable. T11 does not cover same-uid host processes reading that RUN's /proc.

Sandbox-escape scope is a RUN reaching more of the host than docker build allows under the same privileges. Credential-leak scope (line 52) is logs, layers, configs, caches, errors and another build's RUN environment, not same-uid host accounts. --userns is listed under Hardening as designed but not implemented (line 95).

Each Full RUN mounts a fresh proc in its own PID namespace (spawner.rs:1128), and its capabilities are cut to Docker's defaults, without CAP_SYS_ADMIN. So another build's RUN, the in-model co-tenant principal, cannot see or open this RUN's /proc entry.

The project already documents RUN processes as dumpable ('any other process of its uid that is dumpable, other RUN processes included'). Only ranikust is made non-dumpable (crates/ranikust/src/main.rs:101).

Direct variant: for kaniko mode without mounts, the boundary is the outer container only, and section 3 (line 47) trusts the outer container runtime. A host account reading a container process of the same uid is that runtime's property, the same for kaniko or any container without userns remapping.
T14 accepts that cache mounts are shared and writable by design. A write by a same-uid host account through /proc/<pid>/root falls under the ADR-0047 reach.

reason: Source supports the mechanism (no CLONE_NEWUSER, raw USER ids, dumpable exec'd image), but no in-model boundary is crossed and the residue is accepted. (1) The Dockerfile author picks USER and asks for the secret. Their RUN already holds the secret and shares the host network (ADR-0010), so exposing it to a same-uid account gives that principal nothing new. (2) Another build sharing the store, the only co-tenant principal in threat-model section 3, runs its RUN in its own PID namespace with a fresh proc and no CAP_SYS_ADMIN (spawner.rs:1128, child.rs:600). It cannot see this RUN's /proc entry. (3) The only actor left is a distinct non-root host account whose uid equals the USER's. Section 3 does not list it. Accepted ADR-0047:64-69 records that exactly this actor reaches a non-root RUN in overlay mode through /proc/<pid>/root, as Docker without userns-remap does, closed only by user namespaces (--userns, Phase 3). That covers the root writes (A6), uid= secret files and cache-mount writes (T14). /proc/<pid>/environ is gated by the same ptrace_may_access(PTRACE_MODE_READ_FSCREDS) check and has the same docker build/BuildKit parity, which is the bar SECURITY.md:48-54 and threat-model.md:58 set. It needs no new principal or mechanism, and T11's 'variable of that RUN alone' is met. The kernel facts in the blockers are not decisive: either way the result is accepted parity or no exposure. The Direct variant (spawner.rs:1125) is rejected for the same reason: the outer container is the stated boundary, the container runtime is trusted, and inside the container only the RUN's own tree shares its uid. A documentation follow-up, not a finding: ADR-0047 names only /proc/<pid>/root. Threat-model section 6 and SECURITY.md 'By design' could state that a non-root RUN's environ (env= secrets) and root are open to host accounts of its uid until --userns.

title: Journal replay at overlay and per-stage build start opens planted FIFOs and device nodes in sandbox/runs, blocking and read-write, as root; a Direct RUN can plant them on a state volume shared across modes
description: Overlay builds and per-stage kaniko builds replay the stub journals in <state>/sandbox/runs at start, twice: rnk_sandbox::probe (probe.rs:55, called at setup.rs:220 and 344) and Sandbox::start (spawner.rs:149, called at setup.rs:229 and 360). Each *.journal-new goes to remove_unlocked, which opens it O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW (journal.rs:494-497). Each *.journal goes to replay_one, which opens it O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW (journal.rs:513-516). Neither open has O_NONBLOCK or O_NOCTTY, and the type is not checked before the open. After flock, replay_locked checks only st_nlink (journal.rs:542) and calls read_to_end with no cap (journal.rs:546). A FIFO named *.journal-new therefore blocks the build in open(2) until some process opens it for writing. A FIFO named *.journal is opened read-write, so ranikust holds its own writer and read_to_end never sees EOF. A device node is opened read-write as root and read to EOF: /dev/zero-like nodes grow memory until the OOM killer acts, and a block node reads the whole disk into memory. Side effects of opening watchdog or tty nodes are possible. A journal whose replay fails stays in place (journal.rs:486), so every later start repeats the effect. Who can plant a journal: more than the state-directory owner principal. In kaniko mode on a container's / (Isolation::Direct, setup.rs:322-365), a RUN of the Dockerfile author runs as uid 0 on the same / with Docker's default capabilities (CAP_MKNOD and CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE included; mkfifo needs none), and the state directory is a plain path there. That run's store refuses neither a marked persistent store nor a non-empty directory: statedir.rs:191-196 accepts any regular .ranikust-state, and open_anonymous only warns that a RUN can read what the directory holds (store.rs:404-409). If that state directory is a volume or bind that a privileged container or the host also uses for overlay or per-stage builds, the RUN can mkdir sandbox/runs, add .ranikust-state if the volume is not yet a store, and mkfifo or mknod journal names. Nothing in kaniko mode on / removes them: Store::close only removes .ranikust-building. A later overlay or per-stage build on that volume accepts the directory (statedir.rs:196, store.rs:1253-1284), and Runner::new checks only that sandbox/ and runs/ are real directories (spawner.rs:686-687). Replay then runs as root in the privileged context. This contradicts the writer premise of the earlier covered unit on journal replay (h07-sandbox-journal, 'only principals already trusted with the state directory can plant one'). That unit concluded no lower-trust principal reaches sandbox/runs because a Full-mode RUN is pivoted and Direct-on-/ builds create no runs directory. ranikust creates none, but the Direct RUN can, and it is uid 0, the same uid as the state-directory owner that journal.rs:444 trusts. The unit's path-confinement results (O_NOFOLLOW, confined_root at journal.rs:747-763, PLACEABLE at journal.rs:58-68, remove_scratch through descriptors) still hold; only the file-type and size handling is exposed. The project's sibling openers already treat these planted types as hostile: lock::open (lock.rs:20-40) and read_building_marker (store.rs:1155-1183). No accepted risk covers this case. Threat-model section 6 accepts that a Direct RUN reads files mounted into the container, and it states 'Nothing of ranikust's state outlives a kaniko-mode build on /' (threat-model.md:128-129). The effect is conditional: it needs a deployment that shares one state volume between a default-capability container running kaniko mode on / and a privileged container or host running overlay or per-stage builds. The device variant also needs the volume not to be nodev on the opening side.
claimed_root_cause: journal::replay, remove_unlocked and replay_one (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/journal.rs:452-530) open entries of <state>/sandbox/runs by name with blocking flags that let a tty become the controlling terminal (no O_NONBLOCK, no O_NOCTTY), before any file-type check. replay_locked (journal.rs:533-547) checks only st_nlink and then calls read_to_end with no size cap. The trust premise at journal.rs:444 is 'not trusted further than its owner'. In kaniko mode on / the owner uid 0 includes the Dockerfile author's Direct RUN, and that mode accepts a marked or reusable state directory (statedir.rs:191-196, store.rs:404-409). The sibling controls in rnk-store (lock::open, read_building_marker) check the type on a non-blocking, no-follow descriptor before any I/O, and the journal opener does not.

trace.description: Kaniko mode on a container's / opens the state directory with Store::open_anonymous, and RUN runs Isolation::Direct (setup.rs:355, 364): uid 0 on the same / with Docker's default capabilities. The state directory, e.g. a volume at /var/lib/ranikust, is a writable path for that RUN, which can mkdir sandbox/runs, create .ranikust-state, mkfifo, and mknod (CAP_MKNOD).

A non-empty state directory, including a marked persistent store, is used with only a warning that a RUN can read what it holds. Store::close (store.rs:959-971) removes only .ranikust-building, so entries the RUN planted stay.

A later overlay or per-stage build on the same volume accepts the directory as soon as it holds a regular .ranikust-state; nothing below it (sandbox/) is inspected. Store::open's check_marker (store.rs:1253-1284) likewise accepts any regular marker.
Overlay set-up runs rnk_sandbox::probe(&sandbox_dir) as root right after Store::open, then Sandbox::start at setup.rs:229. Per-stage kaniko does the same at setup.rs:344 and 360.
journal::replay(runner.runs_dir(), runner.state_dir(), None). Runner::new (spawner.rs:686-687) checks only that sandbox/ and runs/ are real directories, not their owner or contents.

Every *.journal-new goes to remove_unlocked, which opens it with read(true) and O_NOFOLLOW only (journal.rs:494-497). On a FIFO, open(2) blocks until a writer appears; a device node is opened as root. It then flocks the entry and unlinks it.
Every *.journal is opened read(true).write(true) with O_NOFOLLOW only: O_RDWR, blocking, no O_NOCTTY, no type check. It is then flocked non-blocking (journal.rs:518).

After an fstat that checks only st_nlink (journal.rs:542), read_to_end runs on the descriptor with no size cap. On a FIFO that ranikust itself holds open for writing it never returns. On a device it reads until EOF or an error. On an error the journal is left in place with a warning (journal.rs:486), so the effect repeats at every start.

evidence.description: remove_unlocked: File::options().read(true).custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW).open(path). No O_NONBLOCK and no type check before the open.
replay_one: read(true).write(true).custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW).open(path). O_RDWR and blocking, with no O_NOCTTY.
replay_locked checks only st_nlink == 0 after fstat, never the file type, then calls read_to_end with no limit at line 546.

Doc comment: 'The state directory is not trusted further than its owner'. Planted journals are in the design's model for path effects (PLACEABLE at :56-68, the confined root at :747-763, commit a7bebf4 'do not trust the state directory as root'). In kaniko mode on /, the owner uid 0 includes the Direct RUN.
Sibling control: lock files refuse anything but a regular file before I/O because 'a planted FIFO would block every build in open, and a device node would be opened as root' (lock.rs:22-40).
Sibling control: read_building_marker opens with RDONLY|NOFOLLOW|NONBLOCK|NOCTTY, checks the type with fstat (store.rs:1172-1175) and reads at most 256 bytes (store.rs:1177).

open_anonymous: a non-empty state directory is only warned about ('a RUN can read what it holds'). The doc comment at store.rs:339-340 says anything else there is used as is. No refusal of a marked persistent store in kaniko mode on /.
check_contents accepts any directory holding a regular .ranikust-state (statedir.rs:191-196), whatever the mode, and a root Direct RUN can create that file.

Sandbox::start replays journals again: start_inner calls journal::replay(&runner.runs_dir, ...). Kaniko mode on / uses start_direct (spawner.rs:136-145) and never replays, so the effect lands only on a later overlay or per-stage build.

Accepted risks, section 6: 'Nothing of ranikust's state outlives a kaniko-mode build on /'. This is contradicted when the state directory is a persistent volume. Section 6 accepts reads of files mounted into the container, not writes that a privileged build later trusts.

For kaniko mode on /, 'A volume at /var/lib/ranikust works too, one per container: a second build on a state directory in use is refused' (how-it-builds.md:140-142), which reads as a rule against concurrent use. setup.rs:246-247 advises '-v ranikust-state:/var/lib/ranikust' for overlay mode in a container. No document forbids reusing one volume, one build after another, across the two modes.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run (no OS-enforced sandbox; the VM and T2c lanes have network), so neither the hang nor the device open was observed.

Deployment fact: whether operators mount one ranikust state volume (a Docker named volume, a PVC, or a hostPath or bind of the host's /var/lib/ranikust) into both a default-capability container running kaniko mode on / and a privileged container or host running overlay or per-stage kaniko builds. Without such sharing, no lower-trust principal reaches sandbox/runs, and the earlier unit's conclusion stands.

Runtime fact for the device variant only: whether mknod on the volume succeeds in the default container, and whether the volume is mounted nodev on the opening side (privileged container or host). The FIFO variant needs no capability or mount option.

Runtime fact for the *.journal FIFO variant only: whether flock(2) succeeds on a FIFO opened O_RDWR, which that path needs before read_to_end. The *.journal-new path blocks in open(2) before any flock.

validation_plan.local: T0 (no root, dummy data): add #[cfg(test)] tests in crates/rnk-sandbox/src/journal.rs. Test 1 creates <tmp>/sandbox/runs and makes runs/x.journal-new a FIFO (rustix::fs::mknodat with FileType::Fifo, mode 0600; no privilege needed). It calls replay(&runs, &tmp, None) on a spawned thread that sends its result on an mpsc channel, and waits with recv_timeout(5 s). Expected today: Timeout, the thread blocked in open(2). Then it releases the thread by opening the FIFO O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK, which succeeds while a reader waits in open, joins it, and checks that x.journal-new is gone. Test 2 does the same with runs/y.journal as a FIFO. Expected today: Timeout. It must not join that thread: replay_one holds the FIFO's only writer through its own O_RDWR descriptor, so nothing makes read_to_end return. The test ends and the test process exits with the thread still blocked. Run both under 'timeout 60 cargo test -p rnk-sandbox journal::' as a guard. After a fix (O_NONBLOCK|O_NOCTTY, an fstat S_ISREG check before any I/O, and a capped read, as in read_building_marker), both calls return within the timeout and leave or remove the entry with a warning. T2 (disposable VM, 'just test-vm', rootful Docker, dummy image, output to a tar in scratch, no push): (1) docker volume create rnkv. (2) In a default container (no --privileged) with -v rnkv:/var/lib/ranikust, build in kaniko mode on / a Dockerfile whose RUN is 'mkdir -p /var/lib/ranikust/sandbox/runs && touch /var/lib/ranikust/.ranikust-state && mkfifo /var/lib/ranikust/sandbox/runs/f.journal-new'. Expect the build to succeed with a warning only, and the FIFO to remain in /var/lib/docker/volumes/rnkv/_data/sandbox/runs. (3) Start ranikust --mode=overlay in a detached --privileged container (docker run -d) with -v rnkv:/var/lib/ranikust. After 60 s, expect the process still in set-up with nothing pulled, and /proc/<pid>/wchan or /proc/<pid>/stack (root in the VM) showing a FIFO open wait. Then docker kill the container. That sends SIGKILL, which is needed because no SIGTERM handler exists during set-up (the only one is installed when the build starts, build.rs:918), so a SIGTERM to a ranikust that is the container's PID 1 is ignored. (4) Remove f.journal-new from the VM side. Then repeat step (2) with a RUN that plants only 'mknod /var/lib/ranikust/sandbox/runs/d.journal c 1 3'. A separate build keeps readdir order from consuming the node during step (3). Record findmnt -no OPTIONS for the volume inside that container. (5) Run the overlay build again in a --privileged container under 'strace -f -e trace=openat,flock,read'. Expect openat(.../d.journal, O_RDWR|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC) to return a descriptor on a character device, and d.journal to be gone after start-up: opened, read to EOF and unlinked as root. Record findmnt -no OPTIONS on this side. Stop there: use no device node other than c 1 3 (/dev/null). The T2c lane is acceptable only if it permits a --privileged container, and only with c 1 3.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: list the CI or cluster configurations that mount one ranikust state volume (Docker named volume such as ranikust-state, a PVC, or a hostPath or bind of /var/lib/ranikust) into both unprivileged build containers (kaniko mode on /) and privileged containers or host builds (overlay or per-stage kaniko). For each, record whether the mount is nodev on the privileged or host side, and whether untrusted Dockerfiles run in the unprivileged containers.

title: RUN --network=none leaves AF_VSOCK open, a host/guest transport that network namespaces do not isolate
description: The candidate says a RUN under --network=none (the operator's flag or a Dockerfile RUN --network=none) can open socket(AF_VSOCK) and reach vsock peers outside its network namespace: the hypervisor (CID 2), other guests on a vhost-vsock host, vsock_loopback services, hv_sock. The source trace is accurate. On the NetMode::Clone path (spawner.rs:1025) no seccomp filter is installed. On the ADR-0033 user-namespace path, the filter's socket branch refuses only AF_KEY and filters only AF_NETLINK (seccomp.rs:245-250). Nothing in rnk-sandbox refuses AF_VSOCK, and the CLI has no --seccomp flag. Refuted as a vulnerability for three reasons. (1) --network=none is implemented exactly as decided: ADR-0010:30 and the Network::None contract (spec.rs:16) both say a new, empty network namespace with only lo up. In Docker and BuildKit, --network=none is also just a network namespace. Their AF_VSOCK block comes from the default seccomp profile (buildkit@cd8ee24 vendor/github.com/moby/profiles/seccomp/default_linux.go: AF_VSOCK is commented out of allowedSocketDomains), not from the network mode. (2) Accepted ADR-0003 decides that the default RUN isolation has no seccomp profile. Its defaults are namespaces, pivot_root, Docker's 14 capabilities and PDEATHSIG; Docker's profile is the opt-in --seccomp switch planned for Phase 3, and ADR-0003 explicitly accepts that untrusted builds without hardening keep that risk. Threat-model section 4 lists seccomp as optional for overlay root, and section 6 accepts the ADR-0003 sandbox. ADR-0033 explicitly leaves the Clone path without a filter ('as before, no filter'; 'environments that already had CAP_NET_ADMIN behave as before, without the filter'). It scopes its filter to interfaces that CAP_NET_ADMIN over the namespace opens (T20). AF_VSOCK needs no capability, so it is outside that scope. (3) vsock reach does not depend on --network=none: every default-network RUN has it too, together with the host network that ADR-0010 and section 6 accept. A Dockerfile that writes RUN --network=none itself only restricts its own RUN. What remains is a documentation-precision hardening note, not a code/ADR mismatch. The section 6 'Until --seccomp' bullet (threat-model.md:137-139) names only keyrings among the Docker-profile-only denials the default sandbox lacks. AF_VSOCK, and AF_ALG, are further ones. They could be named there and in ADR-0010's consequences, or refused cheaply as hardening.
claimed_root_cause: RUN --network=none relies only on CLONE_NEWNET (or setns into the helper's namespace). The only seccomp filter, installed on the ADR-0033 path alone, checks socket() for AF_KEY and AF_NETLINK and allows every other family; the NetMode::Clone path has no filter. So a socket family the kernel does not scope to a network namespace (AF_VSOCK) stays usable.

trace.description: run_network (stage.rs:1161-1172) resolves a Dockerfile RUN --network=none, or a default-network RUN under the operator's --network=none, to Network::None.
spec.network = network hands Network::None to rnk-sandbox.
On NetMode::Clone (the process has CAP_NET_ADMIN), only loopback = true is set. A seccomp filter is built only when hold_network is set (line 1045), that is, on the ADR-0033 user-namespace path.
CLONE_NEWNET is the whole network isolation on the Clone path, as ADR-0010 decides.
The child installs a filter only when args.seccomp is Some. Otherwise the RUN execs with no syscall filter (the ADR-0003 default).
socket(): AF_KEY is refused (line 248) and AF_NETLINK goes to the protocol check. Every other family jumps to allow, so socket(AF_VSOCK=40) is not refused on either path.

evidence.description: The socket branch loads arg0 and compares it only with AF_KEY (line 248) and AF_NETLINK (line 250). Every other family is allowed, which confirms the trace.
seccomp is Some only when hold_network is set. The NetMode::Clone path runs without a filter, which confirms the trace.
The decided contract of --network=none is a new, empty network namespace (loopback only). The code gives exactly that.
Network::None is documented as 'A new, empty network namespace with only the loopback interface up'. That is an interface statement, not a promise that every non-namespaced address family is closed.
Accepted decision: the Docker seccomp profile, the only control that blocks AF_VSOCK in Docker and BuildKit, is the opt-in --seccomp=default switch. The defaults (lines 31-36) contain no seccomp.
ADR-0003 explicitly accepts that the host-safety risk stays real for users who build untrusted code without hardening. Line 74: --seccomp lands in Phase 3.

Root on a host, --privileged and rootless podman get the clone's own namespace 'as before, no filter'. Line 125 repeats it as a Neutral consequence. The missing filter on the Clone path is the accepted decision.

The ADR-0033 filter is scoped to interfaces that CAP_NET_ADMIN over the user-namespace-owned netns opens (T20). AF_VSOCK needs no capability and is outside that scope, so allowing it does not contradict the filter's stated purpose.
Mode table: overlay root is separated by namespaces, pivot_root, Docker's 14 capabilities and PDEATHSIG, with 'optional seccomp'.
Section 6 accepts the RUN sandbox as decided by ADR-0003. Section 6 (lines 140-149) also accepts that default-network RUNs reach host services, which already includes vsock.
The 'Until --seccomp (Phase 3)' bullet names only uid 0's keyrings among the Docker-profile-only denials. The AF_VSOCK and AF_ALG gaps are not named (documentation-precision note).
The only seccomp mention in the CLI is the network.none-userns entitlement doc. --seccomp is not implemented yet, consistent with ADR-0003's Phase 3 schedule.

reason: The trace is accurate: no filter refuses socket(AF_VSOCK). But the code implements the accepted decisions exactly. ADR-0010 and spec.rs:16 define --network=none as a new, empty network namespace with lo up. ADR-0003 makes Docker's seccomp profile, the only control that blocks AF_VSOCK in Docker and BuildKit (their --network=none does not), an opt-in Phase 3 switch and accepts the unhardened default. ADR-0033 explicitly leaves the Clone path without a filter and scopes its own filter to CAP_NET_ADMIN-gated interfaces, which AF_VSOCK is not. vsock reach is the same for every default-network RUN, whose host network is accepted, and a Dockerfile's own RUN --network=none is self-restriction. No stated invariant is contradicted. The remaining item is a docs hardening note: name AF_VSOCK (and AF_ALG) beside keyrings in threat-model.md:137-139, or refuse AF_VSOCK cheaply.

title: Default full-sandbox RUN shares ranikust's network namespace as an initial-userns uid, so it can connect to abstract Unix sockets of that namespace with its own peer uid (accepted by ADR-0010 and threat-model section 6)
description: In overlay mode and in kaniko mode with per-stage directories, a RUN without --network=none gets no network namespace of its own (clone_flags adds CLONE_NEWNET only for Network::None) and no user namespace when ranikust runs as real root. Abstract AF_UNIX names are scoped by network namespace, so such a RUN can list (/proc/net/unix) and connect to the abstract sockets of the namespace ranikust runs in (the host's when ranikust runs directly on a host), and SO_PEERCRED reports the RUN's real uid (0 by default, or the Dockerfile USER's uid). Concurrent builds on one host likewise share loopback and the abstract namespace. The source trace is accurate, but this is the documented, accepted default: ADR-0010 decides that RUN shares ranikust's network namespace and 'reaches what ranikust itself can reach', explicitly rejecting Docker's per-RUN bridged network; threat-model section 6 accepts that RUN 'can reach services that listen on the host'; ADR-0003 and SECURITY.md accept that RUN runs as root with a default isolation of mount, PID, UTS and IPC namespaces only, with --userns and --network=none as the opt-in hardening for untrusted Dockerfiles. The code implements exactly that and a unit test pins it.
claimed_root_cause: clone_flags (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/spawner.rs:1123-1137) adds CLONE_NEWNET only for Network::None and never CLONE_NEWUSER, while --network defaults to host (crates/ranikust/src/cli.rs:379) and the build process unshares only CLONE_NEWNS (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:35). A default Full RUN therefore shares ranikust's netns-scoped abstract AF_UNIX namespace and loopback, with a peer credential of an initial-user-namespace uid (0, or the Dockerfile USER's uid set at crates/rnk-sandbox/src/child.rs:556).

trace.description: --network defaults to Network::Host; the RUN commands come from the lower-trust Dockerfile author.
The RUN's network is computed by run_network from the Dockerfile's RUN --network and the build's network.
A RUN without --network (DfNetwork::Default) gets the build's network, Network::Host by default.
The build process unshares only CLONE_NEWNS; it stays in its own user and network namespaces (the initial ones when ranikust runs as root on a host).
The RUN child's clone flags come from clone_flags(spec).
Isolation::Full sets NEWNS|NEWPID|NEWUTS|NEWIPC and adds CLONE_NEWNET only when spec.network == Network::None; never CLONE_NEWUSER.
setresuid to the Dockerfile USER's uid (0 by default) in ranikust's user namespace: the uid SO_PEERCRED reports to a listener.
The RUN is cloned into ranikust's network namespace; a connect(2) to an abstract AF_UNIX name of that namespace reaches its listener with the RUN's real uid as peer credential.

evidence.description: Accepted decision: by default no network namespace is created for RUN; 'it reaches what ranikust itself can reach'. Lines 11-19 considered and rejected Docker's per-RUN bridged network; lines 36-37 record reaching host services as an accepted consequence.

Section 6 accepted risk (lines 140-149): RUN shares the host network by default and 'can reach services that listen on the host'; mitigation is outside ranikust or --network=none. An abstract-socket daemon is such a service in the shared network namespace.
T11 already reasons that 'a RUN shares the host network namespace and could sniff lo or serve the port', covering the concurrent-build squatting variant.
Overlay-root boundary is 'about docker build with a root daemon' with an optional user namespace: RUN as real uid 0 (hence peer uid 0) is the stated default.
Default isolation is enumerated as mount, PID, UTS and IPC namespaces (no network, no user namespace); line 28-30 make --userns the opt-in for untrusted code.
'By design' (not vulnerabilities): RUN shares the host network unless --network=none is given; line 63: RUN runs as root and can do whatever root can do inside its sandbox.
The 'shared abstract Unix sockets' residual is listed for a not-built hardened bare chroot between sibling stages on a container's /, not as an invariant of the full sandbox's network.
Unit test clone_flags_follow_isolation_and_network pins that default Full flags lack CLONE_NEWNET: the code implements the accepted decision.
Network::Host is documented as 'Share the host's network namespace (the default)', citing ADR-0010.

reason: The source trace is correct, but the behaviour is explicitly accepted and implemented as accepted. ADR-0010 (accepted) decides that a default RUN shares the network namespace ranikust runs in and 'reaches what ranikust itself can reach', after rejecting Docker's per-RUN bridged network; threat-model section 6 (lines 140-149) and SECURITY.md 'By design' (line 84) accept that RUN can reach services listening on the host. The abstract AF_UNIX namespace is a property of that network namespace, so reaching abstract-socket daemons is inherent in the accepted decision, and the peer uid they see is the RUN's real uid, which ADR-0003, threat-model.md:58 and SECURITY.md:63 accept as root with no user namespace by default (--userns and --network=none are the documented opt-ins). T11 (threat-model.md:88) already accepts that a RUN on the shared network can serve or sniff loopback ports, which covers the concurrent-build variant. ADR-0060:55-60 lists shared abstract sockets only as a residual of a not-built sibling-stage chroot design, not as an invariant of the full sandbox. No threat-model row, ADR or crate Boundaries section requires a default RUN to have its own network or user namespace, so nothing is contradicted.

title: The kaniko-mode walk keeps a full path for every directory and changed entry with no PATH_MAX bound, but only a RUN can give it a deeper tree, so the quadratic memory is self-impact
description: The source trace is accurate. Ctx::dir_entries builds each entry's full relative path (walk.rs:671-676). It keeps that path in DirOut.path for every directory (walk.rs:661-664, 716-719, child copy at :769) and in Changed.path for every added or modified entry (walk.rs:697-703). All of them are held until Walker::run sorts the changed list (:451) and Tree::build indexes the directories (:483, tree.rs:79). Nothing bounds the length. A D-level chain of n-byte names therefore retains about (n+1)*D^2 bytes, for example about 9 GiB at D=6000 and n=255, and the export later refuses every path past PATH_MAX anyway: pin_same (kaniko/export.rs:279-280) pins each path with one openat2. The overlay exporter refuses such paths up front (export.rs:237, 600-609). Still, no boundary is crossed. In kaniko mode, only a RUN process (the Dockerfile author's command or code it runs) can put a tree deeper than about PATH_MAX into a stage root. That tree then travels by RUN or by FROM/COPY --from of a RUN-made stage. Layers are unpacked by extract_live, the context walk opens directories by full path, and both are bounded. The same RUN process can already use unbounded memory in the same cgroup as the builder: ranikust sets only RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE, and by accepted design (ADR-0003, T15) RUN exhaustion is bounded only by the outer cgroup. The walk grants no new capability. Its only distinct effect is that the attacker's own build, which already fails with ENAMETOOLONG at the export, aborts or is OOM-killed instead. This is a hardening gap: cap the path at PATH_MAX as export.rs:child does.
claimed_root_cause: Ctx::dir_entries (crates/rnk-snapshot/src/kaniko/walk.rs:653-721) builds and keeps a full relative path for every directory (DirOut.path) and every changed entry (Changed.path) with no length bound, although the kaniko export that consumes the diff pins each path with a single openat2 (kaniko/export.rs:279-280, RootPath::pin at rnk-rootfs root.rs:348-359) and so cannot handle paths longer than PATH_MAX; the overlay exporter enforces that bound before buffering (export.rs:600-609).

trace.description: After a RUN of a stage whose layers are needed, diff_in walks the stage root the RUN process filled; the RUN process (Dockerfile author or code it runs) is the only principal that can make a tree deeper than about PATH_MAX there.
child_path is rebuilt as the parent's full path, '/', and the name for every entry read from getdents64, with no length check.
Every added or modified entry (every new directory and file of the RUN) keeps Changed { path: full path }, appended to ctx.changed and held until the walk ends.
Each subdirectory's spawned task receives its own copy of the full path, which becomes that directory's DirOut.path (walk.rs:661-664).
Every directory's DirOut, with its full path, is pushed into ctx.dirs and kept until the walk ends.

All DirOut paths and the sorted changed list (walk.rs:451) are alive together while Tree::build runs; the peak is the sum of all path lengths, about (n+1)*D^2 bytes for a D-level chain of n-byte names, inside the builder process.

evidence.description: a_tree_deeper_than_path_max_is_walked asserts a changed path over 4096 bytes is walked (30 levels of 200-byte names); the walk is depth-unbounded by design (docs/design/kaniko-mode.md:271).

pin_same, called by make_entry (export.rs:187) for each changed path, pins it with root.pin(p), a single openat2 of the whole path (rnk-rootfs root.rs:348-359), so a path past PATH_MAX fails the export with ENAMETOOLONG; the build fails regardless of the walk's memory.
The overlay exporter's PATH_MAX (4095) bound, enforced by child() at export.rs:600-609 before any entry is buffered; the kaniko walk lacks the same bound (hardening parity).

The only limits ranikust gives a RUN are RLIMIT_NOFILE and RLIMIT_CORE (set in child.rs:572 and :579); no memory cgroup or RLIMIT_AS, so the RUN process that makes the deep tree can already exhaust the same memory directly, in the builder's own cgroup.
Accepted decision: the option of always enforcing cgroup limits was rejected; RUN gets roughly docker build isolation, which sets no memory limit.
T15 (deep trees, A7): exhaustion driven by RUN is bounded only by the outer cgroup; 'fail cleanly' concerns untrusted input, and here the input's author already holds unbounded memory.
Every kaniko-mode layer (per-stage bases via extract_blob at stages.rs:424, and COPY --from image views on / via Spooled::extract at root.rs:1100-1102) is unpacked with extract_live.

extract_live resolves each lexical parent from the root by its full path (ENAMETOOLONG past PATH_MAX). It takes the physical path from /proc/self/fd (Live::physical, extract.rs:1176), which the kernel refuses past one page. So a layer publisher cannot plant an entry much deeper than PATH_MAX, and the walk's cost per entry stays linear.
The context walk opens each directory by its full path through RootPath::open_at, so a context deeper than PATH_MAX fails there and cannot reach the stage root through COPY.

reason: Source refutes a security impact, not the trace. The quadratic retention is real. But the only lower-trust input that reaches it, a tree deeper than about PATH_MAX in a kaniko-mode stage root, can come only from a RUN process (directly, or through FROM/COPY --from of a RUN-made stage). Layer extraction (extract_live) and the context walk refuse paths past PATH_MAX. That same RUN process already has unbounded memory in the same cgroup as the builder: there is no memory limit (spec.rs:44, child.rs:572,579), and by accepted design (ADR-0003, threat-model T15) RUN exhaustion is bounded only by the outer cgroup. The walk therefore adds no capability and crosses no boundary. Its only distinct effect is that the attacker's own build, already doomed to fail with ENAMETOOLONG at kaniko/export.rs:280, aborts or is OOM-killed instead. Recovery after a crash is the designed next-start cleanup, a separate deletion path. The runtime blockers (peak RSS, OOM vs error) are therefore not decisive. Per the resource-exhaustion rule, a missing limit without concrete shared impact is hardening: bound child_path at PATH_MAX in Ctx::dir_entries, as export.rs:child does.

title: Kaniko mode on /: the anonymous store's named fallback assumes unlinkat removes the name, but on an NFS or FUSE state directory the open file stays named (.nfs*/.fuse_hidden*) while later RUNs run
description: In kaniko mode on a container's / (Isolation::Direct), ranikust keeps encoded layers, kept-stage tars and, when an output file needs base-layer bytes (keep_blobs, for example --tar-path or --oci-layout-path), pulled blobs as anonymous files in the state directory (ADR-0051, ADR-0056). Where openat(O_TMPFILE) fails with EOPNOTSUPP, AnonFiles::create switches to the named way for the rest of the build (anon.rs:115). The Linux NFS client has no ->tmpfile, and a FUSE server without FUSE_TMPFILE (protocol 7.37) gets the same error [kernel facts, not verified here]. create_named then runs openat(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW) on a random .ranikust-anon- name (anon.rs:183) and unlinkat (anon.rs:195), and drops the fence window as soon as unlinkat returns 0 (anon.rs:202). On an NFS client, unlinking a file that is still open is a 'silly rename' to .nfsXXXX in the same directory, kept until the last close; libfuse high-level filesystems without hard_remove do the same with .fuse_hiddenXXXX. The store keeps every filled blob open for its whole life (store.rs:733), an encoded layer stays open until the outputs are written, and a kept stage's tar stays open in Kept::Tar until its reader is done (root.rs:1221, root.rs:789). So these names stay in the state directory during later RUNs. Fence::enter_run admits each RUN because it counts window guards, not names (fence.rs:79). A Direct RUN runs as root on the same /, and the state directory (root-owned 0700) and its files (root-owned 0600) are open to it. It can therefore read every kept-stage tar (the whole tree for FROM <stage>, RUN --mount from= or a COPY --from source not resolvable before the build, Keep::All; for a static COPY --from only the entries it names, Keep::Paths, rnk-builder stage.rs:119-150) and any kept base-image blobs. It can also rewrite a kept-stage tar in place, and a later COPY --from or FROM <stage> extracts that tar with no digest (root.rs:1096, root.rs:547): content the Dockerfile did not ask for reaches the output image (A6). Example: a binary from a side stage's base image changes a builder stage's output. A rewritten blob or encoded layer fails the build when it is pushed (the registry's digest) or extracted again (extract_checked checks the diff ID after extracting, root.rs:1005-1021); but --tar-path and --oci-layout-path copy anonymous layer bytes with no new hash (output.rs:395-404, layer.rs:514-518), so a same-size rewrite lands in the output file under a stale digest, rejected only by a consumer that checks digests. This breaks T21's stated mitigation, 'the state directory holding no name while a RUN runs' (threat-model.md:98, design/kaniko-mode.md:60), and ADR-0051's goal that a RUN reads no state by any route. Threat-model section 6 does not accept it: its 'files mounted into the container' covers operator-supplied files, not ranikust's own state.
