Conditions: the operator's --state-dir is on such a volume, with root not squashed (statedir.rs:324-350 requires owner uid 0, and make_private, statedir.rs:215-238, a working chmod 0700, so root_squash ends in a refusal or memfd); the RUN runs as root (the default); and the store is not tainted or poisoned (those use memfd). The store expects state directories on NFS, CIFS and FUSE (lock.rs:69, store.rs:137) and on volumes shared between containers (ADR-0056:79-83). ADR-0056 measured 'after the unlink, no name' only on the overlay root and on tmpfs and ext4 volumes (ADR-0056:142-149). Correction to the hunter: after a crash, leftover .nfs* names are not used silently. statedir::check_contents accepts only the marker and .ranikust-anon- names unless a .ranikust-state marker is present (statedir.rs:184-209), so the next build refuses an anonymous store's directory: an availability issue only. On a normal exit the NFS client removes the renamed files at the last close.
claimed_root_cause: AnonFiles::create_named (crates/rnk-store/src/anon.rs:180-204) treats a zero return from unlinkat as proof that the open file no longer has a name, and drops the fence window at once. It does not check fstat(fd).st_nlink == 0, and it does not re-list the directory. Nothing limits the named way to filesystems where an unlinked open file loses its name: Store::open_anonymous (store.rs:346-438) and statedir::prepare (statedir.rs:53-97) check the state directory's identity, owner, mode and contents, never its filesystem type (only /proc/self/fd is checked, store.rs:1207-1219). Fence::enter_run (fence.rs:73-94) counts window guards, not names on disk.

trace.scope: KanikoRoot::keep (StageRootfs for KanikoRoot), kaniko mode on / (tar_store present)
trace.description: The lower-trust Dockerfile names a stage that a later COPY --from or FROM <stage> reads. Before the shared root is reused, ranikust keeps that stage as a plain tar through tar_out, which writes into store.scratch_file() (root.rs:789): the whole tree (Keep::All) for FROM <stage>, RUN --mount from= or an unresolvable source, else the entries the COPY --from sources name (Keep::Paths). When an output file needs base-layer bytes (keep_blobs), FROM also fills its blobs through Store::fill_anonymous, which calls AnonFiles::create (store.rs:720); otherwise layers are streamed and spooled in a short-lived scratch file (root.rs:922).

On a state directory that the operator placed on NFS (no ->tmpfile in the client) or on a FUSE server without FUSE_TMPFILE, openat(O_TMPFILE) returns EOPNOTSUPP, and the store switches to the named way for the build. The filesystem type is never checked.
Inside a Fence::named window (anon.rs:182), openat on the state directory creates .ranikust-anon-<128 random bits> with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW|O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC, mode 0600, root-owned.

unlinkat returns 0. On an NFS client, an open file is silly-renamed to .nfsXXXX in the same directory and keeps its link; a libfuse high-level server without hard_remove renames it to .fuse_hiddenXXXX. Only the return value is checked, not st_nlink.
The window is dropped and the file returned, so the fence now counts no name, although one is on disk.

Filled blobs are kept open for the life of the store; encoded layers stay open until the outputs are written; kept-stage tars (Kept::Tar, root.rs:1220-1222) stay open until their reader is done. So the renamed names last through later stages' RUNs.
store.enter_run() admits the RUN: Fence::enter_run waits only while state.names > 0 (fence.rs:79), and no guard is held.

sandbox.run(spec): the lower-trust RUN (the Dockerfile's command, or a base-image binary it calls) runs as root on ranikust's own /. It can list <state-dir>/.nfsXXXX or .fuse_hiddenXXXX and open them read-write: it can read kept stages and kept blobs, and rewrite a kept tar that root.rs:1096 or root.rs:547 later extracts with no digest.

evidence.description: Module contract for the named way: the file is unlinked at once inside a Fence::named window, 'so the name never exists while a RUN process does'. The only filesystem named is the overlayfs root of a Docker container.
Only unlinkat's return value is checked. No fstat(fd).st_nlink == 0 check and no re-listing follow before drop(window) at anon.rs:202.
enter_run waits only on the in-memory count of window guards (state.names); it never looks at the state directory.
T21 (A3, A5, A6) lists as a mitigation 'the state directory holding no name while a RUN runs' for kaniko mode on /.
Design invariant: 'The state directory holds no name while a RUN runs'.
Maintainer's goal: a RUN cannot read ranikust's state or credentials by any route. Line 38 originally ruled out a named file unlinked later.
'after the unlink, no name' was measured on the container's overlay root only; tmpfs and ext4 volumes took O_TMPFILE. Line 149 lists what was not measured, and it names no network or FUSE filesystem.
The design expects a state directory on a volume that outlives its container, and another container on the same volume.
The store explicitly supports state directories on NFS, CIFS and FUSE filesystems (flock emulation), so such volumes are an expected deployment.

check_chain accepts the state directory by owner (euid 0) and mode only, and no code path checks its filesystem type for kaniko mode on / (set_up_kaniko calls prepare and Store::open_anonymous only, setup.rs:318-323). With root_squash the owner, list or chmod check fails, so the claim needs a no_root_squash NFS or root-accessible FUSE volume.

A kept tar is extracted for COPY --from straight from its descriptor (reopen via /proc/self/fd), with Whiteouts::Literal and no digest. For FROM <stage>, root.rs:547 extracts it into the root with extract_live_literal. Its integrity rests on its being unreachable.

SourceRoot::keep keeps only the entries static COPY --from sources name (Keep::Paths) and the whole stage (Keep::All) for FROM <stage>, RUN --mount from=, a source not resolvable before the build, or a fallback; this bounds what a RUN can read from a kept tar.

The OCI layout writer copies each layer's bytes from its (anonymous) file with no new hash; write_docker_tar reads Content::Anon the same way (layer.rs:514-518). A same-size rewrite of an encoded layer or kept blob reaches --tar-path or --oci-layout-path under its stale digest; only a push is checked by the registry.

Only the marker and .ranikust-anon- names count as the store's own. A crash that leaves .nfs* names makes the next prepare refuse an anonymous store's directory (statedir.rs:188-209): fail-closed, availability only.

blockers: No target-controlled execution and no NFS or FUSE fixture in this run. Two Linux behaviours decide whether the trace is reached, and they are not visible in the repository: O_TMPFILE fails with EOPNOTSUPP on an NFS client and on a FUSE server without FUSE_TMPFILE; and an NFS client silly-renames an open file on a successful unlinkat. On NFSv4.1+ servers that return OPEN4_RESULT_PRESERVE_UNLINKED, newer Linux clients skip the silly rename [inferred], so the NFS version and server decide the outcome.
Whether a given FUSE filesystem implements FUSE_TMPFILE, and whether it hides open unlinked files (libfuse high-level API without hard_remove), depends on that filesystem and how it is mounted.

It is a deployment fact whether operators run kaniko mode on / with --state-dir on a network or FUSE volume (for example an NFS, EFS, Filestore or Azure Files ReadWriteMany PVC) with root not squashed. Under root_squash, statedir.rs refuses the directory or the store falls back to memfd.
The disposable VM (T2) and T2c lanes have no NFS server or FUSE filesystem set up today, and their external network rules them out as the sandbox for this run.

validation_plan.local: Run later in the disposable VM (T2, just test-vm guest), with dummy data only, then discard the VM. (1) As root in the guest: install nfs-kernel-server; mkdir -p /srv/nfs/state && chmod 700 /srv/nfs/state; add '/srv/nfs 127.0.0.1(rw,sync,no_root_squash,no_subtree_check)' to /etc/exports and run exportfs -ra; mount -t nfs -o vers=3 127.0.0.1:/srv/nfs /mnt/nfs3, and separately -o vers=4.2 at /mnt/nfs42. (2) Dummy context ctx/Dockerfile: 'FROM busybox AS a' / 'RUN echo dummy-a > /a.txt' / 'FROM debian:bookworm-slim' / 'RUN ls -la /var/lib/ranikust; for f in /var/lib/ranikust/.nfs* /var/lib/ranikust/.fuse_hidden*; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; od -An -c -j257 -N5 "$f"; off=$(grep -abo dummy-a "$f" | head -n1 | cut -d: -f1); [ -n "$off" ] && printf tamper! | dd of="$f" bs=1 seek="$off" conv=notrunc; done; true' / 'COPY --from=a /a.txt /a.txt'. (3) Start ranikust as tests/smoke/run-cases.sh does with RANIKUST_CASE_MODE=kaniko, but in a rootful container started as root in the guest (run-cases.sh uses rootless podman, which maps the root-owned 0700 NFS directory to nobody, so statedir::prepare refuses it): a default podman or Docker container (no --privileged, no extra capabilities, ranikust as PID 1) with -v $RNK:/ranikust/bin/ranikust:ro -v $PWD/ctx:/ranikust/ctx:ro -v /mnt/nfs3/state:/var/lib/ranikust -v $PWD/out:/ranikust/out, running /ranikust/bin/ranikust --context /ranikust/ctx --mode=kaniko --no-push --tar-path /ranikust/out/image.tar. (4) The claim holds if the log shows 'no O_TMPFILE on this filesystem' (anon.rs:122-127), the second stage's RUN lists .nfs* entries and od prints 'u s t a r' for one of them, and /a.txt in the last layer of out/image.tar reads 'tamper!'. It is refuted for that setup if no .nfs* name is listed, or if O_TMPFILE was accepted. A refusal of the state directory or the warning 'keeping state in memory (memfd)' (anon.rs:170-175) means the set-up is wrong (root squashed, or the directory not owned by root), not a result. (5) Repeat on /mnt/nfs42, and on a libfuse high-level passthrough (libfuse3 example 'passthrough', or bindfs) mounted with -o allow_other and without hard_remove over a root-owned 0700 directory (expect .fuse_hidden*). (6) Fix check: after unlinkat in create_named, require fstat(fd).st_nlink == 0 and no new entry in the state directory; otherwise close the file and switch to memfd, or refuse the state directory. Better still, run that probe once in Store::open_anonymous, and reject the named way when statfs reports NFS (0x6969), FUSE (0x65735546) or SMB/CIFS. With the fix, the same e2e lists no names and /a.txt reads 'dummy-a'. Clean up with umount, exportfs -ua, and discarding the VM.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed, read-only. In each pipeline that runs ranikust in kaniko mode on / (a default Docker container or an ordinary Kubernetes pod): (1) search existing build logs (default --verbosity info) for '<state-dir>: no O_TMPFILE on this filesystem; state files are made by a name unlinked at once, while no RUN runs' (anon.rs:122-127), which says the named way was used; the container's overlay root logs it too and is outside this candidate (measured in ADR-0056). (2) Inside the build container run stat -f -c %T /var/lib/ranikust (or the --state-dir): GNU stat prints nfs for NFSv3 and NFSv4, fuseblk for any FUSE filesystem, and smb2 or cifs for SMB; grep the mount in /proc/self/mountinfo (or findmnt -T <dir> -o FSTYPE,OPTIONS) for the fuse.<name> type and, for NFS, the vers= option. (3) If it is NFS, ask the storage owner whether the export squashes root: the candidate needs no_root_squash; with root_squash ranikust refuses the directory or warns 'keeping state in memory (memfd)'.

title: Published store layers and blobs are reused without re-verification, so a kaniko-mode-on-/ RUN that can write a shared state volume poisons later persistent-store builds
description: The persistent store trusts a published entry on reuse. Store::get and the reuse path of Store::fill check only that blobs/<alg>/<hex> is a regular file and layers/v2/<alg>/<chain> is a directory on the state directory's mount, then return it without hashing it again (store.rs:1040-1059, 626-631, 665-670). This is safe only while no lower-trust principal can write the state directory. Full-sandbox RUNs (overlay mode, kaniko mode off /) cannot. A Direct RUN in kaniko mode on / can: it runs as uid 0 on the container's / with no namespace (rnk-sandbox/src/direct.rs:1-15,35). The state directory (default /var/lib/ranikust) is a plain writable path there, and the ignore list only keeps it out of the walk and the emptying of the root (kaniko/ignore.rs:215-217), so what a RUN writes there stays in the volume. statedir::check_contents accepts a directory holding a regular .ranikust-state marker for every mode (statedir.rs:192-197), with no on-/ distinction (setup.rs:503-509). open_anonymous then uses a non-empty directory as is, with a warning that names only reads (store.rs:403-410). This contradicts ADR-0051 (the directory stays empty), T21's 'the state directory holding no name while a RUN runs', and threat-model section 6 ('Nothing of ranikust's state outlives a kaniko-mode build on /'). Even an empty volume is enough: the RUN can create the marker and a layers/v2/sha256/<chain>/ tree itself, and a later persistent Store::open accepts it on the regular marker alone (store.rs:1253-1265). The precondition is that the same volume is later used as the state directory of an overlay-mode build (a privileged container, or the host). That build then hits the planted chain-ID directory under the per-digest lock, skips extract_layer's diff_id check (rnk-snapshot/src/layer.rs:116-135), and mounts the planted directory as an overlay lowerdir of its stage root (rnk-snapshot/src/stage.rs:303-307). Its RUNs execute the planted files with that build's --secret mounts and network, and its pushed RUN layers carry the effect. This crosses a boundary: the Dockerfile author of build A controls build B's image (A6) and reaches B's secrets (A4). B's RUN stays inside the full sandbox, so there is no host escape. A planted blob alone is weaker. A not-yet-extracted layer still fails the diff_id check (a build failure). tar and OCI-layout outputs copy the store file without hashing it (rnk-builder/src/output.rs:155 and 220; put_blob at output.rs:387-404, whose holds() at output.rs:410-427 hashes only the destination), and a registry push sends it by path (output.rs:319). A registry push of a mismatched blob is probably rejected by the registry's own digest check (not verified). Possible fixes: verify blobs by digest on reuse, and keep a digest of each extracted layer's content that is checked before it is used as a lower. Refusing a marked store in kaniko mode on / would not be enough on its own, because a RUN can forge the marker. The docs should also say that a state volume used by kaniko mode on / must never serve persistent-store builds.
claimed_root_cause: Store::published (crates/rnk-store/src/store.rs:1040-1059) treats any regular file (blob) or directory (layer) under a digest name on the state mount as the verified entry, and Store::get (store.rs:626-631) and Store::fill's reuse path (store.rs:665-670) return it without re-verification, as the crate card states (docs/agents/crates/rnk-store.md:77). Integrity then rests entirely on no lower-trust principal ever writing the state directory. That does not hold when one state directory serves both kaniko mode on / and a persistent store: statedir.rs:192-197 and setup.rs:318-323 accept the directory for kaniko mode on /, where a Direct RUN writes it as uid 0, and check_marker (store.rs:1253-1265) gives no integrity. T13 promises 'verify digests when writing and reading', and threat-model section 3 calls cross-trust-domain sharing safe because only content-addressed data is shared.

trace.description: In kaniko mode on /, the Dockerfile author's RUN is exec'd as uid 0 on the container's / with no namespace or mount, so it can write any path in the container, including the mounted state-directory volume (default /var/lib/ranikust).
A state directory holding a regular .ranikust-state marker is accepted (Ok(true)) for every mode. prepare_state_dir (setup.rs:503) passes no mode, so kaniko mode on / is included.
On / the same directory is opened with Store::open_anonymous, and RUN runs Direct.

A non-empty state directory (an existing persistent store's blobs/, layers/, marker) is used as is. The warning names only that a RUN can read it, not that it can write it, and nothing checks the store's contents afterwards.

trace.scope: ignore list (state directory inside the root)
trace.description: The state directory is kept out of the walk and out of the emptying of /, so whatever the RUN wrote under it stays in the volume after the build.
A later persistent Store::open (overlay mode, or kaniko mode off /) accepts the directory on the regular marker file alone. The RUN may have created that file itself.
Only the entry's type (a directory for a layer, a regular file for a blob) and its mount are checked; its content is not.
Under the per-digest lock, a published entry is returned as reused and the verifying filler never runs.
The chain-ID key finds the planted directory, so the diff_id check of the layer tar (layer.rs:130-135) never runs.

The planted layer directory becomes an overlay lowerdir of the victim build's stage root. Its RUNs (still in the full sandbox) execute the planted files with that build's --secret mounts and network, and its pushed RUN layers carry the result.

evidence.description: T13 (shared-store poisoning, assets A5 and A6, all modes) requires 'Verify digests when writing and reading'.
Other builds sharing the store 'may belong to another trust domain; only content-addressed data is shared'.
T21 names a kaniko-on-/ RUN that tampers with ranikust's state (A5) as a threat, with the mitigation that the state directory holds no name while a RUN runs.
ADR-0051 says the state directory stays empty in kaniko mode on /, yet a marked persistent store is accepted there.
Crate card: the filler must return Ok only for a verified entry; the store does not hash a blob again.
published(): a regular file for a blob, a directory for a layer, on the same mount; nothing else is checked.
In kaniko mode on /, the warning for a non-empty state directory names only that a RUN can read it.

pull_blob returns store.get's path without verification. The path becomes LayerBytes::File (rnk-builder/src/layer.rs:170), which a registry push sends by path (output.rs:319) and the tar and OCI-layout writers copy without hashing it (output.rs:155, 220, 387-404).
The documented volume for overlay mode in a container, -v ranikust-state:/var/lib/ranikust, is the same path kaniko mode on / uses as its default state directory. No document forbids sharing it.

blockers: No target-controlled execution is allowed in this run: no OS-enforced sandbox exists on this host, and the VM and T2c lanes have external network. The plant-then-reuse sequence is therefore unobserved.

It depends on the deployment whether one state-directory volume is mounted both into a default (unprivileged) container that runs kaniko mode on / and, later, into a privileged container or host that runs overlay mode or kaniko mode off /, or is shared across trust domains. Source cannot show this. The docs neither support nor forbid it: the book documents a volume at /var/lib/ranikust both for overlay mode in a container and for kaniko mode on / ('one per container: a second build on a state directory in use is refused', docs/book/src/how-it-builds.md:141-142, which speaks to concurrent use), but not whether one volume may serve both modes in turn.

The owner must decide the scope. T13, threat-model section 3 and T21 promise read-side verification, safe cross-domain sharing and an empty state directory in kaniko mode on /. The crate card says the store does not hash again, and nothing records whether a raw writer reached through a kaniko-on-/ RUN is in scope. T14 (threat-model.md:91) already tells operators to give each trust domain its own store, which bears on the cross-trust-domain part of the impact.

validation_plan.local: Run in the disposable VM (T2) or the T2c rootful-Docker lane with the ADR-0063 marker, using only dummy data and a loopback registry that holds a one-layer base image h11-base built from busybox. For a one-layer base, the chain ID equals the layer's diff_id. (1) docker volume create rnk-h11. (2) In a --privileged container with -v rnk-h11:/var/lib/ranikust, build 'FROM <loopback>/h11-base' + 'RUN true' in overlay mode with --state-dir /var/lib/ranikust. Confirm that layers/v2/sha256/<diff_id>/ now exists. (3) In a default-profile container (no --privileged, no extra capabilities) with the same volume, run kaniko mode on / with 'FROM <loopback>/h11-base' + 'RUN for d in /var/lib/ranikust/layers/v2/sha256/*/; do echo H11-POISON > "$d/h11-marker"; done'. Record whether the start is refused (the source predicts acceptance with only the 'state directory ... is not empty: a RUN can read' warning). (3b) Variant on a fresh empty volume: the kaniko-on-/ RUN creates /var/lib/ranikust/.ranikust-state (regular file) and layers/v2/sha256/<diff_id>/ holding a busybox tree copy plus h11-marker, with modes 0700 and owner root, then step 4 runs on that volume. (4) In the privileged container again, build 'FROM <loopback>/h11-base' + 'RUN cat /h11-marker' with --verbosity=debug. The candidate is confirmed if the RUN prints H11-POISON (the base image has no such file) and the rnk_store.fill span for the layer key shows reused=true. It is disproved if the store is refused, the layer is extracted again, or the diff_id check fails. (5) A T0 regression to add: open a Store in a tempdir, fill an EntryKey::Layer, write a file under the returned path, then call fill again with a filler that panics if invoked. Today it returns the path without calling the filler. Do the same with an EntryKey::Blob whose bytes were overwritten, through Store::get. Then remove the containers and the volume.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed check: in the CI templates, Helm values, GitLab or GitHub runner configurations and docs examples that run ranikust, list each state-directory volume (named volume, hostPath or PVC at /var/lib/ranikust or --state-dir). Record whether any one volume is mounted both by unprivileged jobs (kaniko mode on /) and by privileged or host jobs (overlay mode or kaniko off /), or by jobs of different projects or trust levels. Also decide whether such sharing is supported: if it is not, document it; if it is, require verification on reuse.

title: State-dir set-up creates missing parents by path after the descriptor check, so another local user's symlink planted in /tmp makes root create directories elsewhere
description: statedir::prepare (crates/ranikust/src/statedir.rs:53-97) finds the nearest existing ancestor of --state-dir with lstat by path (lines 55-58), checks only that ancestor's chain by descriptor (lines 60-64), and then creates every missing component by path with std::fs::DirBuilder recursive (lines 68-71). ADR-0050 (line 70) and check_chain (statedir.rs:345) accept root's sticky world-writable directory (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm) as a parent. When the operator's --state-dir has two or more missing components below such a directory (for example /tmp/rnk/state with /tmp/rnk absent), another local user who can write /tmp can create /tmp/rnk as a symlink to any existing directory after the lstat of /tmp/rnk and before std's mkdir calls. In the pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml:4, 1.99.1) DirBuilder::create_dir_all (library/std/src/fs.rs:3566-3609) first calls mkdir on the full path, then on each ancestor until one succeeds or fails with EEXIST while is_dir() (a symlink-following stat) holds, then calls mkdir on each uncreated path from the top. mkdir(2) resolves /tmp/rnk as an intermediate component and follows the symlink, so a symlink present at the first mkdir("/tmp/rnk/state") makes root (ranikust's euid; a non-root run is refused before set-up) create <target>/state (mode 0700 minus umask, root-owned) and return success. A symlink planted only after that first mkdir failed with ENOENT reaches the same result through the EEXIST-and-is_dir() branch only when fs.protected_symlinks is 0 or the sticky parent is not world-writable: is_dir() follows /tmp/rnk as a trailing component, which protected_symlinks=1 refuses (EACCES) for another user's link in a world-writable sticky directory, so std returns EEXIST and nothing is created. Only afterwards does open_dir with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS (statedir.rs:79) refuse the build, leaving the directory behind. This breaks the documented contract that nothing is created for a refused state directory (statedir.rs:30-36, ADR-0050 line 72), and an unprivileged local user gets root to create empty directories in places it cannot write. The overlay-mode set-up has only unshared the mount namespace (crates/rnk-sandbox/src/setup.rs:35), which does not isolate filesystem contents, so the directory lands on the host filesystem. Correction to the hunter's limits: fs.protected_symlinks=1 narrows the window to the interval between the lstat scan and the first mkdir but likely does not close it, because mainline fs/namei.c applies may_follow_link only to a trailing symlink (pick_link with WALK_TRAILING), while /tmp/rnk is an intermediate component of mkdir's parent lookup; this kernel fact is unverified in this run and must be observed. Remaining limits: the window spans about ten syscalls (lstat of /tmp, openat2, the descriptor walk to /, then the first mkdir; with protected_symlinks=0 also the ancestor mkdir calls); a run in which ranikust itself creates /tmp/rnk locks the attacker out of that path until it is removed, while a run in which the symlink is present at the lstat scan is refused cleanly (ELOOP at statedir.rs:60) and can be retried; the created names come from the operator; the directories are empty and root-owned; with a single missing component there is no side effect (mkdir does not follow a trailing symlink and the later checks refuse); the default /var/lib/ranikust and the repository's lanes (--state-dir /tmp/w, one component) are not affected; inside a container no other local user normally exists. No accepted risk in threat-model section 6 or an ADR covers this. Suggested fix: after checking the nearest existing ancestor by descriptor, create each missing component with mkdirat relative to the held descriptor and open it with openat O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY (or openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|RESOLVE_BENEATH) before creating the next, so no path is re-resolved; or refuse to create more than the last component below a directory other users may write.
claimed_root_cause: crates/ranikust/src/statedir.rs:68-71 creates the missing components by path with std::fs::DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700).create(state_dir), whose mkdir(2) calls follow symlinks in intermediate components, after the scan (statedir.rs:55-58) and the descriptor check (statedir.rs:60-64) covered only the nearest existing ancestor. The sticky-directory exception (statedir.rs:345) lets that ancestor be writable by other users, who can create the first missing name as a symlink inside the window.

trace.description: The operator's --state-dir is made absolute with std::path::absolute without touching the filesystem (lines 435-438), for example /tmp/rnk/state with /tmp/rnk absent; the attacker is another local user who can write the sticky /tmp, not the operator.

Overlay-mode set-up calls statedir::prepare through prepare_state_dir (setup.rs:503-509) before the store opens; kaniko-mode set-up does the same at setup.rs:318. Only the mount namespace was unshared before (rnk-sandbox setup.rs:35), so file creation reaches the host filesystem.
The nearest existing ancestor is found with symlink_metadata (lstat) by path over /tmp/rnk/state, /tmp/rnk, /tmp. With /tmp/rnk absent at that moment, existing=/tmp and is_state=false.
Only /tmp and / are checked by descriptor. /tmp passes as a root-owned sticky directory (statedir.rs:345) although other users may create entries in it.

Recursive by-path mkdir as root. If another user created /tmp/rnk as a symlink to a directory of their choice after the lstat scan, mkdir("/tmp/rnk/state") follows the intermediate symlink and creates <target>/state, root-owned, mode 0700 (minus umask). The refusal comes only afterwards (open_dir with RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS at statedir.rs:79) and does not remove it.

evidence.description: The documented contract: 'changing nothing in a directory that fails'; step 2 (lines 34-36) says the nearest existing directory's chain is checked 'before anything is created'.
std::fs::DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700).create(state_dir) creates the missing components by path after a check that covered only the nearest existing ancestor.

Pins Rust 1.99.1, whose library/std/src/fs.rs:3566-3609 (DirBuilder::create_dir_all) calls mkdir on the full path first, accepts an existing ancestor when is_dir() (a trailing, symlink-following stat that fs.protected_symlinks=1 refuses for another user's link in a world-writable sticky directory) holds, and calls mkdir again on each uncreated path; every mkdir resolves intermediate components through symlinks.
Symlinks on the path are refused (open_dir: openat2 RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS|NO_MAGICLINKS, lines 247-261) only after creation, so the refusal leaves what was created through the symlink.
check_chain accepts a root-owned sticky directory as a parent even though group and others may write it, so other local users can create the first missing name during the window.

The ADR states the chain is 'Checked before anything is created, walking the real parents by descriptor', and line 70 allows root's sticky directory (/tmp) above the state directory; nothing in the ADR or threat-model section 6 accepts creation through a planted symlink.
enter_build_namespace unshares only CLONE_NEWNS before overlay-mode set-up; a mount namespace does not isolate directory creation on the host filesystem.
prepare_refuses_without_creating_anything covers only a symlink that exists before prepare runs (lines 122-129), not one planted between the scan and the create; no test injects the race.

blockers: No target-controlled execution and no OS-enforced sandbox are available in this run, so neither the race outcome (root's mkdir following a symlink another user planted after the lstat scan) nor the left-behind directory was observed.

Whether fs.protected_symlinks=1 stops root from following another user's symlink in /tmp when it is an intermediate component of mkdir's parent lookup is a kernel fact not visible in the repository; no kernel source is available locally; the reading of mainline fs/namei.c (may_follow_link only for WALK_TRAILING) says it does not, which leaves the scan-to-first-mkdir window reachable on default distribution settings (protected_symlinks=1 does close the later EEXIST-and-is_dir() branch, a trailing follow), but this was not observed.

Reachability needs a deployment where another local user can write the sticky directory above an operator-chosen --state-dir with two or more missing components (shared CI hosts or runners); the default /var/lib/ranikust and the repository lanes (tests/vm/guest/smoke.sh:134, --state-dir /tmp/w) use paths with no race, and whether such deployments exist is an owner fact.

validation_plan.deployment: The owner checks whether any pipeline or host runs ranikust with a --state-dir that has more than one missing component below /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm on a machine where other local users or untrusted jobs can write that directory (shared CI runners, multi-user build hosts), and whether systemd PrivateTmp or a per-job /tmp isolates it.

title: The T2 VM's QEMU user-mode network lets guest code from mutable-tag base images and RUN steps reach the developer host's loopback-only services at 10.0.2.2
description: tests/vm/vm.sh boots the disposable T2 VM with QEMU user-mode networking (`-netdev user`). The run boot (vm.sh:583) has only an SSH hostfwd and no `restrict=on` or other scoping. In this mode the guest's host alias 10.0.2.2 is translated to the host's 127.0.0.1, and the connection comes from the QEMU process of the invoking user. The harness relies on this to reach the host's test registries (vm.sh:230-232, docs/testing.md:214-215, tests/registry/compose.yaml:8-9). Neither the guest seed (cloud-init/user-data:21-30) nor the provisioning seed adds an egress filter; tests/vm contains no iptables, nftables or ufw rule. The default suites (`unit smoke`, vm.sh:91) run code from mutable Docker Hub tags, pulled through mirror.gcr.io, as root in the guest. smoke.sh:299 runs python:3.13-alpine's own `sh` with `--privileged` on Docker's default bridge. smoke.sh:110 runs the mounted /ranikust in that image, and the RUN steps of tests/smoke/e2e execute alpine:3.20's binaries (smoke.sh:20). smoke.sh:170 runs RUN steps in the python image as real root on the VM's own network. In e2e and ultra, ranikust on the VM itself shares the VM's network (e2e.sh:210), so the W1-W3 pnpm installs share it too. Peer control: the containerized kaniko, BuildKit and rk-kaniko builds use a Docker `--internal` network (e2e.sh:198, 376), so they cannot reach 10.0.2.2. The provisioning boot (vm.sh:519) runs only cloud-init package installs from the Ubuntu archive, so it is not on this path. No project document makes the VM a network-containment boundary: rules.md:17 confines privileged tests to it for host safety. Threat-model section 6 (threat-model.md:140-146) accepts that RUN reaches the services of the machine ranikust runs on and says to mitigate outside ranikust. The harness is that outside, does not mitigate, and widens the reach to the workstation's loopback; the T2c lane, by contrast, runs with `--network none` (lane.sh:138). The only source-visible host service is the dummy test registries (anonymous HTTP with delete enabled on 127.0.0.1:5000, and basic-auth HTTPS on 5443). These run only after `just registry-up`, and no host-side code runs images from them. Any impact beyond tampering with dummy test data depends on which loopback-only services the workstation runs. Likelihood is low: it needs hostile content behind a mutable tag at mirror.gcr.io, or a hostile seeded npm package with lifecycle scripts.
claimed_root_cause: The VM harness uses the QEMU VM as the containment for privileged tests that run third-party image code as root. Yet it configures the guest network as `-netdev user` with no `restrict=on`, no guestfwd allowlist and no guest-side egress filter (vm.sh:583; cloud-init/user-data:21-30). libslirp therefore turns every guest connection to 10.0.2.2:<port> into a connection from the user's QEMU process to the host's 127.0.0.1:<port>. Nothing scopes that path to the test-registry ports it was relied on for.

trace.scope: smoke suite, part of the default `just test-vm` (vm.sh:91)
trace.description: IMAGE is `$REG/library/python:3.13-alpine`, where REG defaults to mirror.gcr.io (line 18). It is a mutable Docker Hub tag whose content the base-image publisher and the mirror control; both are lower-trust per the threat model. E2E_BASE (line 20) is the mutable alpine:3.20 tag.

trace.scope: smoke suite, chroot-refusal checks for the privileged and sysadmin variants
trace.description: `sudo docker run --rm $(docker_args "$name") ... "$IMAGE" sh -c '...'` runs the image's own /bin/sh as root, with `--privileged` for the privileged variant (docker_args, line 60). It runs on Docker's default bridge, which the guest NATs out through its default route to the slirp gateway 10.0.2.2.

trace.scope: guest seed of every T2 run
trace.description: The seed writes only Docker's registry-mirrors file (lines 21-24) and runcmd only enables Docker and the user (lines 26-30). No firewall rule is added, and tests/vm contains no iptables, nftables or ufw configuration, so nothing in the guest restricts egress to 10.0.2.2.

`-netdev user,id=n0,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:$PORT-:22` has no `restrict=on` and no guestfwd scoping. QEMU user networking forwards guest TCP to 10.0.2.2:<port> as a connection from the invoking user's QEMU process to the host's 127.0.0.1:<port>, which reaches any loopback-only service on the developer workstation.

evidence.description: The harness comment (lines 230-232) says the guest reaches the host's test registries as 10.0.2.2 because QEMU's user network maps it to the host's loopback. The mapping is relied on by design.
The documentation (lines 214-215) says the T2 VM reaches the test registries as 10.0.2.2, so they need no wider binding. It sets no limit on what else on the host loopback the guest can reach.

The only source-visible host loopback service: an anonymous plain-HTTP registry:2 on 127.0.0.1:5000 with REGISTRY_STORAGE_DELETE_ENABLED (line 19) and `restart: unless-stopped` (line 16). It holds dummy test images, and no host-side script runs images from it; vm.sh:234 only health-checks it.
The default suites are `unit smoke`, so the smoke suite runs the mutable-tag python:3.13-alpine and alpine:3.20 images on every plain `just test-vm`.
The host variant runs smoke-build on the VM itself as real root. Its RUN steps (for example `python3 -c ...` from line 75) execute in the python:3.13-alpine root and share the VM's network.

Correction to the candidate: here the container's command is the mounted /ranikust, not the python image's binaries. The RUN steps of tests/smoke/e2e run alpine:3.20's binaries (BASE=E2E_BASE, line 104) on the container's bridge network.
In e2e and ultra, ranikust runs on the VM itself, and its RUN shares the VM's network (ADR-0010). The W1-W3 pnpm installs from the seeded verdaccio storage therefore have the same reach.

Peer control that narrows the claim: the containerized builders (kaniko, BuildKit, rk-kaniko) run on `nk-internal`, a Docker `--internal` network (lines 376, 394, 418), so they have no route to 10.0.2.2. Only ranikust on the VM itself and the services on nk-egress have that route.

The golden-image provisioning boot also uses `-netdev user,id=n0` without restrict. It runs only cloud-init package installs from the Ubuntu archive, with no image or RUN code, so it is not on the exploited path.
The sibling privileged lane (T2c, ADR-0063) runs its containers with `--network none`. The T2 VM lane has no equivalent network restriction.

Accepted risk (lines 140-149): RUN shares the network of the machine ranikust runs on, and the threat model says to mitigate outside ranikust. In the harness, that machine is the guest, and QEMU extends its reach to the workstation's loopback. Neither this entry nor ADR-0010:36 accepts that reach, and the harness applies no mitigation.

Calibration: the rules make the VM the place for privileged tests (host safety). No project document states that the VM isolates guest network traffic from the host, so whether VM network containment is in scope is the maintainer's call.

Experiment 13 records that the VM reached host services (nextjs-kaniko's registry on port 5001 and verdaccio on 4873) at 10.0.2.2 through QEMU user networking. The mapping was observed, and the workstation has run other host services beside the test registries.

blockers: No VM boot or target-controlled execution was allowed in this run. Guest-to-10.0.2.2 reachability has not been observed from a default-bridge container or from a RUN in the guest. It is inferred from vm.sh:583, the harness's own reliance on it (vm.sh:230-232, docs/testing.md:214-215) and experiment 13's observation from the guest's root network namespace (containers there used socat forwarders).

Which loopback-only services listen on the developer workstation during `just test-vm`, and whether they are unauthenticated or hold data or credentials, is a workstation fact outside the repository. The only source-visible ones are the dummy test registries, which run only after `just registry-up`. Without a sensitive service, the effect is limited to tampering with dummy test images.

Exploitation needs hostile content behind a mutable tag served by mirror.gcr.io (python:3.13-alpine, alpine:3.20), or a seeded npm package whose lifecycle scripts run in the W1-W3 RUN steps. Neither can be observed from source. Whether the T2 VM is meant to be a network boundary is undecided in the project docs; it is a maintainer decision, which is an open question rather than a source fact.

validation_plan.local: Run only on the KVM workstation's T2 VM lane, as the invoking user with /dev/kvm access, never with sudo or as root on the host, and with dummy data. (1) In a throwaway git worktree of ed718fb, add an uncommitted quick case. tests/smoke/cases/loopback-probe/Dockerfile: `ARG BASE=docker.io/library/alpine:3.20`, `FROM ${BASE}`, `RUN (wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.0.2.2:18080/marker.txt || echo unreachable) > /probe`, `CMD cat /probe`. tests/smoke/cases/loopback-probe/case.sh: `case_run() { build img >/dev/null; echo "probe-run: $(run img)"; echo "probe-container: $($ENGINE run --rm "$BASE" sh -c 'wget -qO- -T 5 http://10.0.2.2:18080/marker.txt || echo unreachable')"; }`. vm.sh:253 copies the working tree's cases into the guest. (2) On the host, start a loopback-only dummy listener: `d=$(mktemp -d); head -c 16 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n' > "$d/marker.txt"; python3 -I -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 18080 --directory "$d"`. Run it in a second terminal, and check with `ss -ltnH 'sport = :18080'` that it listens on 127.0.0.1 only. (3) From the worktree, run `RANIKUST_QUICK_CASES=loopback-probe just test-vm quick`, then read the quick suite's log under target/vm/results/<release>/ and the http.server's request log. (4) The exposure is confirmed if `probe-run` or `probe-container` prints the dummy marker and the server logs `GET /marker.txt` from 127.0.0.1. It is refuted if both print `unreachable` and the server logs no request. (5) Stop the listener, then `rm -rf "$d"` and remove the worktree. After any fix, repeat the run. It must show `unreachable` for both probes while `just test-vm smoke` (mirror.gcr.io pulls) and `just test-vm push` (10.0.2.2:5000 and 10.0.2.2:5443) still pass.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed on every machine that runs `just test-vm` (the KVM workstation; the VPS has no KVM). While a VM run is up, list the loopback listeners with `ss -ltnpH` filtered to 127.0.0.1 and ::1, without probing any of them. Record which ones are unauthenticated or hold data or credentials: dev servers, databases, IDE or agent bridges, Docker or podman TCP APIs, and nextjs-kaniko's registry and verdaccio. Also record whether nextjs-kaniko's pnpm configuration runs dependency lifecycle scripts in the W1-W3 RUN steps. Finally, the maintainer decides whether VM network containment is in scope: a fix such as `restrict=on` with guestfwd entries for the registries and a pull proxy, or else an ADR or threat-model entry that accepts the exposure.
